# V60 Garage — Handoff Package

Generated 2026-10-24 13:13 UTC from commit `e2de8eb` (2026-10-24 ASE article: keep it to car-owner content). Version live at that commit: `2026.10.16-0127-e045733a`.

- Repo (source of truth): https://github.com/bmcdoorz94/V60-Link (branch `main`)
- Live app: https://bmcdoorz94.github.io/V60-Link/
- Files in section 4: 82 text files and 6 binary files, 2,127,673 bytes of text. Each file has a SHA-256 prefix in the manifest so the receiver can confirm it is complete.

## 0. Rules for the receiving AI
1. Read `CLAUDE.md` in section 4 first. It holds the project rules: sourcing, accuracy, file layout, UI conventions and the privacy rule (never write the VIN, plate or chassis number into any file).
2. Kyle directs the work and does not write code. Explain changes in plain words, ask him clarifying questions before or while working, and cite real sources for any car fact.
3. Edit only source files: `src/`, `tools/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `CLAUDE.md`. The live site's `index.html`, `js/`, `sw.js` and `dist-artifact/` are generated by `python3 tools/build.py`. A GitHub Action (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) runs that build automatically when `src/` or `tools/` change on `main`.
4. `src/js/modules/live.js` is generated by `python3 tools/gen/mklive.py` from `tools/gen/live_extra.js` and `src/link-legacy.html`. Edit those, not live.js.
5. New features go in a new file in `src/js/modules/` (see the module contract in CLAUDE.md), added to `MODULES` in `tools/build.py`.

## Return format (when handing back)
Produce one Markdown file containing:
- Updated sections 1, 2 and 3 using the same headings.
- Under `## 4. Complete Codebase`, every file you created or changed, each as `### \`path/from/repo/root\`` followed by one fenced code block with the **entire** file. Never truncate, never write "unchanged" or "rest of file", never use placeholders.
- Files you did not touch may be left out of a return package. `tools/apply_handoff.py` overlays the files present onto the repo. To delete a file, list it under `## Deleted files` as a bullet with its path in backticks.
- If a full copy of a very large file (such as `src/js/core.js`) will not fit in your output, do not send a partial file. Instead list exact find-and-replace edits under `## Edits to apply` (file, exact old text, exact new text).

Kyle's OBDLink CX connected in the official OBDLink app. In V60 Garage (Bluefy, Live link) it connected and then dropped instantly.

Commit `16f762e` (2026-10-11) shipped a fix:
- `BleTransport` in `src/link-legacy.html` keeps the device, and a drop during connecting no longer ends the attempt.
- `connect()` retries once through `transport.reopen()`, without reopening the picker. The status shows "Link dropped. Reconnecting...".
- Every step is logged to the "Adapter log" under the Connect buttons on Live link: picked, GATT connected, notifications on, dropped, retrying.
- Errors are mapped to plain advice:
  - pairing or encryption: re-plug, connect within 5 minutes, PIN 123456
  - NetworkError: close the OBDLink app, which can hold the adapter
  - NotAllowedError: turn on Bluetooth for Bluefy in iPhone Settings
- `tests/ble.js` mocks Web Bluetooth. A first link that drops gets retried and connects; a link that always drops shows the advice.

Most likely real cause: the OBDLink app was still holding the adapter. It only talks to one app at a time.

**Found 2026-10-13, from Kyle's adapter log.** Bluefy lists the CX's services with upper-case UUIDs and includes its FEF5 firmware-update (SUOTA) service, whose characteristics notify and write but never answer. The old `attach()` preferred "fff0" with a case-sensitive test, so it fell through to the first service with notify+write: FEF5 (`5F78DF94…`). ATZ timed out, later writes failed with an empty error, and `close()` logged a "drop" that was really our own disconnect. Fix: UUIDs normalised to lower case and short form, a list of known serial services (FFF0/FFF1/FFF2 first), housekeeping services never picked, every service and characteristic logged. `tests/ble.js` now mocks the decoy service with upper-case UUIDs. Still to confirm on the real car.

Update 2026-10-12: Kyle reports it still drops with the OBDLink app closed and a new adapter. Added (commit after `a9c4b12`): the retry now sends `ATWS` (warm start) instead of `ATZ`, in case the full reset drops the BLE link; a pending command is failed the moment the link drops (no 6 s wait); the log names the last command sent before each drop. `tests/ble.js` covers a drop after `ATZ`. Still unconfirmed on the real car. The next step is unchanged: get the Adapter conversation log.

## 3. Pending Logic & Blockers
- **G1 entry rules (the research brief).** Every body line traces to a page fetched in that session; never from memory. Allowed: Volvo documents (2016 V60 US owner's manual PDF, maintenance schedule, support pages, NHTSA-hosted bulletins), US government (nhtsa, ecfr, epa, osha), industry bodies (USTMA, TIA, SAE), parts and tool makers' own technical pages. Banned: forums, Reddit, YouTube, Wikipedia, study-guide sites, repair-shop marketing (list in `g1merge.py`). Volvo wins over generic sources for this car. Unsourceable task: short body ending "No sourced procedure found yet." Output: JSON array of `{id, body[3-6 lines], car|null, src[[title,url]], qs[{q, o[4], a, why, src}]}`, two ASE-style questions per task. Run at most three research agents at once: eight at once used up a session.
- **OBDLink CX facts.** Source: OBDLink's "OBDLink CX adapter notes" support article.
  - BLE UART service FFF0: notify on FFF1, write on FFF2.
  - Bonding only works in the first 5 minutes after power-on. PIN 123456.
  - Always encrypted.
  - No queued writes; chunk writes to the MTU (Live link uses 20-byte chunks).
  - The CX has three LEDs: PWR, OBD, BLE.
- **Connection flow.** `connect()` runs `open()`, then `initElm()`.
  - `initElm()` sends `ATZ ATE0 ATL0 ATS1 ATH1 ATCAF1 ATAT1 ATSP0`, then `0100` with a 12 s timeout, then `ATDPN`, then reads the supported PIDs.
  - `transport.connecting` suppresses `onclose` while connecting, and `transport.dropped` records a drop.
  - It retries once. A second drop shows the NetworkError advice.
- **Bluefy has no AI.** In Bluefy, reading uploads uses on-device OCR. An own-API-key option was declined for now ("don't care either way").
- **Redaction must happen before storage.** Photos go to IndexedDB, then to the sync repo. `scan.js` redacts first. Never store the original.
- **Gate logic** (`story.js`):
  - Act 1 is open from the start. Later acts need the previous act closed. Within an act, a case opens once the previous one has started.
  - `revealedSet()` is the union of: Today, Story, the `reveals` of every available case, `ACT_REWARD`, and everything once the finale is reached or "Show everything" is on.
  - Jumps to hidden tabs still work.
- **Real scans versus simulated scans.** The Signal and Baseline need a real scan. `scans(api, true)` ignores `lastScan` when it matches a simulated scan's date.
- **Unconfirmed data** (keep it labeled unconfirmed in the UI):
  - Polestar availability and price in 2026
  - 4G modem (SMB 00-035)
  - live tire prices
  - NHTSA position on LED bulbs
  - petrol injection pressure and turbo type
  - which TG-81SC ratio set applies
  - contents of TJ30087
  - Kyle's build month
  - Kyle's oil consumption
- **Workflow.** Gemini's returned work comes back through Claude, which applies it with `tools/apply_handoff.py`, then builds, tests and commits. Gemini's last return (the first `scan.js`) was rewritten for these problems:
  - per-word matching
  - preview outlines saved into the photo
  - a broken script URL
  - not wired to anything
- **Size constraint.** `src/js/core.js` is about 240 KB. Put new features in `src/js/modules/`, and return core.js changes as find-and-replace edits under `## Edits to apply`.
- **Generated file.** Never edit `src/js/modules/live.js` directly. Edit `src/link-legacy.html`, `tools/gen/live_extra.js`, `tools/gen/cipher.py` or `tools/gen/mklive.py`, then run `python3 tools/gen/mklive.py`.
- **Privacy.** Never put the VIN, plate or chassis number in any repo file. Test fixtures use the public example VIN `1HGBH41JXMN109186` only.

### `CLAUDE.md`

```markdown
# V60 Garage

A learn / diagnose / maintain app for one car: Kyle's 2016 Volvo V60 T5 Drive-E Premier. It runs on GitHub Pages as an installable app for iPhone and desktop, and also as a Claude artifact. Kyle directs the work and doesn't write code. Explain changes in plain words.

Read `docs/ROADMAP.md` before starting. It holds the backlog, the decisions so far, and open questions for Kyle. `docs/chats/` holds a digest of every claude.ai chat about the car (what Kyle said and decided, facts with sources, open questions), with personal details left out. `docs/GAME_DESIGN.md` explains the progression. Since Oct 2026 the car is the menu: the home is a side view with numbered points, each opening a view (hood, wheel, cabin, underside, walk-around) whose parts (items) are small manuals of chapters (Know, Check, Service, Diagnose, Upgrade). Three levels only: the car, a view, a part. A part page holds all of its chapters as sections; each step opens in place with the Library article, the Training lesson, the DIY job or the troubleshooter inside it (there is no chapter page; `ch:` jumps land on the part page with that chapter's first undone step open). Everything opens along one strict path (`src/js/data/path.js`, Kyle's choice 2026-10-15): 113 steps in 18 units, in a beginner's order starting with this car: safety, what the car is telling you and its history, then Know and Check one system at a time, each system ending with its G1 study and Owner quiz, then Service, Diagnose, Upgrade, and last the Technician quizzes and the mock G1. Only the current step is open; a step marked `park` (a shop, a purchase, a dealer) can be set aside and closes by itself when its evidence arrives. Story cases no longer open anything: they close from the same evidence, the case board points at the path, and a case step past the current one shows its path step instead of Go. Progression is the certification track (`src/js/modules/track.js`): seven ASE G1 areas, each a level with Owner and Technician rungs, readiness meters, ASE-style quizzes that open hands-on first, and a mock G1. There is no XP, rank, skill tree or V60 Master exam any more. A page is reachable only when an open chapter's step points at it (`src/js/data/manual.js`), the story reveals it (`src/js/modules/story.js` `reveals`, `ACT_REWARD`), or the Index lists it, so a new feature must be placed on the path (as a chapter step) or it stays hidden until the finale.

## The car (public repo: never commit the VIN, plate or chassis number)
- 2016 V60 T5 Drive-E Premier, FWD, B4204T11 2.0 L turbo four, 240 hp / 258 lb-ft, Aisin TG-81SC 8-speed, start/stop, indirect tire monitor (no wheel sensors).
- Volvo bulletin codes: engine code 40, vehicle type 155.
- Bought about Aug 2025, as-is from an independent lot (Lams Austin Autos), at about 84,550 miles, with no service history. 91,357 miles on 2026-10-14 (cluster photo). Digital instrument cluster (a Premier item). Austin, TX (Travis County emissions testing). iPhone only.
- Tire pressure light is always on. Timing belt history is unknown.

## Rules for content
- Every fact needs a real source. Prefer Volvo's owner's manual, Volvo bulletins (NHTSA PDFs), NHTSA APIs and Volvo press releases. Sources live in `window.V60_SOURCES` (facts.js), or as `[title, url]` pairs.
- Mark anything unconfirmed as unconfirmed in the UI text. Never guess numbers, prices, the car's color or its options.
- Volvo's manual wins over forums and generic advice. Where Volvo's documents conflict, say so.
- No meta-commentary or praise in UI copy. Plain, direct sentences.

## Layout
- `src/` is the only place to edit. The root `index.html`, `version.json`, `app.css`, `js/`, `sw.js`, `manifest.webmanifest` and all of `dist-artifact/` are build output.
- `src/body.html` holds the core markup; `src/css/*.css` are concatenated, `app.css` first, then alphabetically (`manual.css` the manual's UI, `modules.css`, `theme.css` last: the workshop-manual dress for everything else). Fonts: Barlow Condensed (display), IBM Plex Sans (body), IBM Plex Mono (numbers, labels), from `src/fonts.html`.
- `src/js/data/manual.js` is the manual's spine (views, items, chapters, steps; `caseOpens` only labels which case points at a chapter); `src/js/modules/manual.js` is its engine and UI (tabs `car`, `view`, `item`, `index`, `path`; the path engine (`compute()` opens chapters up to the current step); `window.V60_MANUAL`; the gate wrapper; markers: amber glow = open and never opened, amber dot = `last` chapter; photo views with pins under `mod("manual").views`). The part page (`renderItem`, also chapter 0 as item `"0"`) renders chapters as sections and steps as `<details>` that open in place: articles through `window.V60_KB.articleHtml`, lessons through `api.trainInto(containerId, missionId)` (core's Training renders into any container; `api.trainReset()` when leaving), DIY jobs through `window.V60_DIYUI.html/done`, troubleshooters with a small walker in manual.js; workbench steps (records, Live link, photos, bulletins) keep a Go button. Navigation is three roots in the bar: `car`, `glove`, `live` (Glovebox and Link are workbenches and always open); Cases (`story`, also where Options live) and the whole path (`path`) are in the Index. The home shows the Next card first (the path's current step, one button, a progress bar, anything set aside, a waiting scene), then the figure (a locked view says which step opens it), one Index button and the red list. `window.V60_PATH` (manual.js) exposes the path: `current()`, `state(key)`, `reached(key)`, `taskReached(id)`, `goStage(go)`, `next()`; jump `path:next` opens the current step. Every other tab is hidden-unless-active and reached by jumps, by the Index page (`INDEX` groups), or by the See also strips (`ALSO`: on each view, and under the titles of Glovebox, Link and Cases); all of these list only pages the gate shows. The crumb bar (`#crumb`) keeps a trail: "← Back to …" retraces the path from any page, and a root clears it. Inner pages (anything but the home) get a one-row header (`body.inner`): the full dashboard, odometer and readiness chip live on the home only. A new page must go in `INDEX` (and `ALSO` where it fits) as well as on the path; `tests/nav.js` fails if any page has no way in.
- `src/js/core.js` is the garage engine: Training (the Academy code, tab id `academy`, hidden from the nav and opened from story steps; it renders into `aui.root`, normally `acadBody`), bay maps, specs, health score, records, Data lab, simulator, backup. It exposes `window.V60` (the API) and `window.__v60` (test hook). The old XP totals still exist internally (`xpTotal`) but nothing shows them; `hud()` writes the track's readiness into the header chip.
- `src/js/data/track.js` is the certification track's data (G1 areas with question counts, part and fact mapping, pass bar) and `quiz.js` its question bank (original ASE-style questions, each with a source, area, rung and part; recall questions are built from V60_FACTS at run time). `src/js/modules/track.js` also renders a path study step (jump `study:D1-D13`) and starts a quiz from the path (jump `quiz:sus:1`); tasks, quizzes and the mock stay locked until the path reaches them, and a chapter set aside counts as hands-on done (`V60_MANUAL.settled`). It owns `window.V60_TRACK` (`ready()`, `areaReady(id)`, `rung(id)`, `passedG1()`, `strip()`, `hud()`, `areaOf(itemId)`) and `window.V60_PERK` (mech: any area at Owner; timeline: 3 records or receipts). Saved under `track`: `quiz{area:rung}`, `g1`. The story's finale needs `passedG1()`.
- `src/js/data/` holds `facts.js` (V60_SOURCES and V60_FACTS, which drive the Library, Cards and the quizzes' recall questions), `articles.js` (V60_ARTICLES; body lines use "## " for headings and "- " for bullets) and `toolprices.js` (V60_TOOL_PRICES: store prices for the Glovebox tool inventory, each from a fetched retailer page, with the date checked; the owner's own prices live in `glove.price`).
- `src/js/modules/*.js` is one feature per file. Each registers itself:
  `(window.V60_MODULES = window.V60_MODULES || []).push({ id, tabs:[{id, section, label, order, hidden?, html}], init(api), render(api), clean(v), xp(api), actions(api, list), today(api) -> [{order, html}], jump(api, kind, id) })`
  - Sections: `today`, `learn`, `car`, `check`, `data`.
  - Saved data lives under `api.mod(id)` / `api.setMod(id, v)`. `clean(v)` must validate it.
  - Navigation: `data-jump="tab:<tabId>"`, or a module's own kind such as `kb:<articleId>`, `diy:<jobId>`, `tree:<id>`, `tsb:<id>`, `story:<id>`, `ask:<text>`.
- `src/js/modules/live.js` is generated. Edit `tools/gen/live_extra.js` or `tools/gen/mklive.py`, then run `python3 tools/gen/mklive.py`. It ports `src/link-legacy.html` (the original V60 Link). Element ids are prefixed `lk-`.
- To add a feature: create `src/js/modules/<name>.js`, add it to `MODULES` in `tools/build.py`, put its styles in `src/css/modules.css`, and give its tab a place in the story's reveal order.
- `sync.js` owns `window.V60_SYNC`. Core calls `changed()` after every local save, and sync uses `api.replaceState`, `api.snapshot`, `api.blobGet` and `api.blobPut`. The token lives in localStorage key `v60-sync`, never in the synced state. `ui.js` draws the header pulse strip and handles `data-speak` read-aloud. `scan.js` owns `window.V60_SCAN.process(file, kind)`: on-device reading (Tesseract.js 5.1.1 from jsDelivr, cached by the service worker in `v60-ocr`) and blacking out personal details before any photo is stored or synced. Core's `shrink()` routes every photo through it; set `window.__V60_NOSCAN = true` to bypass it in tests. The owner's hide list lives in localStorage `v60-scan-private`, never in synced state. `guide.js` owns `window.V60_GUIDE` (no button since the path: the walkthrough opens from code only until it is ported onto path steps) (`level(caseId)` 0 guided / 1 assisted / 2 on your own, `start(caseId)`); it reads the story through `window.V60_STORY` (`cases`, `next`, `status`, `available`, `mark`). See GAME_DESIGN.md, Guided mode.
- Story owns `window.V60_GATE` (which tabs are visible; core's nav asks it), `window.V60_KNOW` (Library and flashcard unlocks) and `window.V60_CB` (Codebook decoding; Live link calls it through hooks in `tools/gen/cipher.py`). Raw adapter signals and their meanings live in `src/js/data/codebook.js`.

## Build, test, deploy
- Build: `python3 tools/build.py`. It writes the root files and `dist-artifact/`, and bumps the service worker version so installed apps show "Update available".
- Tests (Playwright). On Kyle's Windows PC (and anywhere with `npm install` done): `npm test` (= `node tests/run.js`) builds, then runs every test in Chromium and in WebKit dressed as an iPhone 13 (Bluefy's engine; `tests/engine.js` swaps the browser, serves the repo on 127.0.0.1 and gives each context a persistent profile, because WebKit's private contexts can't store Blobs in IndexedDB). Arguments: test names, `--chromium`/`--webkit`, `--no-build`. On Windows use `python`, not `python3`. In the cloud session, one test at a time:
  `PLAYWRIGHT_PATH=/opt/npm-tools/node_modules/playwright CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium node tests/regression.js`
  `tests/regression.js` checks every tab on phone, desktop and dark: no errors, no horizontal overflow, no broken `tab:` jumps. Every test sets exit code 1 on a failure.
  `tests/features.js` exercises Live link (simulated car), Bulletins and Upgrades. `tests/sync.js` exercises cross-device sync against a mocked GitHub API. `tests/guide.js` exercises guided mode (walkthrough, safety check, stuck ladder, level changes, intros, welcome back). `tests/ble.js` runs Live link against a mocked Bluetooth adapter that drops the first link (as the OBDLink CX can while iOS pairs). `tests/scan.js` checks the redaction rules and reads a synthetic receipt end to end (needs jsDelivr reachable). `tests/odo.js` reloads the app four times to check saved data is never overwritten at startup. `tests/tire.js` reads a synthetic tire sidewall (DOT date, size) end to end. `tests/photos.js` saves a photo and checks the record and the picture survive reloads. `tests/story.js` exercises the story case board: closing cases, known-risk closures, scenes and mission jumps. `tests/update.js` checks the "new version is ready" bar works without a service worker (Bluefy has none). `tests/nav.js` checks every page has a way in and a way back (map button, index, see-also, crumb trail) and that the bay map faces the right way. `tests/tools.js` checks the Glovebox tool tiers, store prices and the owner's price override, and the ASE article. `tests/track.js` checks the certification track: the question bank's shape, hands-on-first quiz gating, an area quiz end to end, the Owner rung, the mock G1 with its clock and score report, and the Next card on the home. `tests/path.js` checks the path: every chapter and G1 task on it once, each quiz after what it tests, only the current step open, the home's one Next card, setting a step aside, a study step, the path page, and case steps locked past the path. `tests/manual.js` exercises the manual: path-order opening, glow and resume markers, the gate, steps opening in place (lesson, article, troubleshooter), the Go/back crumb, and a photo as a view with draggable points. Tests set `window.__V60_TEST = true`, which stops the story prologue from auto-playing.
- Look at screenshots in `tests/shots/` (gitignored) before calling UI work done; the `-iphone.png` ones are what Kyle sees.
- Deploy: pull first (`git pull --rebase -X theirs origin main`), because the GitHub Action commits build output after every source push. Then commit to `main` as `bmcdoorz94 <kfitz719@gmail.com>` and push to https://github.com/bmcdoorz94/V60-Link. Pages serves https://bmcdoorz94.github.io/V60-Link/ (the path is case-sensitive).
- Claude artifact (only from a Claude session that has the Artifact tool): publish `dist-artifact/garage.html` with the `files` map from `dist-artifact/files.json` to https://claude.ai/artifact/9mpkZE2EzzU2UxWLbqTohR, with capabilities `{"db":{},"user":{},"sample":{"images":true},"downloads":true,"assets":{}}`. Web Bluetooth doesn't work inside artifacts.

## UI
- Design tokens are in `src/css/app.css` (`--bg` paper, `--panel`, `--ink`, `--line`, `--new` amber which only ever means new or where you left off, `--done`, `--teal` for instrument traces). Square corners, hairlines, no shadows. Live link and the Data lab keep their instrument faces. Light and dark themes are both required.
- Phone first: Kyle uses the app only held upright. 390 px wide with no sideways scroll; `tests/portrait.js` fails on text under 11 px (drawings included, after they shrink), taps under 32 px, or sideways scrolling. Draw new figures tall, not wide; tables stack into cards on phones by themselves. Bottom bar on phone (The car · Cases · Glovebox · Link), side rail on desktop. Figures are 358 wide schematic SVGs in `manual.js` (`FIG`); the owner's photo replaces a figure once pinned.
- With every feature, re-check that its screen isn't crowded. Move secondary material into `<details>`, and prefer one clear next action per card.
- Toggle groups use `.seg` with `aria-pressed`. Pills are `ok`, `watch`, `concern`/`bad`, and `info`/`none`.
- Files out of the app go through `window.V60_FILE.save(name, text, type)` (ui.js), never a bare `<a download>`: Bluefy on iPhone cannot download, cannot print, and its share sheet drops attached files and passes only the title, so the helper always includes the content as text. Copy buttons need a real selection on a visible box (`V60_FILE` does not cover copying; see the adapter log in link-legacy.html). Print buttons need a share-as-text twin (`V60_FILE.textOf(el)`).

## Claude ↔ Gemini handoff protocol
Kyle alternates between Claude and Gemini when usage limits hit. Neither AI can talk to the other, so state moves through one Markdown file.
- **"Initiate Handoff Protocol"** means: stop development immediately and produce the handoff:
  1. Rewrite `docs/HANDOFF_STATE.md` with three sections: `## 1. Current Active Objective`, `## 2. Immediate Next Steps` (precise, prioritized), and `## 3. Pending Logic & Blockers` (errors, hardware test parameters, design choices under evaluation).
  2. Run `python3 tools/handoff.py`. It writes `HANDOFF.md` (gitignored) with those sections plus `## 4. Complete Codebase`: every source file in full, copied byte for byte by the script (never typed out by hand, so nothing is truncated or replaced with placeholders), plus a manifest with SHA-256 prefixes and the icons in base64.
  3. Commit and push the source changes, then send `HANDOFF.md` to Kyle as a downloadable file.
- Build outputs (root `index.html`, `js/`, `sw.js`, `link.html`, `dist-artifact/`) are deliberately left out. `tools/build.py` regenerates them from `src/`, and the GitHub Action `.github/workflows/build.yml` runs that build on every push to `src/` or `tools/`.
- **Always-ready copy:** `.github/workflows/handoff.yml` rebuilds `HANDOFF.md` after every push to `main` and force-pushes it as the only file on the `handoff` branch (https://github.com/bmcdoorz94/V60-Link/blob/handoff/HANDOFF.md). A session can be cut off by a usage limit without warning, so keep `docs/HANDOFF_STATE.md` current and push finished work in small commits; the branch then always holds a usable handoff.
- **Receiving a handoff back** (Kyle uploads a .md from Gemini): run `python3 tools/apply_handoff.py <file> --dry-run`, review it, then run without `--dry-run`. It writes every `### \`path\`` + code block as a full-file replacement, refuses build outputs and paths outside the repo, handles `## Deleted files`, writes sections 1–3 to `docs/HANDOFF_STATE.md`, and prints any `## Edits to apply` (find-and-replace edits for files too large to return whole, such as core.js) for you to apply. Then build, run the tests, review the diff for accuracy problems and placeholders, and commit.
```

### `README.md`

```markdown
# V60 Link

A single-page OBD-II companion for a 2016 Volvo V60 T5 (works with most CAN-era cars). It talks to a Bluetooth LE ELM327-type adapter (tested design target: OBDLink CX) using Web Bluetooth.

- Health check: VIN, check-engine light, stored / pending / permanent codes per module, freeze frame, readiness monitors, emissions readiness estimate (40 CFR 85.2222 rule)
- Live data recording with CSV export (format read by the V60 Garage Data lab)
- Code clearing with safeguards (requires a saved scan, engine off, typed confirmation)
- Simulated car mode for practice without an adapter

## Where it runs
- iPhone / iPad: the free **Bluefy** browser (Safari has no Web Bluetooth)
- Android, Windows, macOS, ChromeOS: Chrome or Edge

Standard OBD-II only. It does not reach airbag/ABS/body modules, change module software, or tune the engine.
```

        <div class="field"><label for="clMiles">Odometer</label><input id="clMiles" type="number" inputmode="numeric" min="0" step="1"></div>
        <div class="field"><label for="clState">State</label><select id="clState"><option value="active">Active</option><option value="cleared">Cleared, may return</option><option value="resolved">Fixed</option></select></div>
        <div class="field" style="flex:1 1 14em"><label for="clNote">Notes</label><input id="clNote" class="wide" type="text" maxlength="200"></div>
        <button type="submit">Add code</button>
      </form>
      <div class="scroll"><table><thead><tr><th>Code</th><th>Meaning</th><th class="num">Date</th><th class="num">Miles</th><th>State</th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody id="codeBody"></tbody></table></div>
      <div class="row"><div class="field"><label for="linkFile">Import a V60 Link report (.json)</label><input id="linkFile" type="file" accept=".json,application/json"></div><span class="status" id="linkStatus" role="status"></span></div>
      <div id="lastScan"></div>
    </section>
    <div class="note calm"><b>What a generic scanner covers.</b> A basic OBD-II adapter reads engine and emissions codes. Airbag, ABS, transmission detail and Volvo-specific codes usually need Volvo-aware software such as the dealer's VIDA or a capable aftermarket tool.</div>
  </div>

  <!-- DATA LAB -->
  <div class="panel" id="p-lab" hidden>
    <section>
      <h2>Data lab</h2>
      <p class="lede">Load a log from a scanner app and the lab checks warm-up, fuel trims, charging, idle and boost, then charts every channel on a shared time axis. This page cannot talk to the car's port itself, so the car-to-page link is an exported file.</p>
      <details class="card">
        <summary><b>How to get a log from the car</b></summary>
        <div class="pbody">
          <ol>
            <li>Plug a Bluetooth or Wi-Fi ELM327-type OBD-II adapter into the port under the dash.</li>
            <li>Use a scanner app that records data to a file, such as Car Scanner, Torque or OBD Fusion, and log at least coolant temperature, RPM, speed, fuel trims, battery voltage and intake pressure.</li>
            <li>Drive a normal mix: cold start, some city, some steady highway, and one firm acceleration if safe.</li>
            <li>Export the log as CSV and load it below. Both one-column-per-channel files and files with PID and VALUE columns are read. If a channel is missed, the mapping step lets you pick the column.</li>
          </ol>
          <p class="lede">Logging is read-only. Nothing here writes to the car or tunes the engine.</p>
        </div>
      </details>
      <div class="row">
        <div class="field"><label for="labFile">Scanner log (.csv)</label><input id="labFile" type="file" accept=".csv,.txt,text/csv,text/plain"></div>
        <button type="button" class="quiet" id="labDemo">Load demo drive</button>
        <div class="field"><label for="tempU">Temperature in file</label><select id="tempU"><option value="auto">Auto</option><option value="C">Celsius</option><option value="F">Fahrenheit</option></select></div>
        <div class="field"><label for="speedU">Speed in file</label><select id="speedU"><option value="auto">Auto</option><option value="kph">km/h</option><option value="mph">mph</option></select></div>
      </div>
      <p class="status" id="labStatus">No log loaded yet.</p>
    </section>
    <section id="labBody" hidden>
      <div class="note" id="demoNote" hidden><b>Demo data.</b> This drive is generated by the page to show the tools. It is not from your car and cannot be saved to your records.</div>
      <h3>Channel mapping</h3>
      <div class="map" id="mapGrid"></div>
      <h3>Findings</h3>
      <ul class="finds" id="finds"></ul>
      <h3>Channel statistics</h3>
      <div class="scroll"><table><thead><tr><th>Channel</th><th class="num">Min</th><th class="num">Mean</th><th class="num">Max</th><th class="num">5th to 95th</th></tr></thead><tbody id="statBody"></tbody></table></div>
      <div class="row"><button type="button" id="saveRun">Save this run to my records</button><span class="status" id="runStatus"></span></div>
      <h3>Traces</h3>
      <div class="toggles" id="toggles" role="group" aria-label="Channels to chart"></div>
      <div id="charts" style="display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:10px"></div>
    </section>
    <section>
      <h2>Saved runs</h2>
      <p class="lede">Save a run after each log to see how coolant warm-up, fuel trims, charging and idle change over weeks. A drift matters more than any single number.</p>
      <div class="scroll"><table><thead><tr><th class="num">Date</th><th class="num">Miles</th><th class="num">Minutes</th><th class="num">Coolant max</th><th class="num">Warm-up</th><th class="num">LTFT</th><th class="num">STFT</th><th class="num">Volts</th><th class="num">Idle rpm</th><th class="num">Flags</th><th></th></tr></thead><tbody id="runBody"></tbody></table></div>
      <h3>Drift against your baseline</h3>
      <p class="lede">Your baseline is the median of your earlier saved runs, so the page compares the car with itself rather than with a generic spec. It needs at least three saved runs. Warm-up time depends on outside temperature, so compare runs from similar weather.</p>
      <ul class="finds" id="driftFinds"></ul>
      <div class="sparks" id="sparks"></div>
    </section>

  <!-- UNLOCKS -->
  <div class="panel" id="p-unlocks" hidden>
    <section>
      <h2>Unlocks</h2>
      <p class="lede">Everything this page cannot do by itself, mapped to a real way to get it done, with cost, effort and risk. Researched October 2026. Prices change, and items marked "verify" could not be confirmed.</p>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>1. Talk to the car live from your iPhone</h3>
      <p>iPhones cannot use classic-Bluetooth adapters, and Safari cannot use Bluetooth from a web page at all. Three routes work, from easiest to most custom.</p>
      <div class="cols">
        <div class="card"><span class="pill ok">Easiest</span><h4>Adapter plus Car Scanner app</h4><p>Car Scanner ELM OBD2 reads and clears codes, freeze frames, emissions readiness, Mode 06 test results and live data, and exports CSV logs that the Data lab reads. Pro is $7.99 one-time. A recording saves when you tap Disconnect, so don't force-quit mid-drive.</p></div>
        <div class="card"><span class="pill info">Custom</span><h4>V60 Link in Bluefy</h4><p>The companion page built for this garage. It runs in the free Bluefy browser with an OBDLink CX and exports reports and logs that import here. It has been tested against a simulated car only, so expect some first-connection troubleshooting. It needs to be hosted at a web address (see the note at the bottom).</p></div>
        <div class="card"><span class="pill watch">New, untested</span><h4>iOSWebBLE Safari extension</h4><p>A free extension for iOS 26.2 and later that claims to add web Bluetooth to Safari. If it works, V60 Link would run in Safari too. It has not been tried here.</p></div>
      </div>
      <div class="scroll"><table>
        <thead><tr><th>Adapter</th><th class="num">Price</th><th>Works on iPhone</th><th>Works with V60 Link</th><th>Notes</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><b>OBDLink CX</b></td><td class="num">$79.95</td><td>Yes, Bluetooth LE</td><td>Yes. Its data channel is documented.</td><td>Best match for V60 Link. Was listed out of stock at OBDLink when checked. Pairs only in the first 5 minutes after power-up.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><b>Veepeak OBDCheck BLE+</b></td><td class="num">$41.99</td><td>Yes, Bluetooth LE</td><td>Probably <span class="tag verify">verify</span></td><td>Good value for scanner apps. The plain BLE version is $31.99.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><b>Vgate iCar Pro</b></td><td class="num">~$25–33</td><td>Yes (BLE version)</td><td>Probably <span class="tag verify">verify</span></td><td>Car Scanner recommends the newer iCar Pro 2S. Update older firmware.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><b>OBDLink MX+</b></td><td class="num">$139.95</td><td>Yes (Apple MFi)</td><td>No, it has no BLE radio</td><td>Fastest with apps, but it cannot talk to a web page.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table></div>
      <p class="status">Pick: an OBDLink CX if you want V60 Link. A Veepeak BLE+ with Car Scanner if you want the cheapest reliable start.</p>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>2. Clear codes without wrecking your inspection</h3>
      <ul class="plain">
        <li>Texas dropped safety inspections for personal cars on January 1, 2025, but <b>Travis County still requires an emissions test</b>.</li>
        <li>The test reads the readiness monitors. A 2001 or newer car may have <b>at most one</b> monitor not ready. Any check-engine light with a stored code fails.</li>
        <li>Clearing codes, or disconnecting the battery, resets every monitor. A generic way to complete them: a cold start, stop-and-go driving up to about 30 mph, then 5 to 7 minutes at a steady 55 mph, repeated over a few days. Some evaporative-system tests need the car to sit about 8 hours first. A Volvo-specific drive cycle could not be confirmed.</li>
        <li>Before an inspection, run a health check in V60 Link or Car Scanner and confirm readiness first.</li>
      </ul>
      <div class="note">Clearing is for confirming a repair, not for hiding a fault. Texas makes manipulating an emissions test result an offense.</div>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>3. Read airbag, ABS, climate and body modules, plus Volvo-only data</h3>
      <p>Phone apps reach the engine (and often the transmission) through standard OBD-II. None of the major iOS apps offers Volvo enhanced diagnostics: OBD Fusion and the OBDLink app do not list Volvo. Owners have reported a Car Scanner "Volvo 2010+" profile showing oil level and transmission temperature, but mostly on diesel cars and Android. Whether it works on your T5 is unconfirmed, and it costs nothing to try. <span class="tag verify">verify</span></p>
      <div class="scroll"><table>
        <thead><tr><th>Route</th><th>What it takes</th><th class="num">Cost</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><b>Volvo VIDA, diagnostics tier</b></td><td>A personal account with a North American VIN, a Volvo DiCE interface, and a Windows 11 <b>Pro</b> PC (Intel i5 from late 2017 or newer, 16 GB RAM). Reads every module. It cannot run from an iPhone.</td><td class="num">$48.15 / 3 days<br><small>plus about $500 for a genuine DiCE, plus a required bulletin fee</small></td></tr>
          <tr><td><b>Independent Volvo specialist</b></td><td>A shop with VIDA does a full-module scan.</td><td class="num">Shop rate <span class="tag verify">verify</span></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table></div>
      <p class="status">For a one-off problem in a non-engine system, a specialist's scan will almost always cost less than buying DiCE and a qualifying PC.</p>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>4. Software updates and module settings</h3>
      <p>VIDA's top tier adds software downloads: $73.14 for 3 days, and each download is bought separately on top. A 3-day pass runs 72 hours straight and cannot be paused. Third-party J2534 interfaces can flash emissions modules only, so DiCE is still needed for the rest. The other route is a Volvo dealer, whose price for a software update could not be found. <span class="tag verify">verify</span></p>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>5. More power</h3>
      <p>The only factory-backed option is <b>Polestar Performance Optimization</b>, built for exactly your car: V60 T5 Drive-E FWD automatic, 2016. A Volvo dealer installs it in about an hour.</p>
      <div class="scroll"><table>
        <thead><tr><th></th><th class="num">Stock</th><th class="num">Polestar</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Peak power</td><td class="num">242 hp</td><td class="num">250 hp</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Mid-range power</td><td class="num">197 hp</td><td class="num">218 hp</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Torque</td><td class="num">258 lb-ft</td><td class="num">295 lb-ft</td></tr>
          <tr><td>0–60 mph</td><td class="num">6.4 s</td><td class="num">6.3 s</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table></div>
      <ul class="plain">
        <li>Volvo states it does not affect the factory warranty or service intervals, and that it keeps certified emissions and fuel figures. The warranty point matters little at this age, but the emissions point matters for inspection.</li>
        <li>The US price and whether dealers still sell it in 2026 could not be confirmed. Call a dealer and ask for article number 31459463. For reference, UK owners paid £700–800 in 2019. <span class="tag verify">verify</span></li>
        <li>No emissions-legal aftermarket tune for the Drive-E T5 was found. Changing engine calibration counts as emissions tampering under the Clean Air Act, and Texas fines disabling emissions systems. Civil enforcement continues even though federal criminal prosecutions were scaled back in 2026.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="status">The honest take: the gain is mostly mid-range torque, and 0–60 drops by a tenth. For this car's age and oil-consumption history, maintenance buys more than tuning.</p>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>6. Recalls and the paper trail</h3>
      <p>Look up open safety recalls by VIN at <a href="https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls" target="_blank" rel="noopener">nhtsa.gov/recalls</a>. Repairs are free at a Volvo dealer. The lookup does not list recalls already repaired. The Recall check training mission walks through it.</p>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>Still impossible, honestly</h3>
      <ul class="plain">
        <li>Any web page, this one included, changing engine calibration or module coding.</li>
        <li>Volvo's dealer software running on an iPhone.</li>
        <li>Clearing a <i>permanent</i> code. Only the car's own self-test after a real fix clears it.</li>
      </ul>
    </section>

    <section>
      <h3>Hosting V60 Link</h3>
      <p>V60 Link is live at <a href="https://bmcdoorz94.github.io/V60-Link/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">bmcdoorz94.github.io/V60-Link</a>. On iPhone, open that address in the free Bluefy browser, because Safari cannot use Bluetooth. The simulated car mode works in any browser for practice.</p>
    </section>

  <!-- LEARN -->
  <div class="panel" id="p-learn" hidden>
    <section>
      <h2>How it works</h2>
      <p class="lede">The T5 is a small four-cylinder that uses a turbocharger to make the power of a bigger engine. The path air and oil take explains most of what goes wrong and why the maintenance list looks the way it does.</p>
      <div class="diagram tall">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 340 498" role="img" aria-label="Diagram of the intake air path down the left, the exhaust path up the right, and the crankcase ventilation loop of a turbocharged four-cylinder engine">
          <defs>
            <marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 z" class="head"/></marker>
            <marker id="ahb" viewBox="0 0 8 8" refX="7" refY="4" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 z" class="headb"/></marker>
          </defs>
          <text x="82" y="14" text-anchor="middle">AIR IN</text><text x="258" y="14" text-anchor="middle">EXHAUST OUT</text>
          <rect class="box" x="24" y="24" width="116" height="44" rx="3"/><text x="82" y="50" text-anchor="middle">Air filter</text>
          <rect class="box" x="24" y="112" width="116" height="44" rx="3"/><text x="82" y="138" text-anchor="middle">Compressor</text>
          <rect class="box" x="24" y="200" width="116" height="44" rx="3"/><text x="82" y="226" text-anchor="middle">Intercooler</text>
          <rect class="box" x="24" y="288" width="116" height="44" rx="3"/><text x="82" y="314" text-anchor="middle">Throttle</text>
          <rect class="box" x="200" y="24" width="116" height="44" rx="3"/><text x="258" y="50" text-anchor="middle">Exhaust out</text>
          <rect class="box" x="200" y="112" width="116" height="44" rx="3"/><text x="258" y="138" text-anchor="middle">Turbine</text>
          <rect class="engine" x="24" y="376" width="292" height="78" rx="3"/>
          <text x="170" y="406" text-anchor="middle">Engine · 4 cylinders</text><text x="170" y="434" text-anchor="middle" class="lab-b">crankcase</text>
          <line class="flow" x1="82" y1="68" x2="82" y2="110" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
          <line class="flow" x1="82" y1="156" x2="82" y2="198" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
          <line class="flow" x1="82" y1="244" x2="82" y2="286" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
          <line class="flow" x1="82" y1="332" x2="82" y2="374" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
          <line class="flow" x1="258" y1="376" x2="258" y2="158" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
          <line class="flow" x1="258" y1="112" x2="258" y2="70" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
          <line class="shaft" x1="140" y1="134" x2="200" y2="134"/>
          <text x="170" y="176" text-anchor="middle">shared</text><text x="170" y="191" text-anchor="middle">shaft</text>
          <text x="266" y="246">hot</text><text x="266" y="261">exhaust</text><text x="266" y="276">spins the</text><text x="266" y="291">turbine</text>
          <path class="pcv" d="M24 430 H10 V90 H80" marker-end="url(#ahb)"/>
          <text x="170" y="474" text-anchor="middle" class="lab-b">Dashed: the PCV loop returns</text><text x="170" y="490" text-anchor="middle" class="lab-b">crankcase vapors to the intake</text>
        </svg>
      </div>
      <div class="cols">
        <div><h3>Air in</h3><p>Air passes the filter, gets squeezed by the compressor, and is cooled in the intercooler so it packs more oxygen. The throttle meters it into the cylinders.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Exhaust out</h3><p>Exhaust spins the turbine, which drives the compressor on a shared shaft. The turbine runs very hot and is lubricated by engine oil, so oil level and quality matter more on a turbo engine.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Crankcase ventilation</h3><p>Some combustion gas always slips past the piston rings. The PCV system pulls those vapors back into the intake to be burned. If it clogs, crankcase pressure rises and oil can be pushed out of seals or drawn into the intake.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Oil</h3><p>Oil lubricates, cools the pistons and feeds the turbo. Spec for your car, per Volvo's 2016 US manual: full synthetic ACEA A5/B5 SAE 5W-30, or Volvo's 0W-20 (VCC RBS0-2AE), such as Castrol Edge Professional. 6.2 US quarts (5.9 L) with the filter.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Cooling</h3><p>The thermostat decides when coolant starts flowing through the radiator. Brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, which is why it is replaced on a calendar and not by miles.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Automatic transmission</h3><p>An Aisin 8-speed. Volvo's published documents list no scheduled fluid change for normal driving, and some independent shops service it anyway. Use the exact fluid your gearbox variant needs and ask a dealer to confirm it by VIN.</p></div>
      </div>
    </section>
    <section>
      <h2>Known trouble</h2>
      <div class="note"><b>Oil consumption is the big one.</b> Volvo issued service bulletins and extended-warranty programs for excessive oil consumption on 2015 and 2016 Drive-E engines, with a repair that replaces pistons and piston rings. The extended coverage was limited to 8 years from delivery or 100,000 miles, so on a 2016 it may already have run out. I could not confirm from the public bulletins whether your exact engine is on the covered list. Ask Volvo customer care or a dealer to check eligibility by VIN, mention your oil log, and ask about goodwill coverage.</div>
      <div class="cols">
        <div><h3>Clogged PCV</h3><p>One owner review describes oil burning at 110,000 miles traced to a clogged PCV system. That is a single account, not a failure rate, but it is a cheap thing to have inspected.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Thermostat</h3><p>Owner comments on Consumer Reports and Edmunds mention thermostat failures. The same Edmunds reviewer says it is costly mainly because the intake has to come off. Anecdotal.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Low oil warning</h3><p>A Volvo service bulletin covers a low oil level message on 2015 and 2016 Drive-E cars and points to piston and ring replacement when consumption stays high. If it appears, check the oil level in the instrument cluster right away and log it.</p></div>
      </div>
    </section>
    <section>
      <h2>What this page can and cannot do</h2>
      <div class="cols">
        <div><h3>Can</h3><p>Track service and part condition, rank what to fix first, look up codes, analyze exported scanner logs, keep a trend of saved runs, and answer questions about your records.</p></div>
        <div><h3>Cannot, on its own</h3><p>Connect to the OBD port directly, since Bluetooth and USB are blocked inside pages like this. The companion page V60 Link does that part: live data, codes, readiness and guarded code clearing. Changing software or tuning the engine needs Volvo's or a tuner's tools. The Unlocks tab maps every one of these to a real route.</p><p><button type="button" class="quiet" data-jump="tab:unlocks">Open Unlocks</button></p></div>
      </div>
    </section>
    <section>
      <h2>Glossary</h2>
      <dl class="gloss">
        <dt>Drive-E</dt><dd>Volvo's family name for its newer 4-cylinder engines. Yours is the 2.0 L turbo petrol.</dd>
        <dt>Turbocharger</dt><dd>A pump driven by exhaust gas that forces extra air into the engine.</dd>
        <dt>Intercooler</dt><dd>A small radiator for the compressed air, since squeezing air heats it.</dd>
        <dt>PCV</dt><dd>Positive crankcase ventilation. Routes crankcase vapors back into the intake.</dd>
        <dt>Piston rings</dt><dd>Seals around each piston that keep combustion gas in and oil out of the cylinder.</dd>
        <dt>Fuel trim</dt><dd>How much the engine computer adds or removes fuel to hit the right mixture. Short-term (STFT) reacts fast, long-term (LTFT) is the learned correction.</dd>
        <dt>MAF</dt><dd>Mass air flow sensor. Measures air entering the engine.</dd>
        <dt>MAP</dt><dd>Manifold absolute pressure. Intake pressure, which rises above outside air pressure under boost.</dd>
        <dt>Thermostat</dt><dd>A valve that holds coolant back until the engine is warm.</dd>
        <dt>ATF</dt><dd>Automatic transmission fluid.</dd>
        <dt>OBD-II</dt><dd>The standard diagnostic port under the dash.</dd>
        <dt>VIDA</dt><dd>Volvo's dealer software for service intervals, bulletins and procedures. Volvo's own sheets treat it as the primary source for intervals.</dd>
        <dt>TSB</dt><dd>Technical service bulletin. A manufacturer notice to dealers about a known problem and its fix. Not the same as a recall.</dd>
        <dt>Extended warranty program</dt><dd>Coverage a manufacturer adds for a specific known defect after the normal warranty ends, usually with its own time and mileage limits.</dd>
      </dl>
    </section>
    <section id="sources">
      <h2>Sources</h2>
      <ul class="src">

        <li><a href="https://www.volvocars.com/au/support/car/v60/article/b51abbf67feb476ec0a8015139ecc710/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Volvo: transmission fluid specifications (later V60 generation)</a></li>
        <li><a href="https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/v60/2015/consumer-reviews/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Edmunds: 2015 V60 owner reviews</a></li>

      </ul>
      <p class="lede">Part descriptions, code meanings, symptom lists and data-lab thresholds are general automotive knowledge, not Volvo-specific specs. Service intervals marked "verify" differ between sources, and some come from other model years or from UK plans in kilometers, converted here. Volvo's dealer system is the final word for your VIN.</p>
    </section>
  </div>
</main>

<main>
  <header>
    <div class="eyebrow">Companion to V60 Garage</div>
    <h1>V60 Link</h1>
    <p class="lede" style="margin-top:8px">Talks to your car through a Bluetooth LE OBD-II adapter. It can read codes, freeze frames and emissions readiness, record live data, and clear codes with safeguards. The results export to V60 Garage.</p>
  </header>

  <section class="card" aria-labelledby="h-conn">
    <h2 id="h-conn">Connect</h2>
    <div class="row">
      <span class="conn" id="conn" role="status"><i></i><span id="connText">Not connected</span></span>
    </div>
    <div class="row" id="connFail" hidden><button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnCopyLog2">Copy the adapter log</button><span class="status" id="connFailMsg">Paste it into the chat so the failure can be read step by step.</span></div>
    <div id="noBt" class="note" hidden></div>
    <div class="row">
      <button type="button" id="btnConnect">Connect adapter</button>
      <button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnDemo">Try with a simulated car</button>
      <button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnDisconnect" disabled>Disconnect</button>
    </div>
    <details id="logBox">
      <summary id="h-log">Adapter log</summary>
      <p class="lede" style="margin:8px 0">Every command sent and every reply, kept on this phone across reloads. Tap Copy and paste it into the chat.</p>
      <textarea class="log" id="log" readonly rows="10" spellcheck="false" aria-label="Adapter log"></textarea>
      <div class="row" style="margin-top:8px"><button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnCopyLog">Copy log</button><button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnShareLog" hidden>Share log</button><button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnDlLog">Save as a file</button><button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnClearLog">Clear log</button></div>
      <p class="lede" style="margin:6px 0 0" id="logHelp">If Copy does nothing, use Share (to Messages, Notes or this chat), or press and hold inside the log, choose Select All, then Copy.</p>
    </details>
    <details>
      <summary>Before you connect</summary>
      <ol style="margin:8px 0 0;padding-left:20px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px">
        <li>Plug the adapter into the OBD-II port under the dashboard on the driver's side.</li>
        <li>Turn the ignition on. The engine can be off to read codes, but it must be running for live data.</li>
        <li>Do not pair the adapter in your phone's Bluetooth settings. This page finds it directly.</li>
        <li>iPhone: Bluefy needs Bluetooth permission. Check Settings, then Bluefy, then Bluetooth is on.</li>
        <li>Tap Connect and pick the adapter from the list. Its name is often OBDII, OBDBLE, IOS-Vlink, OBDLink CX or similar.</li>
        <li>Close any other OBD app first, because only one app can talk to the adapter at a time.</li>
      <li>Empty picker? The adapter only shows while it is advertising, and it stops once the phone holds a link to it. Close this picker, quit Bluefy fully, unplug the adapter for ten seconds, plug it back in, then try again. Music over Bluetooth is fine.</li>
        <li>OBDLink CX: it accepts a new pairing only during the first 5 minutes after it powers up. If it does not show up, unplug it, plug it back in, and connect right away.</li>
      </ol>
    </details>
  </section>

  <section class="card" aria-labelledby="h-scan">
    <h2 id="h-scan">Health check</h2>
    <p class="lede">Reads the VIN, the check-engine light, stored, pending and permanent codes from every module that answers, the freeze frame, and emissions readiness. Engine off with ignition on is fine.</p>
    <div class="row"><button type="button" id="btnScan" disabled>Run health check</button><span class="status" id="scanStatus"></span></div>
    <div id="scanOut" hidden>
      <h3 style="margin-top:6px">Summary</h3>
      <ul class="list" id="summary"></ul>
      <h3>Codes</h3>
      <ul class="list" id="codes"></ul>
      <h3>Freeze frame</h3>
      <p class="lede" style="font-size:14px">A snapshot the engine computer saved at the moment the first code set.</p>
      <dl class="kv" id="freeze"></dl>
      <h3>Emissions readiness</h3>
      <p class="lede" style="font-size:14px">Self-tests the computer runs during normal driving. A monitor that is "not ready" has not finished since codes were last cleared or the battery was disconnected.</p>
      <div class="mon" id="monitors"></div>
      <dl class="kv" id="since"></dl>
      <div class="row">
        <button type="button" id="btnReport">Save report for V60 Garage</button>
        <button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnShareReport" hidden>Share report</button>
        <span class="status" id="reportStatus"></span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="card" aria-labelledby="h-live">
    <h2 id="h-live">Live data</h2>
    <p class="lede">Pick channels, start recording, and drive. Fewer channels give a faster update rate. The recording saves as a CSV that V60 Garage's Data lab reads directly. Have a passenger run it, or set it up before you drive.</p>
    <div class="picks" id="picks" role="group" aria-label="Channels to record"></div>
    <div class="row">
      <button type="button" id="btnLive" disabled>Start recording</button>
      <button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnCsv" disabled>Save CSV</button>
      <button type="button" class="quiet" id="btnShareCsv" hidden>Share CSV</button>
      <span class="status" id="liveStatus"></span>
    </div>
    <div class="tiles" id="tiles"></div>
  </section>

  <section class="card" aria-labelledby="h-clear">
    <h2 id="h-clear">Clear codes</h2>
    <div class="note bad">Clearing codes turns the light off, but it does not fix anything. It also erases the freeze frame and resets every readiness monitor to "not ready." Until you drive enough for the monitors to finish, the car can fail a Texas emissions inspection. If the fault is still there, the light comes back.</div>
    <p class="lede">Unlocks only after a health check in this session, so the codes and freeze frame are saved first.</p>
    <div class="checks" id="clearChecks">
      <label><input type="checkbox" id="ck1" disabled> <span>I saved the health-check report (the Save report button ticks this automatically).</span></label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" id="ck2" disabled> <span>I know what caused the code, or I fixed it and want to confirm the repair.</span></label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" id="ck3" disabled> <span>I am not within about a week of an emissions inspection.</span></label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" id="ck4" disabled> <span>The engine is off and the ignition is on. The page checks this before it sends the command.</span></label>
    </div>
    <div class="row">
      <label for="clearWord" class="status">Type CLEAR to confirm</label>
      <input type="text" id="clearWord" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="characters" disabled>
      <button type="button" class="danger" id="btnClear" disabled>Clear codes</button>
    </div>
    <span class="status" id="clearStatus"></span>
  </section>

  <section class="card">
    <h2>Limits</h2>
    <ul style="margin:0;padding-left:20px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px">
      <li>This page uses standard OBD-II only: engine and emissions data, plus codes from any module that answers the standard request. Airbag, ABS, climate and body modules use Volvo's own diagnostics, which need Volvo's tools.</li>
      <li>It needs an adapter that speaks Bluetooth LE. Classic-Bluetooth adapters do not appear on iPhone or in web browsers.</li>
      <li>It works in Bluefy on iPhone, and in Chrome or Edge on Android, Windows, Mac and ChromeOS. Safari cannot use Bluetooth from a web page.</li>
      <li>It does not change module settings, software or engine tuning.</li>
      <li>The emissions verdict applies the federal readiness rule (40 CFR 85.2222). The inspection station's result is the one that counts.</li>
    </ul>
  </section>
</main>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  function $(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }
  function esc(s) { return String(s == null ? "" : s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, function (c) { return { "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;", "'": "&#39;" }[c]; }); }
  function hex2(n) { return (n < 16 ? "0" : "") + n.toString(16).toUpperCase(); }
  function sleep(ms) { return new Promise(function (r) { setTimeout(r, ms); }); }
  function isNum(x) { return typeof x === "number" && isFinite(x); }

  /* ---------------- log ---------------- */
  var LOG_KEY = "v60-link-log", logLines = [];
  try { logLines = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LOG_KEY) || "[]"); if (!Array.isArray(logLines)) logLines = []; } catch (e) { logLines = []; }
  function showLog() { var el = $("log"); el.value = logLines.join("\n"); el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight; }
  function log(dir, text) {
    logLines.push(new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 23).replace("T", " ") + " " + dir + " " + String(text).replace(/\r/g, "\\r").replace(/\n/g, "\\n"));
    if (logLines.length > 400) logLines.shift();
    showLog();
    try { localStorage.setItem(LOG_KEY, JSON.stringify(logLines)); } catch (e) {}
  }
  if (logLines.length) { showLog(); log("..", "page loaded"); }

  /* ---------------- transports ---------------- */
  /* Full 128-bit UUIDs: Bluefy does not accept the 16-bit short forms. FFF0 is the OBDLink CX UART service (notify FFF1, write FFF2). */
  function u16(x) { return "0000" + x + "-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"; }
  var KNOWN_SERVICES = [u16("fff0"), u16("ffe0"), u16("18f0"), u16("ffe5"), "e7810a71-73ae-499d-8c15-faa9aef0c3f2"];
  function BleTransport() {
    var self = this, rx = "", waiter = null, dev = null, txChar = null, rxChar = null, useWWR = false;
    var enc = new TextEncoder(), dec = new TextDecoder();
    function onNotify(ev) {
      rx += dec.decode(ev.target.value);
      if (waiter && rx.indexOf(">") >= 0) { var out = rx.slice(0, rx.indexOf(">")); rx = rx.slice(rx.indexOf(">") + 1); var w = waiter; waiter = null; w.resolve(out); }
    }
    self.name = "";
    /* Some adapters (the OBDLink CX among them) can drop the link right after the first connection while iOS
       finishes pairing. During connecting, a drop is reported to connect() so it can retry once without the picker. */
    /* UUIDs as Bluefy and Chrome give them: any case, sometimes the short 16-bit form. Everything is compared lower-case. */
    function norm(u) { u = String(u || "").toLowerCase(); if (/^[0-9a-f]{4}$/.test(u)) u = "0000" + u + "-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"; return u; }
    function short(u) { u = norm(u); return u.slice(0, 4) === "0000" && u.slice(8) === "-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb" ? u.slice(4, 8) : u; }
    function props(c) { var p = c.properties || {}; return (p.notify ? "N" : "") + (p.indicate ? "I" : "") + (p.write ? "W" : "") + (p.writeWithoutResponse ? "w" : "") + (p.read ? "R" : ""); }
    /* Serial channels we know. Each entry: service, notify characteristic, write characteristic. The OBDLink CX is FFF0/FFF1/FFF2
       (OBDLink CX adapter notes). Its FEF5 service is firmware-update only and answers nothing; it is never picked. */
    var UARTS = [["fff0", "fff1", "fff2"], ["ffe0", "ffe1", "ffe1"], ["18f0", "2af0", "2af1"], ["ffe5", "ffe9", "ffe4"], ["e7810a71-73ae-499d-8c15-faa9aef0c3f2", "bef8d6c9-9c21-4c9e-b632-bd58c1009f9f", "bef8d6c9-9c21-4c9e-b632-bd58c1009f9f"]];
    var NEVER = { fef5: 1, "180a": 1, "1800": 1, "1801": 1, "180f": 1, "1805": 1, "fe59": 1 };
    function attach(server) {
      return server.getPrimaryServices().then(function (services) {
        var jobs = services.map(function (s) { return s.getCharacteristics().then(function (cs) { return { s: s, cs: cs }; }, function () { return { s: s, cs: [] }; }); });
        return Promise.all(jobs);
      }).then(function (groups) {
        groups.forEach(function (g) { log("..", "service " + short(g.s.uuid) + ": " + (g.cs.map(function (c) { return short(c.uuid) + "[" + props(c) + "]"; }).join(" ") || "no characteristics")); });
        var best = null;
        function find(g, id, kind) { return g.cs.filter(function (c) { var p = c.properties || {}; return short(c.uuid) === id && (kind === "n" ? (p.notify || p.indicate) : (p.write || p.writeWithoutResponse)); })[0]; }
        function anyN(g) { return g.cs.filter(function (c) { var p = c.properties || {}; return p.notify || p.indicate; })[0]; }
        function anyW(g) { return g.cs.filter(function (c) { var p = c.properties || {}; return p.write || p.writeWithoutResponse; })[0]; }
        /* 1. a known serial service, by its own characteristics */
        UARTS.forEach(function (u) {
          if (best) return;
          var g = groups.filter(function (x) { return short(x.s.uuid) === u[0]; })[0]; if (!g) return;
          var n = find(g, u[1], "n") || anyN(g), w = find(g, u[2], "w") || anyW(g);
          if (n && w) best = { n: n, w: w, how: "known service " + u[0] };
        });
        /* 2. any other service with a notify and a write characteristic, never the housekeeping ones */
        groups.forEach(function (g) {
          if (best || NEVER[short(g.s.uuid)]) return;
          var n = anyN(g), w = anyW(g);
          if (n && w) best = { n: n, w: w, how: "unlisted service " + short(g.s.uuid) };
        });
        if (!best) throw new Error("Connected, but this device does not offer a serial data channel this page recognizes. It may not be an OBD adapter, or it may be a Classic-Bluetooth model.");
        rxChar = best.n; txChar = best.w; useWWR = !best.w.properties.write && best.w.properties.writeWithoutResponse;
        log("..", "using " + best.how + ": notify " + short(rxChar.uuid) + ", write " + short(txChar.uuid) + (useWWR ? " (without response)" : ""));
        rxChar.addEventListener("characteristicvaluechanged", onNotify);
        return rxChar.startNotifications();
      }).then(function () { log("..", "notifications on (" + short(rxChar.uuid) + ")"); return sleep(350); });
    }
    /* The picker lists only adapters that are advertising, and the CX stops advertising while the phone still holds a link to it
       (Bluefy keeps one after "allow future background connections"). So first try the adapter picked last time, without the picker. */
    function remembered() {
      var name = null; try { name = localStorage.getItem("v60-link-dev"); } catch (e) {}
      if (!name || !navigator.bluetooth.getDevices) return Promise.resolve(null);
      return navigator.bluetooth.getDevices().then(function (list) { var d = (list || []).filter(function (x) { return x.name === name; })[0]; if (d) log("..", "trying " + name + " from last time, no picker"); return d || null; }, function () { return null; });
    }
    self.open = function () {
      return remembered().then(function (known) {
        if (known) return known;
        return navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({ acceptAllDevices: true, optionalServices: KNOWN_SERVICES });
      }).then(function (d) {
        dev = d; self.name = d.name || "adapter"; log("..", "picked " + self.name);
        try { if (d.name) localStorage.setItem("v60-link-dev", d.name); } catch (e) {}
        d.addEventListener("gattserverdisconnected", function () { log("!!", "the adapter dropped the Bluetooth link" + (self.lastCmd ? " (last command sent: " + self.lastCmd + ")" : "")); if (waiter) { var w = waiter; waiter = null; var de = new Error("The adapter is not connected."); de.name = "NetworkError"; w.reject(de); } if (self.connecting) { self.dropped = true; return; } if (self.onclose) self.onclose(); });
        return d.gatt.connect();
      }).then(function (server) { log("..", "GATT connected"); return attach(server); }, function (e) { try { localStorage.removeItem("v60-link-dev"); } catch (x) {} throw e; });
    };
    self.reopen = function () { self.dropped = false; return dev.gatt.connect().then(function (server) { log("..", "GATT reconnected"); return attach(server); }); };
    self.send = function (cmd, timeoutMs) {
      rx = "";
      return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {
        if (!dev || !dev.gatt.connected) { var de = new Error("The adapter is not connected."); de.name = "NetworkError"; reject(de); return; }
        var timer = setTimeout(function () { waiter = null; reject(new Error("timeout")); }, timeoutMs || 4000);
        self.lastCmd = cmd;
        waiter = { resolve: function (v) { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(v); }, reject: function (e) { clearTimeout(timer); reject(e); } };
        var bytes = enc.encode(cmd + "\r"), chunks = [];
        for (var i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 20) chunks.push(bytes.slice(i, i + 20));
        chunks.reduce(function (p, c) { return p.then(function () { return useWWR ? txChar.writeValueWithoutResponse(c) : (txChar.writeValueWithResponse ? txChar.writeValueWithResponse(c) : txChar.writeValue(c)); }); }, Promise.resolve())
          .catch(function (e) { clearTimeout(timer); waiter = null; reject(e); });
      });
    };
    self.close = function () { try { if (dev && dev.gatt.connected) dev.gatt.disconnect(); } catch (e) {} };
  }

  /* Simulated 2016 V60 T5 for learning the page without a car. CAN 11-bit, headers on. */
  function SimTransport() {
    var self = this, t0 = Date.now(), headers = false, engineOn = true, cleared = false;
    var stored = ["0171"], pending = ["0420"], permanent = ["0171"];
    self.name = "Simulated V60";
    self.engine = function (on) { engineOn = on; };
    function sec() { return (Date.now() - t0) / 1000; }
    function frame(hdr, bytes) {
      var out = [];
      if (bytes.length <= 7) out.push([bytes.length].concat(bytes));
      else {
        out.push([0x10 | (bytes.length >> 8), bytes.length & 255].concat(bytes.slice(0, 6)));
        for (var i = 6, sn = 1; i < bytes.length; i += 7, sn++) out.push([0x20 | (sn & 15)].concat(bytes.slice(i, i + 7)));
      }
      return out.map(function (f) { while (f.length < 8) f.push(0); return (headers ? hdr + " " : "") + f.map(hex2).join(" "); }).join("\r");
    }
    function dtcBytes(list) { var b = []; list.forEach(function (c) { var v = parseInt(c, 16); b.push(v >> 8, v & 255); }); return b; }
    function val(pid) {
      var s = sec(), warm = Math.min(1, s / 300), spd = engineOn ? Math.max(0, 50 + 30 * Math.sin(s / 25)) : 0, rpm = engineOn ? (spd < 1 ? 760 : 1400 + spd * 18) : 0;
      switch (pid) {
        case 0x04: return [Math.round((engineOn ? 25 + spd / 4 : 0) * 2.55)];
        case 0x05: return [Math.round(30 + 58 * warm + 40)];
        case 0x06: return [Math.round(128 + (Math.random() * 6 - 3) * 1.28)];
        case 0x07: return [Math.round(128 + 6.3 * 1.28)];
        case 0x0B: return [Math.round(engineOn ? 35 + spd * 0.8 : 99)];
        case 0x0C: var r = Math.round(rpm * 4); return [r >> 8, r & 255];
        case 0x0D: return [Math.round(spd)];
        case 0x0F: return [40 + 31];
        case 0x10: var m = Math.round((engineOn ? 3 + spd / 4 : 0) * 100); return [m >> 8, m & 255];
        case 0x11: return [Math.round((engineOn ? 14 + spd / 5 : 0) * 2.55)];
        case 0x2F: return [Math.round(0.62 * 255)];
        case 0x33: return [99];
        case 0x42: var v = Math.round((engineOn ? 14.1 + Math.random() * 0.1 : 12.5) * 1000); return [v >> 8, v & 255];
        case 0x46: return [40 + 29];
        case 0x5C: return [Math.round(40 + 25 + 70 * warm)];
        case 0x01: var a = (cleared ? 0 : 0x80) | (cleared ? 0 : stored.length); var b = 0x07 | (cleared ? 0x00 : 0x00); var c = 0x01 | 0x04 | 0x20 | 0x40 | 0x80; var d = cleared ? (0x01 | 0x04 | 0x20 | 0x40 | 0x80) : 0x04; return [a, b, c, d];
        case 0x21: return cleared ? [0, 0] : [0, 85];
        case 0x30: return [cleared ? 0 : 12];
        case 0x31: return cleared ? [0, 0] : [1, 44];
        case 0x4E: return cleared ? [0, 0] : [3, 200];
      }
      return null;
    }
    var SUP = [0x01, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x11, 0x1F, 0x20, 0x21, 0x2F, 0x30, 0x31, 0x33, 0x40, 0x42, 0x46, 0x4E, 0x5C];
    function supMask(base) { var m = [0, 0, 0, 0]; SUP.forEach(function (p) { if (p > base && p <= base + 32) { var i = p - base - 1; m[i >> 3] |= 0x80 >> (i & 7); } }); return m; }
    self.open = function () { return sleep(400); };
    self.close = function () {};
    self.send = function (cmd) {
      var c = cmd.replace(/\s/g, "").toUpperCase(), out;
      if (/^AT/.test(c)) {
        if (c === "ATZ" || c === "ATI") out = "ELM327 v1.5";
        else if (c === "ATDPN") out = "A6";
        else if (c === "ATRV") out = engineOn ? "14.1V" : "12.5V";
        else { if (c === "ATH1") headers = true; if (c === "ATH0") headers = false; out = "OK"; }
      } else if (/^01(00|20|40)$/.test(c)) { var base = parseInt(c.slice(2), 16); out = frame("7E8", [0x41, base].concat(supMask(base))) + (base === 0 ? "\r" + frame("7E9", [0x41, 0, 0x80, 0, 0, 0]) : ""); }
      else if (/^01[0-9A-F]{2}$/.test(c)) { var pid = parseInt(c.slice(2), 16), v = val(pid); out = v ? frame("7E8", [0x41, pid].concat(v)) : "NO DATA"; }
      else if (c === "03") out = frame("7E8", [0x43, cleared ? 0 : stored.length].concat(cleared ? [] : dtcBytes(stored))) + "\r" + frame("7E9", [0x43, 0]);
      else if (c === "07") out = frame("7E8", [0x47, cleared ? 0 : pending.length].concat(cleared ? [] : dtcBytes(pending))) + "\r" + frame("7E9", cleared ? [0x47, 0] : [0x47, 1].concat(dtcBytes(["0700"])));
      else if (c === "0A") out = frame("7E8", [0x4A, permanent.length].concat(dtcBytes(permanent)));
      else if (c === "0902") { var vin = "YV1612FH0G0000000"; out = frame("7E8", [0x49, 0x02, 0x01].concat(vin.split("").map(function (ch) { return ch.charCodeAt(0); }))); }
      else if (c === "020200") out = cleared ? frame("7E8", [0x42, 0x02, 0x00, 0, 0]) : frame("7E8", [0x42, 0x02, 0x00, 0x01, 0x71]);
      else if (/^02[0-9A-F]{2}00$/.test(c)) { var fp = parseInt(c.slice(2, 4), 16), fv = { 0x04: [80], 0x05: [128], 0x06: [150], 0x07: [137], 0x0B: [40], 0x0C: [0x0B, 0xE0], 0x0D: [0], 0x11: [36] }[fp]; out = (!cleared && fv) ? frame("7E8", [0x42, fp, 0x00].concat(fv)) : "NO DATA"; }
      else if (c === "04") { if (engineOn) out = frame("7E8", [0x7F, 0x04, 0x22]); else { cleared = true; stored = []; pending = []; out = frame("7E8", [0x44]) + "\r" + frame("7E9", [0x44]); } }
      else out = "?";
      return sleep(25 + Math.random() * 25).then(function () { return out + "\r\r"; });
    };
  }

  /* ---------------- ELM327 + ISO-TP parsing ---------------- */
  var link = null, busy = Promise.resolve(), protoCAN = true;
  function cmd(c, timeout) {
    var p = busy.then(function () {
      if (!link) throw new Error("Not connected");
      log(">", c);
      return link.send(c, timeout).then(function (r) { log("<", r.trim()); return r; });
    });
    busy = p.catch(function () {});
    return p;
  }
  var ERR_RE = /NO DATA|UNABLE TO CONNECT|CAN ERROR|BUS ERROR|BUS BUSY|STOPPED|ERROR|FB ERROR|DATA ERROR|^\?$/i;
  function parseResponse(raw) {
    var lines = String(raw).split(/[\r\n]+/).map(function (l) { return l.trim(); }).filter(function (l) { return l && !/^(SEARCHING|BUS INIT|>|OK$)/i.test(l); });
    var ecus = {}, partial = {}, errors = [];
    lines.forEach(function (l) {
      if (ERR_RE.test(l)) { errors.push(l); return; }
      l = l.replace(/^[0-9A-F]:\s*/i, "");
      var tok = l.split(/\s+/), hdr, bytes;
      if (/^[0-9A-F]{3}$/i.test(tok[0])) { hdr = tok[0].toUpperCase(); bytes = tok.slice(1); }

  function runScan() {

    s.push(stored + pend ? [stored ? "bad" : "watch", stored + " stored and " + pend + " pending code" + (stored + pend === 1 ? "" : "s"), "Pending means seen once but not confirmed. It may set the light if it repeats."] : ["ok", "No stored or pending codes", ""]);

["watch", notReady + " of " + R.monitors.length + " readiness monitors not ready", "Normal for a few days after codes are cleared or the battery is disconnected. Mixed driving completes them."] : ["ok", "All " + R.monitors.length + " readiness monitors are ready", ""]);

" : "") + (notReady > 1 ? notReady + " monitors are not ready, and federal rules allow at most one on a 2001 or newer car. " : "") + "Fix the cause, then drive normally until the monitors finish before testing."] : ["ok", "Emissions inspection: readiness looks passable", "No light, and " + (notReady ? "only one monitor" : "no monitors") + " not ready (the federal limit for 2001 and newer cars is one). This is a readiness check, not a full test."]);

  /* ---------------- export helpers ---------------- */
  function fileFor(name, text, type) { return new File([text], name, { type: type }); }
  function download(name, text, type) {
    if (window.V60_FILE) { window.V60_FILE.save(name, text, type).catch(function () {}); return; }
    var url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([text], { type: type })), a = document.createElement("a");

  function canShareFiles() { try { return !!(navigator.canShare && navigator.canShare({ files: [fileFor("x.txt", "x", "text/plain")] })); } catch (e) { return false; } }
  /* Bluefy's share sheet has delivered only the file name, not the file. Pass the content as text too, so the receiving app gets it either way. */
  function share(name, text, type) {
    var data = { title: name, text: text };
    if (canShareFiles()) data.files = [fileFor(name, text, type)];
    return navigator.share(data);
  }
