The 10 to 15 minutes above 20 mph figure comes from Volvo's support page, not the manual.",
```javascript
      "## If it keeps coming back",
      "Volvo bulletin TJ29818 covers false warnings on indirect-system cars: a body module software update, recalibrating at least every 10,000 miles, and checking the wheel-hub encoder rings for metal debris. A light that flashes for about a minute and then stays on, with 'Tire press. syst Service required', means a system fault for a shop."],
    src: ["tpms", "tsb29818", "vpic"] },
  { id: "a-belt", cat: "Maintenance", t: "Timing belt: why it is your biggest unknown", tags: "timing belt cambelt interference water pump tensioner cost due",
    body: ["The timing belt keeps the crankshaft and camshafts in step. Your engine is an interference design, so if the belt breaks, valves and pistons collide and the engine is usually destroyed.",
      "## When",
      "Volvo's 2016 US schedule lists the timing belt tensioner and idler pulley at 150,000 miles or 10 years. Independent sources replace the belt with them as a kit. Some UK owners report a later reduction to 90,000 miles. Rubber ages with time as well as miles, and your car reaches 10 years in 2026.",
      "## Your situation",
      "The car was bought as-is with no history, so there is no proof it was ever done. Look for a shop sticker under the hood, check old receipts, and ask any Volvo dealer to look up service history by VIN.",
      "## Cost",
      "RepairPal's range for a 2016 V60 is about $740 to $990 for the belt alone. A full kit with tensioner and idler, and possibly the water pump, costs more, and dealer quotes run far higher. Get two quotes from Volvo specialists."],
    src: ["ms", "acr", "repairpal"] },
  { id: "a-complaints", cat: "Known issues", t: "What actually goes wrong: owner complaints to NHTSA", tags: "complaints problems issues common failures nhtsa oil sunroof start stop",
    body: ["NHTSA had 21 owner complaints for the 2015 V60, 14 for the 2016 and 6 for the 2017 when checked in October 2026. Small numbers, so treat this as signals, not statistics.",
      "## Patterns",
      "- Oil consumption (2015 and 2016, the most common by far): owners adding a quart every few hundred to a thousand miles, dealers pointing to piston rings, partial repair coverage, and one report of an oil-fouled spark plug.",
      "- Sunroof glass shattering at highway speed (three reports across 2016 and 2017).",
      "- Engine start/stop: stalling or not restarting cleanly at a stop on early cars. A 2015 recall (R39574) fitted a stronger starter fuse on some.",
      "- Infotainment screen stuck rebooting, taking climate and settings controls with it.",
      "- Brake control module failure at about 55,000 miles on one 2016, with stability and collision-avoidance warnings.",
      "- Transmission shove or power cut between first and second gear (2017 reports).",
      "- Door latch problems, including after the door latch recall repair.",
      "## What to do with this",
      "Oil level checks are the single most valuable habit on your car. Know the sound of a healthy start/stop restart. If the screen ever boot-loops, a software update is the usual first fix."],
    src: [["NHTSA complaints API, 2015 to 2017 Volvo V60", "https://api.nhtsa.gov/complaints/complaintsByVehicle?make=volvo&model=v60&modelYear=2016"]] },
  { id: "a-recalls", cat: "Known issues", t: "Recalls on 2016 V60s", tags: "recall seat belt door latch starter fuse buckle",
    body: ["Four safety recalls cover 2016 V60s. Each covers a range of cars, so some may not apply to yours or may already be done. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or call Volvo at 1-800-458-1552. Repairs are free at any Volvo dealer.",
      "- Front seat belt anchor cable (Volvo R10029): the steel cable can fatigue. Both front seats get new cables.",
      "- Door latches (R89978): a latch part can break, so a door seems closed but is not latched. All four latches are replaced.",
      "- Front passenger seat belt buckle stud (R89708): cars built February 2015 to August 2016.",
      "- Starter motor fuse for start/stop (R39574): cars built April to August 2015."],
    src: ["nhtsa"] },
  { id: "a-inspect", cat: "Ownership", t: "Emissions inspection in Travis County", tags: "inspection emissions texas travis readiness monitors registration pass fail",
    body: ["Texas ended safety inspections for personal cars on January 1, 2025, and you now pay a $7.50 inspection program fee at registration. Travis County still requires an emissions test, which reads the car's computer through the OBD port.",
      "## What makes a 2016 fail",
      "- A lit check-engine light with a stored code.",
      "- More than one readiness monitor not ready. Clearing codes or disconnecting the battery resets them all.",
      "## Getting monitors ready",
      "Drive normally over a few days: cold starts, some stop-and-go up to about 30 mph, and 5 to 7 minutes at a steady 55 mph. Some evaporative tests need the car to sit about 8 hours first. Check readiness with V60 Link before you go."],
    src: ["dps", "cfr"] },
  { id: "a-obd", cat: "Diagnostics", t: "Talking to your car: adapters, apps and limits", tags: "obd adapter obdlink cx car scanner bluefy v60 link codes live data",
    body: ["Every US car since 1996 has an OBD-II port. Yours is under the dash on the driver's side.",
      "## What a phone adapter can do",
      "Read and clear engine and emissions codes, show the freeze frame and readiness monitors, record live data like fuel trims, coolant temperature and voltage, and log drives.",
      "## What it cannot do",
      "Reach the airbag, ABS, climate and body modules, which use Volvo's own diagnostics. That needs Volvo VIDA with a DiCE interface on a Windows 11 Pro PC, or a Volvo specialist.",
      "## The setup for an iPhone",
      "- OBDLink CX (Bluetooth LE, about $80) works with V60 Link in the Bluefy browser, Car Scanner and OBDLink's own app.",
      "- Classic-Bluetooth adapters do not work on iPhone at all.",
      "- Safari has no web Bluetooth; use Bluefy for the Live tab."],
    src: ["cx", "vida"] },
  { id: "a-schedule", cat: "Maintenance", t: "Volvo's maintenance schedule for your engine", tags: "schedule service intervals maintenance plan when",
    body: ["From Volvo's 2016 US/Canada maintenance schedule, engine code 40 (your B4204T11).",
      "- Every 10,000 miles or 12 months: oil and filter, reset the service reminder, check fluids, brakes, tires, wipers, lights and belts.",
      "- Every 20,000 miles: add the cabin air filter (at least yearly), headlight aim, a leak check and tire pressures.",
      "- 40k, 80k, 120k miles: add the engine air filter, brake fluid replacement (or every 3 years), and checks of suspension, CV boots and brake hoses.",
      "- 60k and 120k miles: spark plugs.",
      "- 150k miles or 10 years: accessory belt with tensioner and idler, plus the timing belt tensioner and idler.",
      "- Transmission fluid: level check at 50k, 100k and 150k only if leaking. No routine change in normal use."],
    src: ["ms"] },
  { id: "a-drivee", cat: "How it works", t: "How your Drive-E engine works", tags: "drive-e engine turbo direct injection how works vea",
    body: ["Drive-E (Volvo Engine Architecture, VEA) is the family of 2.0 liter four-cylinders Volvo introduced around 2015 to replace its five- and six-cylinder engines.",
      "## The path from air to power",
      "- Air comes through the air filter box and the mass-airflow sensor, which measures it.",
      "- The turbocharger, spun by exhaust gas, compresses it.",
      "- An intercooler cools the compressed air so it is denser.",
      "- The throttle meters it into the intake manifold and cylinders.",
      "- Fuel is injected directly into each cylinder at high pressure, the spark plug fires, and the exhaust spins the turbo again.",
      "## Why that matters to you",
      "Small turbo engines make big torque low down: all 258 lb-ft from 1,500 rpm. They are sensitive to oil quality and level, to boost leaks in the pipes between turbo and engine, and to ignition health, because cylinder pressures are high. The timing belt drives the camshafts.",
      "Your T5 is turbocharged only. The more powerful T6 version adds a supercharger."],
    src: ["acr", "om"] },
  { id: "a-tpmshow", cat: "How it works", t: "How the indirect tire monitor works", tags: "abs wheel speed sensor tire monitor how",
    body: ["Each wheel has an ABS speed sensor that reads a toothed or magnetic ring on the hub. A tire with low pressure has a slightly smaller rolling radius, so it turns a little faster than the others at the same road speed. The car compares all four, together with how the tires vibrate, against the reference it learned at the last calibration.",
      "That is why calibration matters: the car only knows 'different from before', not an absolute pressure. It is also why metal debris on an encoder ring, or one new tire among old ones, can trigger false warnings."],
    src: ["tpms", "tsb29818"] },
  { id: "a-vida", cat: "Diagnostics", t: "Volvo's own diagnostic system (VIDA)", tags: "vida dice volvo software update module scan",
    body: ["VIDA is Volvo's dealer diagnostic and service information system. Owners in the US and Canada can buy short subscriptions with a North American VIN.",
      "- Service information only (procedures, torque specs, wiring): about $21 for 3 days. No interface needed.",
      "- Diagnostics: about $48 for 3 days, plus a Volvo DiCE interface (about $500 genuine) and a Windows 11 Pro PC with an Intel i5 from late 2017 or newer and 16 GB RAM.",
      "- Software downloads: about $73 for 3 days, plus each software item bought separately.",
      "For a one-off problem, an independent Volvo specialist who already owns VIDA is almost always cheaper. The service-information tier is the cheapest way to get exact procedures and torque specs for your VIN; record what you find under Verified data."],
    src: ["vida"] },
  { id: "a-lights", cat: "How it works", t: "Warning lights and what to do", tags: "warning lights symbols dashboard red yellow messages",
    body: ["Color tells you urgency. Red: stop safely and find out why. Yellow or amber: get it checked soon. Green and blue: information.",
      "## Red, from Volvo's manual",
      "- Oil pressure: stop, switch off, check oil. If the level is fine and the light stays on after restart, tow it.",
      "- Brake system: fluid may be low. If below MIN, do not drive. If it is on together with ABS, stop and restart; if both stay on with fluid OK, drive carefully to a shop.",
      "- Charging (generator): the battery is not being charged. Get to a Volvo workshop.",
      "- Airbag (SRS): on while driving, or more than about 10 seconds after start, means a fault.",
      "- Red triangle: stop in a safe place and read the message.",
      "- 'High engine temp, Stop engine' or 'Coolant level low, Stop safely': stop and let it cool before checking.",
      "## Yellow",
      "- Check engine: get codes read soon. A loose fuel cap or refueling with the engine running can trigger it.",
      "- ABS: stop, switch off, restart. If it stays on, normal brakes still work; drive to a shop.",
      "- Tire pressure: check pressures, then calibrate (see the tire monitor article).",
      "- Turn signal flashing fast: a bulb or circuit fault.",
      "## Text messages",
      "- 'Stop engine' or 'Stop safely': serious risk of damage.",
      "- 'Service urgent': now. 'Service required': as soon as possible.",
      "- 'Oil service required': the oil level may be too high.",
      "- 'Low battery, Power save mode': the audio switched off to save current; charge the battery."],
    src: ["om"] },
  { id: "a-startstop", cat: "How it works", t: "Start/stop: when it stops, when it won't, and why", tags: "start stop auto stop battery agm restart",
    body: ["Start/stop shuts the engine off when you stop and restarts it when you lift off the brake. That is why your car has an AGM main battery, a small support battery and a heavier-duty starter.",
      "## It may not stop the engine when",
      "- You have not driven above about 5 mph since the last start.",
      "- The engine or transmission is not warm, or it is below about 25 F or above about 85 F outside.",
      "- Battery charge is low, the blower is on high, or climate cannot hold the setting.",
      "- You are reversing, steering hard, on a steep incline, or the selector is in S or manual.",
      "## It may restart on its own when",
      "Windows fog, the climate needs it, battery charge drops, you pump the brake, the hood is opened, the car starts rolling, or you turn the wheel.",
      "## Off switch",
      "Press the Start/Stop button on the center console; the light goes out until the next engine start.",
      "## Safety",
      "Never open the hood while the engine is auto-stopped. It can restart without warning."],
    src: ["om"] },
  { id: "a-tirekit", cat: "Tires", t: "Flat tire: sealing kit, spare and changing a wheel", tags: "flat tire repair kit sealant spare jack change wheel",
    body: ["Your car most likely carries Volvo's Tire Sealing System under the cargo floor, because the temporary spare was an accessory. Check now so you know before you need it.",
      "## Sealing kit, in short",
      "- Stick the speed-limit label on the steering wheel. Screw the sealant bottle into the compressor; it cannot be removed after.",
      "- Connect the hose to the valve, plug into the 12 V socket, start the engine, switch the compressor on.",
      "- Within 7 minutes reach 22 to 44 psi. If it will not reach 22 psi, the hole is too big: do not drive.",
      "- Drive about 2 miles at up to 50 mph, then recheck. After that: max 50 mph and about 120 miles to a tire shop.",
      "- Tread punctures only, not sidewalls. Leave the nail in.",
      "## Changing a wheel",
      "- Parking brake on, P selected, wheels blocked. Loosen the bolts half a turn while the car is still on the ground.",
      "- Use the jack only at the jack points, on firm level ground, and never put any part of your body under the car.",
      "- Tighten crosswise to 103 lb-ft once lowered. The temporary spare takes 60 psi."],
    src: ["om"] },
  { id: "a-fuses", cat: "How it works", t: "Fuses: where they are and which you may change", tags: "fuse box location replace amp",
    body: ["Your car has fuse boxes in the engine bay, under the glove compartment, under the cargo floor, and a start/stop cold-zone box in the engine bay.",
      "- The fuse puller is on the underside of the engine bay fuse box cover.",
      "- Pull the fuse straight out and look at the wire from the side. A broken wire means blown. Replace with the same color and amperage, never higher, never metal.",
      "- Engine bay: positions 16 to 33 and 35 to 41 are owner-changeable; 1 to 15, 34 and 42 to 44 are relays or breakers for a technician.",
      "- A fuse that keeps blowing means a fault to find, not a fuse to upsize."],
    src: ["om"] },
  { id: "a-wash", cat: "Ownership", t: "Washing and paint care, Volvo's way", tags: "wash car paint wax polish care detailing",
    body: ["- Wash out of direct sun with lukewarm water and a soft sponge. Remove bird droppings quickly; they etch paint in Texas heat.",
      "- Pressure washer no closer than about 12 inches, and not at the locks.",
      "- Turn off the rain sensor before an automatic wash, and brake gently afterward to dry the brakes.",
      "- Polish or wax only when the paint is below 113 F and not in sun.",
      "- Volvo advises against long-life paint coatings, which it says can soften or cloud the clear coat.",
      "- Your paint code is on the label on the B-pillar."],
    src: ["om"] },
  { id: "a-polestar", cat: "Upgrades", t: "Polestar Performance Optimization", tags: "polestar tune performance power upgrade",
    body: ["Volvo's Polestar division made a software optimization for exactly your car: the 2016 V60 T5 Drive-E FWD automatic.",
      "- Peak power 242 to 250 hp; mid-range power 197 to 218 hp.",
      "- Torque 258 to 295 lb-ft.",
      "- 0-60 mph 6.4 to 6.3 seconds.",
      "- Dealer-installed in about an hour. Volvo stated it keeps certified emissions and does not affect the factory warranty or service intervals.",
      "Whether US dealers still sell it in 2026, and the price, are unconfirmed. Ask a dealer for article number 31459463. Aftermarket engine tunes are a different matter: changing calibration is treated as emissions tampering under the Clean Air Act, and Travis County still tests emissions."],
    src: ["polestar"] },
  { id: "a-shops", cat: "Ownership", t: "Volvo-capable shops in Austin", tags: "shop mechanic austin independent dealer repair service where volvo specialist vida",
    body: ["Ratings and phone numbers are Google data from October 10, 2026. None of the independent shops' websites say whether they have Volvo's own diagnostic system (VIDA), so ask when you call. Dealers have it, and Volvo programs like the oil consumption warranty require an authorized retailer.",
      "## Volvo or Swedish specialists",
      "- Swedish Auto Service, 11008 N Lamar Blvd, 512-836-0022. Swedish cars since 1993, also other European makes and body work. 4.8 stars from 355 reviews.",
      "- Capital V Connection, 1134 Airport Blvd, 512-441-1334. Volvo-focused; the site mentions diagnostics and software updates. 4.7 from 73.",
      "- Austin Vol-Tech, 1707 Bench Mark Dr, 512-251-4107. Volvo and VW. 4.5 from 78.",
      "## European generalists",
      "- Northwest Imports, 13200 Pond Springs Rd C5. The site lists 512-331-7372, Google lists 512-601-8246. ASE-certified. 4.9 from 563.",
      "- European Motorwerks, 9234 Burnet Rd, 512-508-8966. 4.7 from 628.",
      "- Euro Garage, 10921 E Crystal Falls Pkwy G-400, Leander, 512-528-4684. 4.9 from 405.",
      "## Dealers",
      "- Volvo Cars of Austin, 7216 N IH-35. Service 737-299-7339. Service department 4.1 from 76 reviews.",
      "- Volvo Cars Hill Country, 10600 N FM 620. 737-380-0773. Service department 3.2 from 11 reviews.",
      "## What to ask on the first call",
      "- Do you have VIDA, or another tool that reads all Volvo modules, not just the engine?",
      "- Can you inspect the timing belt and tell me whether it has been replaced?",
      "- What oil do you use? (Volvo specifies Castrol Edge Professional V 0W-20 or ACEA A5/B5 5W-30.)",
      "- Bring the shop note from the Bulletins tab if you marked any bulletins."],
    src: [["Swedish Auto Service", "https://swedishautoservice.com/about-us/"], ["Capital V Connection", "https://www.capitalvconnection.com/"], ["Northwest Imports", "https://nwimports.com/"]] },
  { id: "a-ase", cat: "Ownership", t: "ASE certification: what the sign on the shop means, and the tests", tags: "ase certification certified technician mechanic g1 master test exam cost fee study guide credential automotive service excellence",
    body: ["ASE (the National Institute for Automotive Service Excellence) runs the voluntary certification program for US repair technicians. It is a certification, not a license: no law requires it. Certification takes a passed test plus matching hands-on work experience, and each credential lasts five years. Prices below are from ASE's fee page, checked October 15, 2026.",
      "## The tiers",
      "- Entry-Level: for students in training programs. No experience needed, valid two years. Usually given through a school, not bought directly.",
      "- Professional: single tests across more than 50 subjects. The A1–A9 car series, G1 Maintenance and Light Repair, C1 Service Consultant, the B collision series (B6 is damage estimating) and the P parts series.",
      "- Master: hold every test in a series. Master Automobile Technician means A1 through A8.",
      "- Advanced Level (L1–L4): specialist diagnosis (engine performance, diesel, hybrid and EV, driver-assist systems). The related certifications come first.",
      "## What it costs",
      "- $34 registration per order, plus $62 per standard test or $124 per Advanced Level test. Texas adds sales tax.",
      "- One G1 test in one order: $96. A1–A8 in one order: $530.",
      "- After buying, you have 90 days to schedule and sit the test. New tests are taken in person at a Prometric center; remote online testing is for recertification only.",
      "- Untaken tests cancelled within 90 days of purchase are refunded.",
      "- Recertifying costs the same per test, capped at $186 in test fees per order ($220 with registration). A1–A9 holders can instead keep current with ASE's Renewal App at $52 a year.",
      "## The experience rule",
      "- Accepted experience: repair technician (1 to 3 years, depending on the test), parts specialist, collision damage estimator, or service consultant (2 years each). It has to match the test: shop work does not count toward C1, B6 or the parts tests.",
      "- Some formal training can substitute for part of the experience.",
      "- You can sit a test before you have the experience. You get a score report, but no certificate until the experience requirement is met.",
      "- ASE says it may credit other experience at its own judgment.",
      "## G1 maps onto this car",
      "G1 is the broad entry test: 55 scored questions (plus 10 unscored ones you can't tell apart) in 90 minutes. ASE publishes a study guide on the test's page. Its seven areas line up with items in this manual:",
      "- Engine systems: 1 Engine bay, 1.1 Oil through 1.9 Spark plugs & coils.",
      "- Automatic transmissions: 4.4 Transmission & driveline (the Aisin 8-speed).",
      "- Manual drivetrains and axles: the axles in 4.4. Your car has no manual gearbox, so the clutch and gearbox parts of this area have nothing to look at on it.",
      "- Suspension and steering: 4.3 Suspension & steering.",
      "- Brakes: 2.3 Brake pads & rotors, 2.4 Parking brake, 1.6 Brake fluid.",
      "- Electrical: 1.3 Battery, 1.8 Fuses, 5.1 Headlights & bulbs, 3.1 Driver display & warning lights.",
      "- Heating and air conditioning: 1.2 Coolant & cooling, which also carries the A/C refrigerant label from under the hood.",
      "## On a shop",
      "- A shop advertising ASE certification doesn't say which areas its techs hold or whether they know Volvos. Ask which certifications the tech working on your car holds, and whether the shop has Volvo's VIDA (see Volvo-capable shops in Austin)."],
    src: [["ASE: register now, dates and fees", "https://ase.com/tests/register-now/"], ["ASE: work experience requirements", "https://ase.com/tests/work-experience/"], ["ASE: G1 Auto Maintenance and Light Repair test", "https://ase.com/?p=2669"], ["ASE Education Foundation: Entry-Level FAQ", "https://www.aseeducationfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/FAQs.pdf"]] },
  { id: "a-tsb", cat: "Known issues", t: "Volvo's service bulletins for your car, in plain words", tags: "tsb bulletin technical service bulletin known problems dealer fix tj29818 tj31216 piston rings thermostat",
    body: ["A technical service bulletin (TSB) is Volvo telling its dealers how to fix a known problem. It is not a recall: the dealer applies it when you bring the symptom in, and you pay unless a warranty or special program covers it. NHTSA publishes the PDFs, which is where these come from. The Bulletins tab checks each one against your build date.",
      "## The ones that matter most for your car",
      "- TJ29818: false tire pressure warnings. Calibrate, match tires within 5% circumference, recalibrate every 10,000 miles, then check the hub encoder rings for metal debris. Your always-on light is exactly this territory.",
      "- TJ31216: low oil message from worn piston rings on Drive-E engines built from late 2013 to January 2016. The fix is new pistons and rings.",
      "- TJ29131: oil leaking from the cam pulley plugs, which can soak the timing belt. Covers your engine built through mid-August 2016.",
      "- TJ30268: thermostat codes (P0597–P0599 and others) on engines built through early May 2016. Replace the thermostat.",
      "- Service action S29842: spark plugs that could crack, replaced free on 2015–16 four-cylinder cars. A dealer can check by VIN whether yours was done.",
      "- SMB 00-035: the 2022 3G shutdown killed Volvo On Call and the connected apps on 2015–17 V60s unless a new 4G modem was fitted.",
      "## Bulletins that people online mention but that do not apply",
      "- TJ34588 (oil consumption) is for the five-cylinder engine.",
      "- TJ32169, TJ33901 and TJ29078 (shift quality) are for the older 6-speed. Yours is the 8-speed TG-81SC.",
      "## Decoding a bulletin",
      "In Volvo's tables your engine (B4204T11) is engine code 40 and the V60 is vehicle type 155. Ranges are written as production weeks, for example 201604 means week 4 of 2016."],
    src: [["NHTSA: TJ29818", "https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2019/MC-10165233-9999.pdf"], ["NHTSA: TJ31216 rev 5", "https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2019/MC-10169029-9999.pdf"], ["NHTSA: TJ36858 (engine and type codes)", "https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2024/MC-11006558-0001.pdf"]] },
  { id: "a-oilprogram", cat: "Known issues", t: "The oil consumption warranty and lawsuit", tags: "oil consumption warranty extended p10186 p10207 class action buchanan settlement piston rings program",
    body: ["In January 2023 Volvo began mailing owners about an extended warranty for oil consumption on Drive-E four-cylinder engines (and some five-cylinders), about 78,000 vehicles in total.",
      "## Terms",
      "- 2015–16 V60s with engine codes 26, 40 or 49 and chassis numbers 0185883 to 0326049. Engines from serial 1501327 already had updated pistons.",
      "- 8 years from first delivery or 100,000 miles, whichever comes first. Original engine only, authorized Volvo retailer only.",
      "- The test: a free oil change, the system sealed with tamper tape, then a return after 620 to 1,240 miles or when the low oil light comes on.",
      "- If use is excessive: no cylinder scratches means new pistons and rings; scratches mean an engine replacement with Volvo's approval.",
      "## Does it still cover your car?",
      "Almost certainly not. A 2016 delivered new in 2015 or 2016 passed the 8-year limit in 2023 or 2024, even though your mileage would still qualify. It would only be live if the first delivery was in October 2018 or later. A dealer can check in Warranty Vehicle Inquiry. If you enter your VIN in Glovebox, the Bulletins tab checks the chassis range.",
      "## The lawsuit",
      "Buchanan v. Volvo Car USA, in federal court in New Jersey, covered 2013–16 2.0-liter four-cylinder and 2.5-liter five-cylinder engines. It ended in a confidential settlement.",
      "## What it means for you now",
      "The repair is on you if your engine burns oil, so evidence matters: log every top-up with the mileage in the Oil watch log. That log also tells a buyer or a shop exactly where the engine stands."],
    src: [["Volvo P10186 (Aug 2023)", "https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2023/MC-10242508-9999.pdf"], ["Volvo P10207", "https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2023/MC-10231933-9999.pdf"], ["Berger Montague: Buchanan v. Volvo", "https://bergermontague.com/cases/buchanan-et-al-v-volvo-car-usa-llc-et-al"]] },
  { id: "a-trans", cat: "How it works", t: "Your 8-speed automatic (Aisin TG-81SC)", tags: "transmission gearbox 8 speed aisin tg-81sc tg81sc gears shift ratios automatic",
    body: ["Volvo co-developed the gearbox with Aisin AW. Transmission Digest describes it as the world's first transverse front-wheel-drive 8-speed. It replaced the 6-speed TF-80SC that earlier V60s used, which is why many online shift-quality fixes do not apply to your car.",
      "## Why eight gears",
      "More ratios keep the engine nearer its most efficient speed: short low gears for pulling away, tall top gears so the engine turns slowly on the highway.",
      "## Ratios",
      "Transmission Digest lists 5.250, 3.029, 1.950, 1.457, 1.221, 1.000, 0.809, 0.673, reverse 4.015, with a 3.075 or 3.200 final drive. It also lists a second set, and which one Volvo uses is not confirmed.",
      "## Living with it",
      "- Overboost: Volvo's press releases say the engine briefly allows extra torque (280 or 285 lb-ft, the two releases disagree) for 10 seconds at full throttle in gears 2 to 8.",
      "- Sport (S) or manual shifting disables start/stop.",
      "- No NHTSA bulletin for TG-81SC shift quality turned up in October 2026 research."],
    src: [["Transmission Digest on the TG-81SC", "https://www.transmissiondigest.com/?p=27645"], ["Volvo Drive-E press release, 2014", "https://mb.cision.com/Main/23620/4197159/3563897.pdf"], ["Volvo 2016 V60 overview", "https://mb.cision.com/Main/23622/4196524/3563289.pdf"]] },
  { id: "a-txhistory", cat: "Your car", t: "The paper trail: five Texas inspections, 2015 to 2026", tags: "history inspection mileage odometer mytxcar tceq previous owner houston austin p0455 emissions readiness",
    body: ["Texas keeps every state inspection on file at MyTxCar.org (TCEQ). Looked up on 2026-10-14, your car has five. VIN and plates are left out here on purpose.",
      "## The record",
      "- 2015-12-03, Roger Beasley Volvo, Austin. New-car safety check, 5 miles. Passed. So the car was sold new in Austin.",
      "- 2018-09-10, Sames Quick Service. Emissions and safety at 37,000 miles. Passed, all monitors complete, no codes, fuel cap passed.",
      "- 2019-09-18, Volvo Cars West Houston. Emissions and safety at 45,122 miles, listed with no plate, which usually means dealer stock. Passed, no codes.",
      "- 2025-06-20, Lams Austin Autos. Emissions only at 84,574 miles, no plate: the lot's test before sale. Passed, no codes.",
      "- 2026-05-16, Jiffy Lube, Austin. Emissions only at 89,617 miles. Passed with the light off, but code P0455 (large evaporative leak, usually the fuel cap) was on file.",
      "## What it tells you",
      "- Mileage ran about 12,000 a year to 2018, then slowed: 39,000 miles in the six years from 2019 to 2025, with no Texas inspection at all in that gap. The car was most likely registered elsewhere or parked for part of it.",
      "- Every emissions test passed with all readiness monitors complete and the light off. Nothing here suggests the computer was cleared just before a test.",
      "- Your Live link report of 2026-10-14 says codes were last cleared about 6,700 miles ago. With 91,357 on the cluster that day, that is about 84,650 miles: right after the lot's test and at the sale, so the lot most likely cleared the computer before handing it over. Trip T2 on the cluster, 6,803 miles, is the distance you have driven it.",
      "- The next emissions test is due with the May 2027 registration renewal. A lit check-engine light fails it, so P0171 needs to be resolved before then, not this week.",
      "- The 2025 entry lists the engine as a 2.5 five-cylinder. That is a typing mistake at the station; every other entry and your hood label say 2.0, four cylinders."],
    src: ["txcar", "dps"] },
  { id: "a-trim", cat: "Your car", t: "What Premier means, and what your options could be", tags: "premier trim options packages platinum base equipment features leather navigation sunroof headlights halogen",
    body: ["The 2016 V60 FWD came as T5 Drive-E, T5 Drive-E Premier and T5 Drive-E Platinum, all on 215/50R17 tires.",
      "## Every 2016 V60",
      "- Sensus Connect with a 7-inch screen and Volvo On Call (its connected services died with 3G in 2022).",
      "- HD Radio, SiriusXM, Bluetooth audio, 160-watt 8-speaker sound.",
      "- Moonroof, LED daytime running lights, 40/20/40 folding rear seat, power-folding rear headrests, power lumbar. 43.8 cubic feet of cargo space.",
      "## What Premier adds",
      "Volvo lists leather, an auto-dimming rear-view mirror, the adaptive digital gauge display, roof rails, and Sensus Navigation with MapCare. Edmunds lists navigation as the only difference and shows cloth seats, so check your own seats.",
      "## What Platinum had that you probably don't",
      "Harman Kardon audio, active dual xenon headlights, and the Convenience and Technology packages. That makes Premier headlights halogen unless options were added.",
      "## Options a previous owner may have chosen",
      "- Climate: heated front and rear seats, heated windshield, heated steering wheel, air quality sensor.",
      "- Convenience: keyless drive, rear camera, HomeLink, power-folding mirrors, grocery bag holder.",
      "- BLIS: blind spot information, cross traffic alert, front park assist, lane change merge aid.",
      "- Technology: adaptive cruise with queue assist, collision warning with full auto brake, pedestrian and cyclist detection, lane keeping aid, driver alert, road sign information, active high beam.",
      "- Sport: paddle shifters and sport chassis.",
      "A Volvo dealer can print the car's factory option list from the VIN, which settles which of these you actually have."],
    src: [["Volvo 2016 V60 What's New", "https://mb.cision.com/Main/23622/4196507/3563273.pdf"], ["Volvo 2015.5 V60", "https://mb.cision.com/Main/23622/4196871/3563634.pdf"], ["Edmunds 2016 V60 trims", "https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/v60/2016/trims"]] },
  { id: "a-safety", cat: "How it works", t: "Safety systems: what every 2016 V60 has", tags: "safety city safety auto brake stability dstc traction airbags collision warning blis lane keeping",
    body: ["## Standard on your car",
      "- City Safety: at 30 mph or less it watches the car ahead and pre-charges or applies the brakes to avoid or soften a rear-end crash. Dirt, snow or a cracked windshield in front of the sensor can disable it.",
      "- Dynamic Stability and Traction Control (DSTC) with Advanced Stability Control.",
      "- Corner Traction Control by torque vectoring, which brakes the inside front wheel slightly in a fast corner so the car turns in more cleanly.",
      "## Only if the packages were fitted",
      "Collision Warning with Full Auto Brake and pedestrian and cyclist detection, adaptive cruise, lane keeping aid, driver alert, BLIS, cross traffic alert. See the Premier article to check which packages your car has.",
      "## What you can do",
      "- Keep the windshield area in front of the rear-view mirror clean and uncracked: that is where City Safety looks.",
      "- Warning messages for these systems need a full-module scan, which a basic OBD-II reader cannot do. Volvo's VIDA can."],
    src: [["Volvo 2016 V60 overview", "https://mb.cision.com/Main/23622/4196524/3563289.pdf"], ["Volvo 2016 V60 What's New", "https://mb.cision.com/Main/23622/4196507/3563273.pdf"]] },
  { id: "a-parkbrake", cat: "How it works", t: "The electric parking brake", tags: "parking brake handbrake electric apply release symbol message hill",
    body: ["There is no lever. A control on the centre console drives an electric motor that locks two wheels when the car is parked. Volvo's manual for your car says it \"helps to keep the vehicle stationary when it is parked\". The foot brake does all the braking while you drive.",
      "## Applying it",
      "- Press firmly on the brake pedal.",
      "- Push the control. The parking brake symbol in the instrument panel flashes while the brake applies and stays lit once it is on.",
      "- Release the brake pedal and check that the car is standing still.",
      "- Put the gear selector in P.",
      "- A faint sound from the motor is normal, and the brake pedal moves slightly as the brake applies or releases.",
      "## Releasing it by hand",
      "- Fasten the seat belt.",
      "- Key in the ignition slot and press START/STOP ENGINE (with keyless drive, a valid key inside the car is enough).",
      "- Press firmly on the brake pedal, then pull the control.",
      "## Releasing it automatically",
      "- Start the engine, fasten the seat belt, select D or R and press the accelerator. The brake releases as the car begins to move.",
      "- It only releases by itself with the engine running and the driver's belt on.",
      "- With a heavy load or a trailer on a steep hill the car can roll back on automatic release. Hold the control in with your left hand while you shift to D, and let go only once the car moves.",
      "## In an emergency",
      "- The parking brake can be applied while moving by holding the control in. Braking stops when you let go or press the accelerator. A signal sounds above 6 mph.",
      "## Parking on a hill",
      "- Uphill: turn the front wheels away from the curb. Downhill: toward the curb. Apply the parking brake as well as P.",
      "## Symbols and messages",
      "- A flashing symbol means the brake is being applied. Flashing at any other time means a fault: read the message.",
      "- \"Park brake not fully released\": a fault is stopping the release. Apply and release several times. If it stays, an authorized Volvo workshop. Driving on gives a warning sound.",
      "- \"Parking brake not applied\": a fault is stopping it from applying. Same remedy.",
      "- \"Parking brake Service required\": a fault. Apply and release; if it remains, a Volvo workshop.",
      "- If you must park with a fault, always use P and turn the wheels into the curb as above.",
      "## Battery",
      "- With the battery too low the brake can neither be applied nor released. Connect a donor battery first (see the jump-start job).",
      "## Service",
      "- The 2014 edition of the V60 manual says the rear brake linings must be replaced at a workshop because of the electric parking brake's design. The 2016 US page does not repeat the line, so treat it as unconfirmed for your car and ask the shop."],
    src: ["pb_gen", "pb_apply", "pb_rel", "pb_sym", "pb_au"] },
  { id: "a-ignition", cat: "How it works", t: "Starting the car, and the three ignition modes", tags: "start button ignition mode key keyless remote cold start",
    body: ["The engine is started and stopped with the remote key and the START/STOP ENGINE button. The same button also steps through three ignition modes that power parts of the car without starting it.",
      "## Starting",
      "- Push the remote key fully into the ignition slot. With keyless drive the key only has to be inside the car.",
      "- Press the brake pedal (automatic).",
      "- Press START/STOP ENGINE and release it. The starter runs until the engine starts or its overheat protection cuts in.",
      "- If it has not started after 3 attempts, wait 3 minutes. The battery recovers and the next try is stronger.",
      "- A high idle right after a cold start is normal on some engines: it gets the emissions system to temperature faster.",
      "- Never pull the key out while driving or while the car is towed. Take it with you when you leave the car, in position 0, especially with children around.",
      "## The three ignition modes, no engine",
      "- The brake pedal must not be pressed, or the engine starts instead.",
      "- Mode 0: the car is unlocked. Odometer, clock and temperature gauge are lit, power seats work, and the infotainment works for a limited time.",
      "- Mode I: key in the slot, press START/STOP ENGINE briefly. Moonroof, windows, 12 V sockets, navigation, climate blower and wipers work.",
      "- Mode II: hold START/STOP ENGINE for about 2 seconds. Headlights and tail lights come on and every warning and indicator light shows for 5 seconds, which is a handy lamp check. Heated seats and the heated rear window still need the engine running.",
      "- Back to 0: press the button briefly.",
      "- Mode II only for very short periods, or it drains the battery.",
      "## Start/stop",
      "- The engine can switch itself off at a stop and restart on its own. That is why the safety rules say fully off, key out, before you touch anything under the hood. See the start/stop article for when it does and does not stop."],
    src: ["start", "ign"] },
  { id: "a-steering", cat: "How it works", t: "Steering: adjusting the wheel, steering force, what is on the wheel", tags: "steering wheel adjust lever height reach force heavy overheated horn paddles",
    body: ["The steering is fully electric on this car: no pump, no fluid to check. Two things are yours to set.",
      "## Adjusting the wheel",
      "- A lever under the column releases it. Pull the lever toward you, move the wheel for height and reach, push the lever back to lock. If it is hard to push in, press the wheel lightly while you push.",
      "- Never adjust the steering wheel while driving.",
      "## Steering force",
      "- Cars with the optional speed-dependent power steering let you choose how heavy the steering feels: My Car, Car settings, Steering wheel force, then Low, Medium or High. The menu cannot be opened while the car is moving.",
      "- Whether your Premier has the option is unconfirmed. If the menu entry is not there, it does not.",
      "- Steering force rises with speed by design: light for parking, firmer on the highway.",
      "- If the power steering overheats it cools down for a while with reduced assistance; the steering gets heavier and a message shows. It recovers on its own.",
      "## On the wheel",
      "- Keypads for cruise control (adaptive cruise on some cars), paddles for manual shifting, infotainment controls. The horn is the hub.",
      "## Economical driving, Volvo's list",
      "- Bring the engine to operating temperature as soon as possible and avoid short trips; a cold engine uses more fuel and wears faster.",
      "- Think ahead, accelerate gently, no hard braking. Use D as much as possible and avoid kick-down.",
      "- Check tire pressure regularly, cold. Take off roof racks and unneeded load. At highway speed, A/C with the windows closed uses less fuel than open windows.",
      "- A dirty air filter, old oil, dragging brakes and bad alignment all cost fuel.",
      "- Eco mode is optional on certain four-cylinders in the US manual. A Volvo page for a 2017 S60 in another market describes what it changes: shift points, throttle response, start/stop before standstill, coasting with the gearbox disengaged, and reduced climate control. Whether your car has the ECO button is unconfirmed until you look."],
    src: ["sw", "swf", "ecodrv", "eco"] }
];
```

### `src/js/data/codebook.js`

```javascript
/* Codebook: the adapter's raw signals and the meaning behind each one. Live link shows the raw label until an entry
   is decoded (one tap, no puzzles). Generic OBD-II definitions follow SAE J1979 / J2012 as summarized in the sources below. */
window.V60_CB_SOURCES = {
  pids: ["OBD-II PIDs (Wikipedia summary of SAE J1979)", "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OBD-II_PIDs"],
  obd: ["On-board diagnostics (Wikipedia)", "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-board_diagnostics"],
  cfr: ["40 CFR 85.2222, on-board diagnostic test procedures", "https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-85/subpart-W/section-85.2222"]
};
window.V60_CODEBOOK = [
  /* live signals: key pid:XX matches the hex PID Live link requests */
  { k: "pid:0C", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 0C", n: "Engine speed (RPM)", what: "How fast the crankshaft is turning, in revolutions per minute.", car: "Your Data lab baseline drives record your own warm idle speed, which is the number to compare against later.", src: "pids", art: "a-drivee" },
  { k: "pid:05", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 05", n: "Coolant temperature", what: "The temperature of the engine coolant. It climbs after a cold start, then holds steady once the thermostat starts regulating.", car: "A curve that never settles, or climbs in traffic, is what the overheating path in Troubleshoot covers. Volvo bulletin TJ30268 deals with thermostat fault codes on engines like yours.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:0D", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 0D", n: "Vehicle speed", what: "Road speed as the car's computers see it, from the wheel speed sensors.", car: "The same wheel speed sensors feed your tire monitor, which compares how fast each wheel turns. Live link uses this signal for the 0–60 timer and trip log.", src: "pids", art: "a-tpmshow" },
  { k: "pid:07", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 07", n: "Long-term fuel trim", what: "The fuel correction the engine computer has learned over time to keep the air-fuel mix right. Positive means it is adding fuel because it sees extra air; negative means it is taking fuel away.", car: "A long-term trim that sits well positive points toward unmetered air, such as a vacuum leak. That is the pattern behind code P0171.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:06", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 06", n: "Short-term fuel trim", what: "The instant fuel correction. It swings constantly as the oxygen sensor reports, which is normal.", car: "Read it together with the long-term trim: the two added together are the total correction.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:42", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 42", n: "Control module voltage", what: "System voltage at the engine computer. Engine off, it reflects the battery. Running, it reflects the charging system.", car: "Your car uses an AGM battery because of start/stop. Low voltage readings make start/stop stand down.", src: "pids", art: "a-startstop" },
  { k: "pid:0B", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 0B", n: "Intake manifold pressure", what: "Absolute air pressure inside the intake. Below outside pressure at idle (vacuum), above it when the turbo is making boost.", car: "Boost is this reading minus barometric pressure (PID 33). Live link's boost gauge does that subtraction for you.", src: "pids", art: "a-drivee" },
  { k: "pid:10", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 10", n: "Mass air flow", what: "Grams of air per second entering the engine, measured by the air flow sensor after the air filter.", car: "It rises with load. A dirty or failing sensor misreports air and shows up as fuel trim problems.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:04", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 04", n: "Calculated engine load", what: "How hard the engine is working, as a percentage of what it could do at that speed.", car: "High load at light throttle can mean the car is fighting something, such as dragging brakes.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:11", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 11", n: "Throttle position", what: "How far the electronic throttle is open.", car: "Your throttle is drive-by-wire: the pedal sends a request and the engine computer moves the throttle.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:0F", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 0F", n: "Intake air temperature", what: "Temperature of the air entering the engine.", car: "After a turbo compresses air, it gets hot. Very high intake temperatures reduce power.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:5C", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 5C", n: "Engine oil temperature", what: "Oil temperature, if the engine reports it.", car: "Oil warms up more slowly than coolant. Hard driving before it is warm is extra wear.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:46", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 46", n: "Outside air temperature", what: "Ambient temperature from the car's outside sensor.", car: "Start/stop stands down in very hot or cold weather, so this helps explain why it is not stopping on an Austin summer day.", src: "pids", art: "a-startstop" },
  { k: "pid:33", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 33", n: "Barometric pressure", what: "Outside air pressure.", car: "Needed to turn intake pressure into boost.", src: "pids" },
  { k: "pid:2F", g: "Live signals", raw: "PID 2F", n: "Fuel level", what: "Fuel tank level as a percentage.", car: "Some emissions self-tests only run with the tank between about a quarter and three quarters full.", src: "pids" },
  /* readiness monitors: key mon:<name> */
  { k: "mon:Misfire", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 01", n: "Misfire", what: "Watches crankshaft speed for cylinders that fail to fire. Runs continuously.", car: "A flashing check-engine light means a misfire bad enough to damage the catalytic converter.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Fuel system", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 02", n: "Fuel system", what: "Checks that the fuel trims stay within limits. Runs continuously.", car: "This is the test that sets lean or rich codes such as P0171.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Components", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 03", n: "Comprehensive components", what: "Checks emissions-related sensors and actuators for circuit faults. Runs continuously.", car: "Most sensor circuit codes come from this monitor.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Catalyst", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 04", n: "Catalyst", what: "Compares the oxygen sensors before and after the catalytic converter to judge how well it is cleaning the exhaust.", car: "Usually needs steady cruising to run. Code P0420 comes from this test.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Heated catalyst", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 05", n: "Heated catalyst", what: "Tests an electrically heated catalytic converter. Most cars, likely including yours, do not have one, so it shows as not supported.", car: "If it does not appear in your scan, the car does not run it.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Evaporative system", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 06", n: "Evaporative system", what: "Checks the fuel vapor system for leaks, from the fuel cap to the charcoal canister.", car: "A loose fuel cap is the classic cause of an evaporative leak code. This test often needs a cold start after the car sits overnight.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Secondary air", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 07", n: "Secondary air", what: "Tests a pump some cars use to blow air into the exhaust after a cold start.", car: "If it does not appear in your scan, the car does not have that system.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:A/C refrigerant", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 08", n: "A/C refrigerant", what: "A rarely used test for the air conditioning refrigerant.", car: "Usually not supported.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Oxygen sensor", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 09", n: "Oxygen sensors", what: "Checks that the oxygen sensors respond quickly and correctly.", car: "Coasting with your foot off the pedal (fuel cut) helps this test run.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:Oxygen sensor heater", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 10", n: "Oxygen sensor heaters", what: "Checks the heaters that bring the oxygen sensors up to working temperature quickly.", car: "Usually completes early in a drive.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "mon:EGR / VVT", g: "Readiness monitors", raw: "MONITOR 11", n: "EGR / variable valve timing", what: "Checks exhaust gas recirculation or variable valve timing, depending on the engine.", car: "Your engine has variable timing on both camshafts.", src: "obd" },
  /* trouble code anatomy: decoding any code teaches all four parts */
  { k: "dtc:1", g: "Trouble code anatomy", raw: "P····", n: "First letter: which system", what: "P is powertrain (engine and transmission), C chassis, B body, U network communication between modules.", car: "A basic adapter like yours mostly sees P codes. Body and chassis codes on your Volvo need Volvo's own tools.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "dtc:2", g: "Trouble code anatomy", raw: "·0···", n: "Second digit: who defined it", what: "0 means a generic code with the same meaning on every car. 1 means a manufacturer-specific code. 2 and 3 are mixed.", car: "Generic codes can be looked up anywhere. Volvo-specific ones need Volvo information.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "dtc:3", g: "Trouble code anatomy", raw: "··1··", n: "Third digit: which subsystem", what: "For powertrain codes: 1 and 2 fuel and air metering, 3 ignition and misfire, 4 extra emissions controls, 5 speed and idle control, 6 computer and output circuits, 7 and 8 transmission.", car: "So a P03xx code is about ignition: on your engine, think coils and spark plugs first.", src: "obd" },
  { k: "dtc:4", g: "Trouble code anatomy", raw: "···71", n: "Last two digits: the exact fault", what: "The specific problem within that subsystem.", car: "Example: P0171 means the fuel system on bank 1 is running too lean.", src: "obd" }
];
```

```javascript
   "A cooling-system pressure test shows external leaks as visible seepage; a pressure drop with no visible leak can mean coolant is getting into a combustion chamber through a failed head gasket or cracked block, so the oil and transmission fluid are checked for coolant.",

   "The specified amount of oil goes in, the engine idles for 2 minutes while the drain plug and filter are checked for leaks, and the level is checked again after shutdown.",
   "The mileage and date are recorded and the next change is set from the maker's interval; Mobil does not recommend more than 5,000 miles between changes with conventional oil.",
   "Used oil and drained filters go to a collection point for recycling; the EPA says the used oil from one oil change can contaminate one million gallons of fresh water."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo requires full synthetic oil meeting ACEA A5/B5 with no additives, about 6.2 US qt (5.9 L) including the filter for the 4-cylinder, and reads its level electronically (no dipstick) after about 20 miles of driving or 5 minutes parked level with the engine off. The 'Time for regular maintenance' message is timed by miles, months since the last service and engine running time; the manual does not say how to reset it.",

 "A6": {
  "body": [
   "With the system cool, the cap is removed, the coolant level and hoses are checked, and a tester adapter is fitted to the radiator filler neck or to a pressurized expansion tank.",
   "The pump is worked to the test range for the cap's rating, for example 14 to 18 psi for a 15 or 16 psi cap, or 12 to 16 psi for a 13 or 14 psi cap, and the gauge is watched for a drop.",
   "An overflow bottle with a snap-on or vented cap is not part of the sealed system, so testing through it only vents the pressure; plastic tanks can crack if the adapter plug is overtightened.",
   "While the system holds pressure, the whole system, including every hose and connection, is checked for seepage, and the pressure is released with the tester's relief valve before disconnecting.",
   "Coolant dye made for water-based fluids can be circulated and then traced with a UV lamp to find small or hidden leaks.",
   "Gates notes that a faulty pressure cap can let air into the system and speed up corrosion, so the cap is inspected and replaced if faulty."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo's manual says never to open the expansion tank cap with the engine warm and, if a warm top-up cannot be avoided, to unscrew it slowly so the overpressure escapes. The V60 has a radiator and a coolant expansion tank, and the manual does not give the cap's pressure rating.",

 "A7": {
  "body": [
   "Gates recommends replacing accessory belts at least every 4 years or 62,000 miles (100,000 km) and inspecting them at every service, with the vehicle maker's procedure taking priority.",
   "Before removal the routing is recorded; the automatic tensioner is released and held, and the tensioner, idlers, torsional vibration damper and overrunning alternator pulley are checked for wear along with pulley alignment.",
   "The new belt must sit square in every pulley groove (feel behind any pulley that cannot be seen); the automatic tensioner is released slowly to set tension, and the engine is run a few minutes with no readjustment afterwards.",
   "Too much tension causes heat, cracking and broken cords; too little causes slipping, noise and shiny flanks on both sides of the ribs. For manually tensioned Micro-V drives Gates gives 100 N (10 kg) per rib for a new belt and 60 N (6 kg) per rib for a used one.",
   "Misalignment above 1 degree causes pilling, damaged outer ribs that can get into the timing belt drive, and shine on one side of the ribs; it must be corrected before a new belt goes on.",
   "Belt dressing, soap, silicone spray and similar products only hide noise and can permanently damage the belt."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo's owner's manual lists checking the condition of the drive belts among the checks before a long trip.",
  "src": [
   [
    "Gates: How to replace a Micro-V belt in 7 easy steps",
    "https://www.gatestechzone.com/en/installation/belts-and-kits/micro-v-belts"
   ],

   ]
  ],
  "qs": [
   {
    "q": "A Micro-V belt shows small rubber balls in its grooves and a shiny surface on one side of the ribs. What is the most likely cause?",
    "o": [
     "Too much belt tension",
     "Pulley misalignment",
     "Oil contamination",
     "A belt that is too long"

    ]
   },
   {

    "o": [
     "Technician A only",
     "Technician B only",
     "Both A and B",
     "Neither A nor B"

     "https://gates.com/us/en/industries/automotive/vehicle-aftermarket/power-up/identifying-and-addressing-causes-of-belt-noise.html"
    ]
   }
  ]
 },
 "A8": {
  "body": [
   "A coolant hose has three layers: an inner tube, a reinforcement and an outer cover.",
   "Electrochemical degradation is the most common failure: dissimilar metals produce an electrical charge in the coolant that cracks the tube from inside. It is found by squeezing near the ends; soft, mushy spots within about 2 inches of the connectors or internal channels mean replacement with an ECD-resistant hose.",
   "Heat damage shows as slight swelling or a hard, glossy, cracked cover; ozone causes fine parallel cracks, usually at bends; oil contamination makes a hose soft, spongy and swollen.",
   "Hoses are checked for kinks and for contact with hot or moving parts and sharp edges; an abraded hose is replaced and rerouted or sleeved, but not with a slit piece of old hose.",
   "Leaks at clamps come from low clamp torque or worn parts; adjustable clamps are retightened after a short run-in, or constant-tension clamps are used."
  ],
  "car": null,
  "src": [
   [
    "Gates: Hose Failure Symptoms",
    "https://www.gatestechzone.com/en/problem-diagnosis/cooling-system/hose-failure-symptoms"
   ]
  ],
  "qs": [
   {
    "q": "A lower radiator hose feels firm in the middle but soft and mushy within about 2 inches of each end. What is the most likely cause?",
    "o": [
     "Ozone attack",
     "Electrochemical degradation",
     "Heat damage from the exhaust",
     "A loose clamp"
    ],
    "a": 1,
    "why": "Gates describes soft, mushy hose ends within about 2 inches of the connectors as the sign of electrochemical degradation.",
    "src": [
     "Gates: Hose Failure Symptoms",
     "https://www.gatestechzone.com/en/problem-diagnosis/cooling-system/hose-failure-symptoms"
    ]
   },
   {
    "q": "Technician A says fine parallel cracks at a hose bend are typical of ozone damage. Technician B says a slit piece of old hose makes a good protective sleeve against abrasion. Who is correct?",
    "o": [
     "Technician A only",
     "Technician B only",
     "Both A and B",
     "Neither A nor B"

    "src": [
     "Gates: Hose Failure Symptoms",
     "https://www.gatestechzone.com/en/problem-diagnosis/cooling-system/hose-failure-symptoms"
    ]
   }
  ]

 "A9": {
  "body": [
   "A thermostat's wax element changes volume with temperature: when the engine is cold, coolant bypasses the radiator through a smaller bypass loop, and at operating temperature the thermostat opens the path to the radiator.",
   "If the temperature climbs sharply, all the coolant goes through the radiator and the bypass closes; map-controlled thermostats add a heater controlled by the engine computer so they respond faster.",
   "MAHLE lists a jammed working piston, corrosion, a faulty housing or gasket, debris in the system and failed electric actuation as causes of thermostat faults, which can lead to overheating, poor cabin heat, higher fuel use and coolant loss.",
   "An infrared thermometer helps: an upper radiator hose that gets hot before warm-up is complete points to a thermostat stuck open, and one that stays cold points to a thermostat that does not open.",
   "A badly installed thermostat can leak at the mounting surface; torque specs are followed, seals and gaskets are checked for damage and seating, and sealant is used only where the maker calls for it."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo's fuse list for 4-cylinder engines puts the thermostat on a 10 A fuse with the mass air meter and EVAP valve, so this engine's thermostat has an electrical part. That fits MAHLE's description of a map-controlled thermostat, but no fetched Volvo document confirms the type.",
  "src": [
   [
    "MAHLE: Thermal management control units brochure 2024 (EN)",
    "https://mpulse.mahle.com/assets/Artikelbilder/Thermostate/EN_48_1803_Thermostat_Broschuere_EN_2024_WEB_Doppelseiten.pdf"

    "o": [

 "A10": {
  "body": [
   "A refractometer reads the coolant's freeze point: it is zeroed with distilled water, one or two drops of coolant go on the prism, and the reading is where the shadow line crosses the scale. The Robinair 75240 reads from -60 °F to 32 °F and is re-zeroed every 30 minutes.",
   "Draining starts only with a fully cool engine; the front is raised on stands, the undertray removed if needed, and the coolant drained from the radiator drain valve. Rust or debris in it calls for further inspection.",
   "For a flush, PEAK has the system filled with water, run for 10 to 15 minutes with the heater on high, and drained, repeated two or three times until the water runs clear.",
   "The system is refilled with correctly diluted coolant (most cars take 50/50, and concentrate should be mixed before pouring), then run 10 to 15 minutes with the heater on high to push out air pockets that could cause overheating.",
   "PEAK says tap water will do for flushing; Volvo says chlorinated tap water must not go into the cooling system, and for this car Volvo's rule wins. Used coolant goes to a service center or hazardous-waste site."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo specifies Volvo Genuine Coolant mixed 50/50 with water, 8.7 US qt (8.3 L) for the B4204T11, says coolant types must not be mixed and the system must not be topped up with water alone, and says a drained system should be flushed with clean water or premixed antifreeze before refilling. The manual adds that the coolant normally does not need changing.",

 "A11": {
  "body": [
   "The water pump circulates coolant, and a failing one can overheat the engine; Gates recommends replacing the pump together with the belt, tensioner and other drive parts, because each affects the others' life.",
   "With the engine off, the pump shaft should show no side-to-side play by hand; play or a rumbling or screeching noise means a worn bearing, caused by misalignment, an over-tensioned belt or coolant washing out lubricant through a failed seal.",
   "The weep hole sits between the pump's bearings and seals; a little seepage is normal for about 10 minutes on a new pump while the seal seats, but a continuing drip or a large stain means failure, and AISIN warns against sealing the weep hole with epoxy.",
   "Corroded impeller fins, sludge deposits and cavitation pitting come from contaminated, incompatible or mixed coolant; the fix is a new pump, a system flush and the correct coolant, plus a check of the pressure cap.",
   "A pump must never run dry, even briefly, because it destroys the mechanical seal; the system is flushed at replacement and belt tension and pulley alignment are checked."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo's fuse list shows a 50 A fuse for the coolant pump on 4-cylinder engines, and TJ 36858 (covering type 155 with engine 40) describes a replacement pump, PN 32441265, with modified internal programming; this points to an electrically driven pump rather than a belt-driven one, but that is not confirmed in a Volvo repair document fetched here.",
  "src": [
   [
    "Gates: Water Pump Failure Signs",
    "https://www.gatestechzone.com/en/problem-diagnosis/cooling-system/water-pump-failure-signs"
   ],

   ],

   ],
   [
    "Volvo V60 Owner's Manual, Model Year 2016 (US, TP 20238)",
    "https://ldgsvccassets.blob.core.windows.net/pdfs/610e4b1a5665ac4d99bd89bd1971f063df1c7284/V60_OwnersManual_MY16_en-US_TP20238.pdf"
   ]
  ],
  "qs": [
   {
    "q": "A newly installed water pump shows slight seepage at the weep hole during the first few minutes of running. What is the most likely explanation?",
    "o": [
     "The pump is defective and must be replaced",

     "The cooling system is overpressurized",
     "The wrong coolant was used"
    ],
    "a": 1,
    "why": "Gates says a little weep-hole seepage is normal for about ten minutes while a new pump's mechanical seal seats.",

     "Technician B only",
     "Both A and B",
     "Neither A nor B"
    ],
    "a": 1,
    "why": "Gates says there should be no shaft play under hand pressure, and that rumbling or screeching indicates a worn bearing.",
    "src": [

   }

 "A12": {
  "body": [
   "This task confirms that the radiator cooling fan runs when it should and that nothing blocks airflow through the radiator: the fan clutch on engine-driven fans, the fan shroud and the air dams.",
   "MAHLE's workshop guide says electric fans are switched by pressure or temperature switches or by a control unit, either in steps or continuously with pulse-width control, and are mounted on a shroud as close to the radiator as possible so air passes through the core with little loss.",
   "When an electric fan does not run, MAHLE lists checking the switch-on point, the fuse, the thermal switch and the fan control unit; a scan tool can read the fault memory, and an infrared thermometer can compare radiator inlet and outlet temperatures.",
   "Hayden's thermal fan clutch guide gives fan speed as about 10 to 20 percent of pulley speed when the clutch is disengaged and about 60 to 90 percent when engaged, and says the blade tip should rock forward and back no more than 1/4 inch.",
   "Hayden also lists blocked shrouds and air dams, debris on the radiator and condenser, and bent, cracked or chipped blades as airflow problems to rule out; a clutch that will not disengage causes excessive fan noise and, on some later vehicles, codes P2181 or P0128.",
   "MAHLE's engine-off hand test for a viscous clutch: the fan should turn easily when the engine is cold and with difficulty when it is warm."
  ],
  "car": "The V60's cooling fan sits at the front of the engine compartment behind the radiator, has its own 60 A fuse (4- and 5-cylinder engines), and can start or keep running for up to 6 minutes after the engine is switched off.",

 "A13": {
  "body": [
   "This task checks that the instrument panel warning lamps and indicators work, so a real fault is visible when it happens.",
   "EPA's OBD fact sheet says the check engine light should come on briefly when the ignition is switched on and stay off while driving unless a problem is detected; a steady light means a detected problem, and a flashing light means a severe one, such as a misfire that can damage the catalytic converter.",
   "Under 40 CFR 85.2222, an OBD emissions inspection fails a vehicle whose malfunction indicator does not light at all with the key on and engine off, even with no codes stored, and also fails one whose computer has commanded the lamp on while the lamp itself stays dark.",
   "Volvo's red warning symbols include low oil pressure, generator not charging, brake system fault and the SRS airbags. For low oil pressure Volvo says to stop, switch off the engine and check the oil level; if the level is normal and the light stays on after a restart, the car should be towed.",
   "Volvo signals overheating with text and a red warning triangle in the instrument display, ranging from High engine temp Reduce speed to High engine temp Stop engine, and says to let the engine cool before checking oil and coolant."
  ],
  "car": "On the 2016 V60 all indicator and warning symbols light in ignition mode II or at engine start; once the engine runs, all should go out except the parking brake symbol. If the check is done in mode II without starting, all go out after 5 seconds except the malfunction indicator and low oil pressure symbols.",
  "src": [
   [
    "Do You Drive a 1996 or Newer Car or Light Truck? (EPA420-F-02-016)",
    "https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=P1002K2N.txt"
   ],
   [
    "§ 85.2222 Onboard diagnostic test procedures (40 CFR 85.2222)",
    "https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-85/subpart-W/section-85.2222"
   ],
   [
    "Volvo 2016 V60 US Owner's Manual (TP20238)",
    "https://ldgsvccassets.blob.core.windows.net/pdfs/610e4b1a5665ac4d99bd89bd1971f063df1c7284/V60_OwnersManual_MY16_en-US_TP20238.pdf"
   ]
  ],
  "qs": [
   {
    "q": "During a key-on, engine-off check at an OBD emissions inspection, the malfunction indicator lamp does not light at all. No trouble codes are stored. Under 40 CFR 85.2222 the vehicle:",
    "o": [
     "Passes, because no codes are stored",
     "Fails the OBD inspection",
     "Passes if all readiness monitors are complete",
     "Is sent away to complete a drive cycle"
    ],
    "a": 1,
    "why": "The rule says a vehicle whose MIL does not illuminate at all in the key-on/engine-off condition fails, even if no DTCs are present and the MIL has not been commanded on.",
    "src": [
     "§ 85.2222 Onboard diagnostic test procedures (40 CFR 85.2222)",

     "Only the parking brake symbol",
     "Every indicator and warning symbol",

    ]
   }

 },
 "A14": {
  "body": [
   "This task covers inspecting and cleaning the intake air path from the air filter to the throttle body, and relearning idle afterwards when the vehicle requires it.",
   "Standard Motor Products describes electronic throttle control: pedal position sensors send the driver's request to the PCM, a motor opens and closes the throttle blade, and several throttle position sensors report the blade's position back. The PCM, not the pedal, sets the actual opening.",
   "CRC's cleaning procedure starts with a cool engine, removes the intake duct from the throttle, and checks the blade edges, the seat line and the manifold side of the plate for deposits. It lists rough idle, hesitation, stalling and a check engine light as signs of a dirty throttle body.",
   "CRC warns not to force the blade of an electronic throttle open, which can damage the throttle motor, not to use carburetor or brake cleaner, and not to spray through the air filter or across the mass air flow sensor. With the throttle body still on the engine, the cleaner goes on a rag, not into the bore.",
   "After an electronic throttle part is replaced, Standard says to clear the PCM memory and relearn the throttle values to avoid idle problems; the procedure varies by vehicle, so service information decides it.",
   "Walker lists the intake boot joints between the mass air flow sensor and the intake manifold as a common place for small leaks, which can badly skew sensor readings."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo's fuse table for 4-cylinder engines lists the mass air meter on a 10 A fuse shared with the thermostat and EVAP valve. The manual warns that engine damage will occur if water is drawn into the air cleaner.",
  "src": [

    "https://www.walkerexhaust.com/support/tech-tips/finding-exhaust-system-leaks.html"

   ]
  ],
  "qs": [
   {
    "q": "A technician cleans an electronic throttle body that is still installed on the engine. Which step is LEAST likely to be recommended?",
    "o": [
     "Spraying cleaner onto a rag and wiping the bore",
     "Prying the throttle blade open by hand to reach behind it",
     "Using a lint-free cloth with light pressure",
     "Keeping cleaner away from the mass air flow sensor"
    ],
    "a": 1,
    "why": "CRC says not to force the butterfly of a drive-by-wire throttle open because it can damage the electronic throttle control motor; with the unit on the engine, cleaner goes on a rag.",

   {
    "q": "After an electronic throttle body is replaced, the engine idles erratically. Technician A says the PCM may need to relearn the throttle values. Technician B says the relearn procedure is the same on every vehicle. Who is correct?",
    "o": [
     "Technician A only",
     "Technician B only",
     "Both A and B",
     "Neither A nor B"
    ],
    "a": 0,

    "src": [
     "A Closer Look: Electronic Throttle Bodies",
     "https://www.standardbrand.com/training-insights/training/a-closer-look-electronic-throttle-bodies/"
    ]
   }
  ]
 },
 "A15": {
  "body": [
   "This task covers checking and replacing the engine air filter and inspecting its housing and intake ducts for dirt, damage and poor sealing.",
   "FRAM's procedure: let the engine cool, find the air filter housing (usually a black plastic box joined to a large intake hose), release its hooks or screws without forcing them, note how the old filter sits, and vacuum dirt out of the housing before fitting the new one.",
   "The new filter should sit snugly without being forced, with no edges bent or caught, and the cover must be fully secured. FRAM says a whistle or rattle after start-up can mean a poor seal.",
   "FRAM advises against reinstalling a used filter, even one removed only for inspection, because dirt from the outer side can reach the engine side. It lists lower fuel economy, sluggish acceleration and a check engine light as signs of a clogged filter.",
   "FRAM says manufacturers generally recommend changing standard filters every 12,000 to 15,000 miles, and more often in dusty conditions."
  ],
  "car": "The air cleaner is one of the main inspection points in Volvo's V60 engine compartment overview. Volvo lists a dirty air cleaner among the factors that lower fuel economy and warns that water drawn into the air cleaner will damage the engine. The air filter interval for this car is unconfirmed.",
  "src": [

    "https://www.fram.com/vehicle-maintenance-center/post/how-to-change-engine-air-filter"
   ],

    "https://www.fram.com/vehicle-maintenance-center/post/dirty-air-filter-symptoms"

   ]
  ],
  "qs": [
   {
    "q": "A customer asks for the engine air filter to be removed, looked at, and put back if it seems clean. According to FRAM, the best practice is to:",
    "o": [
     "Reinstall it if light shines through it",
     "Tap it clean and reinstall it",
     "Replace it once it has been removed",
     "Reinstall it facing the opposite way"
    ],
    "a": 2,
    "why": "FRAM says that if an air filter is removed, even for inspection, it should be replaced, because contaminants on the dirty side can be drawn into the engine.",

 },
 "A16": {
  "body": [
   "This task covers inspecting the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) system, its valve, hoses and any oil separator, and replacing worn parts.",
   "EPA's 1977 PCV training manual explains that combustion gas leaking past the piston rings, called blowby, carries fuel vapor, acids and water vapor into the crankcase; the PCV system draws it into the intake to be burned and replaces it with fresh air. The valve's plunger, moved by manifold vacuum, limits flow at idle, allows the most flow at cruise and closes when the engine stops or backfires.",
   "The same manual's inspection: confirm all parts are present and unmodified, check hoses for cracks, deterioration and loose connections, check for large crankcase oil leaks, and look for oil in the air cleaner, which points to a blocked valve pushing blowby out through the fresh-air inlet.",
   "Two of its tests: at operating temperature, remove the valve and cover its end, and idle should drop 40 to 80 rpm (no drop suggests a blocked system); or hold thin paper over the oil filler opening at idle, and crankcase vacuum should pull it tight.",
   "Standard Motor Products notes that a faulty PCV system can leave the crankcase under excessive pressure and cause oil leaks, that some PCV valves have heaters to stop them freezing, and that oil separators keep oil from being drawn into the cylinders. EPA warns that the wrong replacement hose may collapse."
  ],
  "car": null,
  "src": [
   [
    "Motor Vehicle Emissions Control: Book One - Positive Crankcase Ventilation Systems (EPA-450/3-77-036)",
    "https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=91010D2I.TXT"
   ],
   [
    "Emission Control Components: EVAP, EGR & Crankcase Ventilation Systems | Standard",
    "https://www.standardbrand.com/whats-in-your-box/emission-controls/?tab=evap-components&subtab=canister-purge-solenoids"
   ]
  ],
  "qs": [
   {
    "q": "With the engine at operating temperature, a technician removes the PCV valve and covers its open end. Idle speed does not change. What is most likely?",
    "o": [
     "The PCV system is working normally",
     "The PCV system is blocked",
     "The engine has excessive blowby",
     "The oil level is overfull"
    ],
    "a": 1,
    "why": "EPA's PCV manual says idle should drop 40 to 80 rpm when the valve is blocked off; no drop indicates a blocked PCV system.",
    "src": [
     "Motor Vehicle Emissions Control: Book One - Positive Crankcase Ventilation Systems (EPA-450/3-77-036)",
     "https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=91010D2I.TXT"
    ]
   },
   {
    "q": "Oil is found in the air cleaner housing. Technician A says a blocked PCV valve can cause this. Technician B says cracked or loose PCV hoses can lean out the air-fuel mixture. Who is correct?",
    "o": [
     "Technician A only",
     "Technician B only",
     "Both A and B",
     "Neither A nor B"
    ],
    "a": 2,
    "why": "EPA says a blocked PCV valve sends blowby out through the air inlet, leaving excess oil in the air cleaner, and that air leaks from cracked or loose hoses may lean out the air-fuel ratio.",
    "src": [
     "Motor Vehicle Emissions Control: Book One - Positive Crankcase Ventilation Systems (EPA-450/3-77-036)",
     "https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=91010D2I.TXT"
    ]
   }
  ]
 },
 "A17": {
  "body": [
   "This task covers checking the exhaust system for leaks and for loose, broken or missing hangers, brackets and heat shields.",
   "Walker's inspection checks welds for breaks, cracks and corrosion, pipe joints for misalignment and burned gaskets, clamp joints, and the flex pipe, which it calls a common failure point; a road test listens for unusual exhaust sounds and checks for exhaust odor in the cabin.",
   "Walker says to look for leaks with the system cold and again at operating temperature, that a smoke machine is the usual way to find small leaks, and that pinholes in the welds around oxygen sensor ports and joints ahead of the converter or within 3 inches after it are typical leak points. Small leaks can badly skew oxygen sensor readings.",
   "Hangers and isolators are checked for wear and for loose, damaged or missing parts. On a lift, moving the system side to side and up and down (carefully, since it gets hot) shows whether it is hung securely or touching the underbody.",
   "Walker's installation guidance calls for 1/4 to 1/2 inch of clearance where metal parts could touch and 2 to 3 inches from parts not built for heat; cold isolators should be loaded evenly and angled slightly forward, and hang straight up and down at operating temperature.",
   "Leak symptoms Walker lists include a loud rumble on acceleration, popping or hissing, lost power and lower fuel economy; it warns that many exhaust gases have no odor."
  ],
  "car": "Volvo warns that carbon monoxide, which has no color or smell, is present in all exhaust gas, and that any exhaust smell inside the V60 calls for ventilating the cabin and having the car checked right away. Volvo also says not to park over grass or leaves, which the hot exhaust system can ignite.",

    ]
   },
   {
    "q": "Technician A says an exhaust system should be checked for leaks cold and again at operating temperature. Technician B says that if no exhaust smell is noticed in the cabin, the exhaust has no leak. Who is correct?",
    "o": [
     "Technician A only",
```
