### `tests/sync.js`

```javascript
/* Sync across devices against a mocked GitHub contents API: connect, push, pull on a second device, conflict choice. */
const { chromium } = require(process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_PATH||'playwright');
const path=require('path');const ROOT=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
function ok(c,m){ if(!c){ console.log('FAIL',m); process.exitCode=1; } else console.log(' ok',m); }
(async()=>{const b=await chromium.launch(process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH?{executablePath:process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH}:{});
const store={}; let n=0;
async function device(){ const ctx=await b.newContext({viewport:{width:390,height:844}}); await ctx.addInitScript(()=>{window.__V60_TEST=true;});
  await ctx.route('https://api.github.com/**', async route=>{ const req=route.request(); const u=new URL(req.url()); const p=decodeURIComponent(u.pathname.split('/contents/')[1]);
    if(req.headers()['authorization']!=='Bearer good') return route.fulfill({status:401,body:'{}'});
    if(req.method()==='GET'){ const f=store[p]; if(!f) return route.fulfill({status:404,body:'{}'}); return route.fulfill({status:200,contentType:'application/json',body:JSON.stringify({sha:f.sha,encoding:'base64',content:f.content})}); }
    if(req.method()==='PUT'){ const body=JSON.parse(req.postData()); const f=store[p]; if(f && body.sha!==f.sha) return route.fulfill({status:409,body:'{}'}); const sha='s'+(++n); store[p]={sha,content:body.content}; return route.fulfill({status:f?200:201,contentType:'application/json',body:JSON.stringify({content:{sha}})}); }
    route.fulfill({status:405,body:'{}'}); });
  const p=await ctx.newPage(); const errs=[]; p.on('pageerror',e=>errs.push(e.message)); await p.goto('file://'+ROOT+'/index.html'); await p.waitForTimeout(400); p.errs=errs; return p; }
async function connect(p,tok){ await p.evaluate(()=>{__v60.go('story');}); await p.evaluate(()=>{ window.V60.jump('opts:sync'); }); await p.fill('#syncRepo','bmcdoorz94/v60-garage-data'); await p.fill('#syncTok',tok); await p.click('#syncGo'); await p.waitForTimeout(800); }
const A=await device(), B=await device();
await connect(A,'bad'); ok(/rejected/.test(await A.textContent('#syncStatus')),'bad token explained');
await A.evaluate(()=>{V60.state.odo=95210; V60.save();});
await connect(A,'good'); ok(!!store['garage.json'],'device A pushed its progress');
await connect(B,'good'); ok(await B.evaluate(()=>V60.state.odo)===95210,'device B pulled A\'s progress');
await B.evaluate(()=>{V60.state.oil.push({id:'o1',date:'2026-10-11',miles:95300,qts:0}); V60.save();}); await B.waitForTimeout(3600);
await A.evaluate(()=>window.V60_SYNC.pull()); await A.waitForTimeout(600);
ok(await A.evaluate(()=>V60.state.oil.length)===1,'change on B reaches A');
// conflict: both change
await A.evaluate(()=>{V60.state.odo=95400; V60.save();}); await A.waitForTimeout(3600);
await B.evaluate(()=>{ const m=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('v60-sync')); m.dirty=true; localStorage.setItem('v60-sync',JSON.stringify(m)); V60.state.odo=95350; }); 
await B.evaluate(()=>window.V60_SYNC.pull()); await B.waitForTimeout(600);
ok(await B.isVisible('#syncConflict'),'conflict asks which copy to keep');
await B.click('[data-keep="there"]'); await B.waitForTimeout(400);
ok(await B.evaluate(()=>V60.state.odo)===95400,'keeping the other device applies it');
ok(!A.errs.length && !B.errs.length,'no page errors '+A.errs.concat(B.errs).join('|'));
await b.close();})();
```

### `tests/tire.js`

```javascript
/* Tire sidewall photos: DOT date, size and age are read on the device; the saved photo carries the reading.
   Synthetic text only. Needs jsDelivr reachable for the OCR engine. */
const PW = process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_PATH || "playwright";
const { chromium } = require(PW);
const http = require("http"), fs = require("fs"), path = require("path");
const ROOT = path.join(__dirname, "..");
let fails = 0; const ok = (c, m) => { console.log((c ? " ok " : " FAIL ") + m); if (!c) fails++; };
const srv = http.createServer((q, r) => {
  let f = path.join(ROOT, decodeURIComponent(q.url.split("?")[0])); if (f.endsWith("/")) f += "index.html";
  fs.readFile(f, (e, d) => { if (e) { r.writeHead(404); r.end(); return; } r.writeHead(200, { "content-type": f.endsWith(".js") ? "text/javascript" : f.endsWith(".css") ? "text/css" : "text/html" }); r.end(d); });
}).listen(0);
(async () => {
  const port = srv.address().port;
  const b = await chromium.launch({ executablePath: process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH });
  const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 } });
  const errs = []; p.on("pageerror", e => errs.push(e.message));
  await p.addInitScript(() => { window.__V60_TEST = true; });
  await p.goto(`http://localhost:${port}/index.html`); await p.waitForTimeout(800);
  const u = await p.evaluate(() => {
    const S = window.V60_SCAN, yy = String(new Date().getFullYear() % 100).padStart(2, "0");
    const old = S._tireDot("DOT 4H3R FXN 1522"), none = S._tireDot("DOT 4H3R FXN"), badwk = S._tireDot("DOT 4H3R FXN 9922"), fut = S._tireDot("DOT 4H3R FXN 10" + String(+yy + 3));
    const f = S._parse("MICHELIN 215/50R17 95V DOT 4H3R FXN 1522", "", S._classify("215/50R17 DOT 4H3R FXN 1522"));
    const d = S.describe({ kind: "tire", fields: { dot: "0118", size: "225/45R17" }, text: "", read: true }, "sidewall");
    return { old, none, badwk, fut, f, cls: S._classify("215/50R17 DOT 4H3R FXN 1522"), d };
  });
  ok(u.old === "1522", "DOT date read (" + u.old + ")");
  ok(u.none === null && u.badwk === null && u.fut === null, "no date, week 99 and a future year are rejected");
  ok(u.cls === "tire" && u.f.size === "215/50R17" && u.f.dot === "1522", "classified and decoded (" + JSON.stringify(u.f) + ")");
  ok(u.d.concern === "act" && /replace tires at 6 years/.test(u.d.next[0]) && /225\/45R17/.test(u.d.observations.join(" ")), "old tire and different size flagged");
  /* full run: synthetic sidewall photo saved from My V60 */
  const png = await p.evaluate(() => {
    const c = document.createElement("canvas"); c.width = 1100; c.height = 600; const g = c.getContext("2d");
    g.fillStyle = "#fff"; g.fillRect(0, 0, c.width, c.height); g.fillStyle = "#111"; g.font = "bold 60px Arial";
    ["215/50R17 95V", "DOT 4H3R FXN 1522"].forEach((t, i) => g.fillText(t, 60, 180 + i * 150));
    return c.toDataURL("image/png").split(",")[1];
  });
  await p.evaluate(() => __v60.go("my")); await p.selectOption("#phKind", "sidewall");
  await p.setInputFiles("#phFile", { name: "sidewall.png", mimeType: "image/png", buffer: Buffer.from(png, "base64") });
  await p.waitForSelector("#scanOv:not([hidden])", { timeout: 10000 });
  await p.waitForFunction(() => !document.getElementById("scanSave").disabled, null, { timeout: 120000 });
  const fields = await p.textContent("#scanFields"); console.log("   fields:", fields.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " "));
  ok(/week 15 of 2022/.test(fields) && /215\/50R17/.test(fields), "review sheet shows the DOT date and size");
  await p.click("#scanSave");
  await p.waitForFunction(() => (V60.state.photos || []).length === 1, null, { timeout: 20000 });
  const rec = await p.evaluate(() => V60.state.photos[0]);
  ok(rec.kind === "sidewall" && rec.ai && rec.ai.dot === "1522" && rec.ai.device === true, "saved photo carries the reading (" + JSON.stringify(rec.ai && rec.ai.dot) + ")");
  const card = await p.textContent("#phGallery"); ok(/DOT date code 1522/.test(card), "gallery shows the DOT date");
  await p.reload(); await p.waitForTimeout(800); await p.evaluate(() => __v60.go("my"));
  ok(/DOT date code 1522/.test(await p.textContent("#phGallery")), "reading is still there after a reload");
  ok(errs.length === 0, "no page errors " + JSON.stringify(errs));
  await b.close(); srv.close();
  console.log(fails ? fails + " failed" : "all passed"); process.exit(fails ? 1 : 0);
})().catch(e => { console.error(e); srv.close(); process.exit(1); });
```

### `tests/tools.js`

```javascript
/* Glovebox tool inventory: tiers, sourced store prices, the owner's own price (saved, survives reload, cleared back to the store price),
   tier totals. Also the ASE article: it opens in the Library and The Belt case unlocks it. */
const { chromium } = require(process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_PATH || 'playwright');
const path = require('path'); const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
function ok(c, m) { if (!c) { console.log('FAIL', m); process.exitCode = 1; } else console.log(' ok', m); }
(async () => {
  const b = await chromium.launch(process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH ? { executablePath: process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH } : {});
  const ctx = await b.newContext({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 } }); await ctx.addInitScript(() => { window.__V60_TEST = true; });
  const p = await ctx.newPage(); const errs = []; p.on('pageerror', e => errs.push(e.message));
  await p.goto('file://' + ROOT + '/index.html'); await p.waitForTimeout(400);

  // the ASE article is locked at the start and unlocked by The Belt case
  const belt = await p.evaluate(() => (window.V60_STORY.cases || []).filter(c => c.id === 'belt')[0]);
  ok(belt && belt.know.arts.indexOf('a-ase') >= 0, 'The Belt case unlocks the ASE article');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => !window.V60_KNOW.article('a-ase')), 'ASE article is not in the Library on day one');

  await p.evaluate(() => { const s = V60.mod('story'); s.all = true; V60.setMod('story', s); V60.save(); __v60.go('glove'); });
  await p.waitForTimeout(300);
  const tiers = await p.$$eval('#gbTools .ttier h4', els => els.map(e => e.textContent));
  ok(tiers.length === 3 && /Tier 1/.test(tiers[0]) && /Tier 3/.test(tiers[2]), 'three tiers shown: ' + JSON.stringify(tiers));
  const n = await p.$$eval('#gbTools .tool', els => els.length);
  ok(n === await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_TOOLS.length), 'every tool is shown (' + n + ')');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_TOOLS.every(t => t.length >= 3 && typeof t[1] === 'string')), 'V60_TOOLS keeps [id, name, use] for the DIY jobs');

  // sourced prices: every price has a store, a link and a number, and the check date is set
  const P = await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_TOOL_PRICES);
  ok(P && /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(P.checked), 'price list has a checked date');
  const bad = [];
  Object.keys(P.items).forEach(k => P.items[k].forEach(x => { if (x.price != null && !(x.store && /^https:\/\//.test(x.url) && x.price > 0)) bad.push(k); }));
  ok(bad.length === 0, 'every store price has a store, an https link and a positive number ' + JSON.stringify(bad));
  const ids = await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_TOOLS.map(t => t[0]));
  ok(Object.keys(P.items).every(k => ids.indexOf(k) >= 0), 'every priced id is a real tool');

  // the owner's price replaces the store price, persists, and can be cleared
  const tool = 'gauge';
  await p.click('details[data-tp="' + tool + '"] summary');
  await p.fill('#gbTP-' + tool, '7.5'); await p.press('#gbTP-' + tool, 'Tab'); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  ok(/\$7\.50 · your price/.test(await p.textContent('details[data-tp="' + tool + '"] summary')), 'own price shows in the summary');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => V60.mod('glove').price.gauge === 7.5), 'own price saved');
  await p.reload(); await p.waitForTimeout(500); await p.evaluate(() => __v60.go('glove')); await p.waitForTimeout(200);
  ok(/\$7\.50 · your price/.test(await p.textContent('details[data-tp="' + tool + '"] summary')), 'own price survives a reload');
  const head1 = await p.textContent('#gbTools .ttier:first-child h4');
  await p.click('details[data-tp="' + tool + '"] summary');
  await p.click('[data-tpclear="' + tool + '"]'); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => V60.mod('glove').price.gauge === undefined), 'Use the store price clears it');
  ok(!/your price/.test(await p.textContent('details[data-tp="' + tool + '"] summary')), 'summary is back to the store price');

  // owning a tool takes it out of the tier total
  await p.check('[data-tool="' + tool + '"]'); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  const head2 = await p.textContent('#gbTools .ttier:first-child h4');
  ok(head1 !== head2, 'tier total changes when a tool is ticked (' + head1 + ' → ' + head2 + ')');
  ok(/owned/.test(await p.textContent('#gbToolStat')), 'inventory count shown');

  // junk in saved prices is dropped by clean()
  const cleaned = await p.evaluate(() => { const m = window.V60_MODULES.filter(x => x.id === 'glove')[0]; return m.clean({ tools: {}, price: { gauge: '3', jack: -4, torx: 'abc', 'bad key!': 2, stands: '' } }).price; });
  ok(JSON.stringify(cleaned) === '{"gauge":3}', 'clean() keeps only valid prices ' + JSON.stringify(cleaned));

  // the ASE article opens and carries its sources
  await p.evaluate(() => V60.jump('kb:a-ase')); await p.waitForTimeout(300);
  const txt = await p.evaluate(() => document.body.innerText);
  ok(/ASE certification/.test(txt) && /\$34 registration/.test(txt) && /ase\.com/.test(await p.content()), 'ASE article opens with the fee lines and ASE sources');

  ok(errs.length === 0, 'no errors ' + JSON.stringify(errs));
  await b.close();
})();
```

### `tests/track.js`

```javascript
/* The certification track: readiness meters, hands-on-first quiz gating, an area quiz end to end with weak spots,
   the Owner rung, the mock G1 with its clock, and the HUD chip. */
const { chromium } = require(process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_PATH || 'playwright');
const path = require('path'); const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
function ok(c, m) { if (!c) { console.log('FAIL', m); process.exitCode = 1; } else console.log(' ok', m); }
(async () => {
  const b = await chromium.launch(process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH ? { executablePath: process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH } : {});
  const ctx = await b.newContext({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 } }); await ctx.addInitScript(() => { window.__V60_TEST = true; });
  const p = await ctx.newPage(); const errs = []; p.on('pageerror', e => errs.push(e.message)); p.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errs.push(m.text()); });
  await p.goto('file://' + ROOT + '/index.html'); await p.waitForTimeout(600);

  ok(/%$/.test((await p.textContent('#hudRank')).trim()) && /G1/.test(await p.textContent('#hudRankName')), 'the header chip shows G1 readiness instead of a level');
  const D = await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_TRACK_DATA);
  ok(D.areas.reduce((s, a) => s + a.q, 0) === D.test.scored, 'area question counts add up to the scored total (' + D.test.scored + ')');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_QUIZ.every(q => q.o.length === 4 && q.a >= 0 && q.a < 4 && q.src && window.V60_TRACK_DATA.areas.some(a => a.id === q.area))), 'every quiz question has four options, a right one, a source and an area');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_QUIZ.every(q => !q.item || window.V60_MANUAL.data.items.some(it => it.id === q.item))), 'every question points at a real part');

  await p.evaluate(() => V60.jump('track:')); await p.waitForTimeout(200);
  ok(/G1 readiness/.test(await p.textContent('#tkBody')), 'the track page renders');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => document.querySelectorAll('#tkBody [data-area]').length === 7), 'seven areas listed');
  await p.click('#tkBody [data-area="eng"]'); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => !document.querySelector('#tkBody [data-quiz="1"]') && /step \d+ of your path/.test(document.querySelector('#tkBody').textContent)), 'the Engine quiz is locked until the path reaches it');
  /* close every Know and Check chapter of the engine area by faking their evidence, then the quiz opens */
  await p.evaluate(() => { const st = V60.mod('story'); st.all = true; V60.setMod('story', st); const d = V60.mod('manual'); const a = window.V60_TRACK_DATA.areas.filter(x => x.id === 'eng')[0];
    const A = V60.acad(), dy = V60.mod('diy') || { done: {} }, today = V60.todayStr();
    a.items.forEach(id => { const it = window.V60_MANUAL.data.items.filter(x => x.id === id)[0]; it.chapters.forEach(c => { if (c.tier !== 'K' && c.tier !== 'C') return; c.steps.forEach((s, i) => {
      if (s.manual) d.manual[s.manual] = today; else if (s.kb) V60_KNOW.discover('a', s.kb); else if (s.mission) A.done[s.mission] = { date: today, outcome: 'good' }; else if (s.diy) dy.done[s.diy] = today;
      else if (s.oil) { V60.state.oil = V60.state.oil || []; while (V60.state.oil.length < s.oil) V60.state.oil.push({ id: 'o' + V60.state.oil.length, date: today, miles: 91000 + V60.state.oil.length, level: 'ok' }); }
      else if (s.photo) { V60.state.photos = (V60.state.photos || []).concat([{ id: 'ph-' + s.photo, asset: 'x', url: 'data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7', local: false, date: today, kind: s.photo, part: null, note: '', ai: null }]); }
      else if (s.scans) { V60.state.lastScan = { date: today, mil: false, codes: 0 }; const L = V60.mod('live') || { scans: [] }; L.scans = (L.scans || []).concat([{ date: today, sim: false }]); V60.setMod('live', L); }
      else d.went[c.id + ':' + i] = 1; }); }); });
    V60.setMod('diy', dy); V60.save(); window.V60_MANUAL.bust(); V60.jump('track:eng'); });
  await p.waitForTimeout(200);
  const handsTxt = await p.textContent('#tkBody .tk-parts');
  const quizBtn = await p.$('#tkBody [data-quiz="1"]');
  ok(!!quizBtn || /Still to close/.test(await p.textContent('#tkBody')), 'closing hands-on chapters moves the meter (' + handsTxt.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() + ')');
  /* the manual-drivetrain area has no hands-on step on this car: its quiz is open at once */
  await p.evaluate(() => V60.jump('track:mdt')); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  ok(!!(await p.$('#tkBody [data-quiz="1"]')), 'an area with nothing to do on this car opens its quiz straight away');
  await p.click('#tkBody [data-quiz="1"]'); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  const n = await p.evaluate(() => document.querySelectorAll('#tkBody .tk-opt').length);
  ok(n === 4, 'a question shows four options');
  /* answer every question right by reading the bank */
  let guard = 0;
  while (guard++ < 30) {
    const done = await p.evaluate(() => !document.querySelector('#tkBody .tk-opt'));
    if (done) break;
    await p.evaluate(() => { const qText = document.querySelector('#tkBody .tk-q h3').textContent; const q = window.V60_QUIZ.filter(x => x.q === qText)[0] || Object.values(window.V60_G1_ENTRIES || {}).reduce((a, e) => a.concat(e.qs || []), []).filter(x => x.q === qText)[0] || window.V60_FACTS.filter(f => f.q === qText)[0]; const right = q.o ? q.o[q.a] : q.a; const btn = [...document.querySelectorAll('#tkBody .tk-opt')].filter(b => b.textContent.slice(1).trim() === right)[0]; btn.click(); });
    await p.waitForTimeout(80);
    const nxt = await p.$('#tkBody [data-tk="next"]'); if (nxt) { await nxt.click(); await p.waitForTimeout(80); }
  }
  ok(/100 %/.test(await p.textContent('#tkBody .mn-h1')), 'a perfect round scores 100 %');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => { const t = V60.mod('track'); return !!(t.quiz['mdt:1'] && t.quiz['mdt:1'].passed) && window.V60_TRACK.rung('mdt') === 1; }), 'passing the Owner quiz earns the Owner rung for that area');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => window.V60_TRACK.ready() > 0), 'G1 readiness rose above zero');
  /* a wrong answer shows the explanation and the source, and lands in the weak spots */
  await p.evaluate(() => V60.jump('track:eng')); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  const open = await p.$('#tkBody [data-quiz="1"]');
  if (open) {
    await open.click(); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
    await p.evaluate(() => { const qText = document.querySelector('#tkBody .tk-q h3').textContent; const q = window.V60_QUIZ.filter(x => x.q === qText)[0] || Object.values(window.V60_G1_ENTRIES || {}).reduce((a, e) => a.concat(e.qs || []), []).filter(x => x.q === qText)[0] || window.V60_FACTS.filter(f => f.q === qText)[0]; const right = q.o ? q.o[q.a] : q.a; const wrong = [...document.querySelectorAll('#tkBody .tk-opt')].filter(b => b.textContent.slice(1).trim() !== right)[0]; wrong.click(); });
    await p.waitForTimeout(100);
    ok(await p.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('#tkBody .tk-why.bad a[href]') && !!document.querySelector('#tkBody .tk-opt.right')), 'a miss shows the right answer, the explanation and a source link');
    await p.click('#tkBody [data-tk="quit"]'); await p.waitForTimeout(100);
  } else console.log(' .. engine quiz still locked here (some Know/Check evidence is not fakeable); skipped the miss check');
  /* the mock G1: 55 drawn in proportion when the bank allows, a clock, a score report by area */
  await p.evaluate(() => V60.jump('track:')); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  await p.click('#tkBody [data-mock]'); await p.waitForTimeout(200);
  ok(/\d+:\d\d/.test(await p.textContent('#tkClock')), 'the mock G1 shows a clock');
  const total = await p.evaluate(() => +document.querySelector('#tkBody .tk-q .mn-kick span').textContent.replace(/.*OF /, ''));
  ok(total > 30 && total <= 55, 'the mock draws from every area (' + total + ' questions)');
  for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) { await p.click('#tkBody .tk-opt:first-child'); await p.waitForTimeout(20); }
  await p.waitForTimeout(200);
  ok(/SCORE REPORT/.test(await p.textContent('#tkBody')) && await p.evaluate(() => document.querySelectorAll('#tkBody [data-area]').length === 7), 'the mock ends with a score report by area');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => (V60.mod('track').g1.tries || 0) === 1), 'the mock attempt is saved');
  /* the home strip */
  await p.evaluate(() => __v60.go('car')); await p.waitForTimeout(150);
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => !document.querySelector('#mnHome .tk-strip') && !!document.querySelector('#mnHome .mn-next .mn-pbar')), 'the home carries one Next card with the path progress, not the readiness strip');
  ok(errs.length === 0, 'no errors ' + JSON.stringify(errs));
  await b.close();
})();
```

### `tests/update.js`

```javascript
/* Updates without a service worker (Bluefy on iPhone has none): the page compares its version with version.json.
   - the header's Version chip shows when this copy was built; tapping it checks now
   - opening the app when a newer version exists updates by itself, once (no reload loop if a cache serves the old page)
   - once you have tapped something, a newer version is offered with the bar instead, and Refresh loads it */
const { chromium } = require(process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_PATH || 'playwright');
const http = require('http'), fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'); const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
function ok(c, m) { if (!c) { console.log('FAIL', m); process.exitCode = 1; } else console.log(' ok', m); }
const TYPES = { '.html': 'text/html', '.js': 'text/javascript', '.css': 'text/css', '.json': 'application/json', '.png': 'image/png', '.webmanifest': 'application/manifest+json' };
let published = null; /* what the server says version.json holds; null = the real file */
const srv = http.createServer((q, r) => {
  const u = q.url.split('?')[0];
  if (u === '/version.json' && published) { r.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); return r.end(JSON.stringify({ v: published })); }
  const f = path.join(ROOT, decodeURIComponent(u === '/' ? '/index.html' : u));
  fs.readFile(f, (e, d) => { if (e) { r.writeHead(404); return r.end(); } r.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': TYPES[path.extname(f)] || 'application/octet-stream' }); r.end(d); });
}).listen(0, '127.0.0.1');
(async () => {
  await new Promise(r => srv.on('listening', r));
  const base = 'http://127.0.0.1:' + srv.address().port + '/';
  const b = await chromium.launch(process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH ? { executablePath: process.env.CHROMIUM_PATH } : {});
  const errs = [];
  async function open() {
    const ctx = await b.newContext({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 }, serviceWorkers: 'block' }); await ctx.addInitScript(() => { window.__V60_TEST = true; });
    const p = await ctx.newPage(); p.on('pageerror', e => errs.push(e.message));
    p.loads = 0; p.on('load', () => { p.loads++; });
    return p;
  }
  const mine = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'version.json'), 'utf8')).v;
  const newer = mine.replace(/-[0-9a-f]+$/, '-ffffffff');

  /* 1. up to date: the chip, a manual check */
  let p = await open();
  await p.goto(base + 'index.html'); await p.waitForTimeout(2600);
  const chip = () => p.textContent('#verChip');
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => document.getElementById('updateBar').hidden) && p.loads === 1, 'same version: no bar, no reload');
  ok(await p.isVisible('#verChip') && /^Version [A-Z][a-z]{2} \d{1,2}, \d{1,2}:\d{2}/.test(await chip()), 'the header shows the version as a date and time: ' + await chip());
  ok(await p.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth), 'the header still fits a 390-wide phone');
  await p.click('#verChip'); await p.waitForTimeout(500);
  ok(/^Up to date/.test(await chip()), 'tapping it checks now: ' + await chip());

  /* 2. in use: a newer version is offered, not forced */
  published = newer;
  await p.click('#verChip'); await p.waitForTimeout(500);
  ok(await p.isVisible('#updateBar') && /^New version ready/.test(await chip()) && p.loads === 1, 'while in use, a newer version shows the bar: ' + await chip());
  const nav = p.waitForNavigation({ timeout: 10000 }).catch(() => null);
  await p.click('#updateBar button'); await nav; await p.waitForTimeout(800);
  ok(p.loads === 2 && await p.evaluate(() => !!window.V60_VERSION), 'Refresh reloads the app');
  ok(!/[?&]u=/.test(p.url()), 'the cache-busting address is tidied away after the reload (' + p.url() + ')');
  await p.context().close();

  /* 3. opening the app with a newer version waiting: it updates by itself, once */
  published = newer;
  p = await open();
  await p.goto(base + 'index.html'); await p.waitForTimeout(5500);
  ok(p.loads === 2, 'opened with a newer version waiting: reloaded by itself (' + p.loads + ' loads)');
  ok(await p.isVisible('#updateBar') && !/[?&]u=/.test(p.url()), 'the server still has the old page: no loop, the bar is offered instead');
  await p.context().close();

  /* 4. a tap before the check: no automatic reload */
  published = mine.replace(/-[0-9a-f]+$/, '-eeeeeeee');
  p = await open();
  await p.goto(base + 'index.html'); await p.waitForTimeout(300); await p.mouse.click(5, 400); await p.waitForTimeout(2600);
  ok(p.loads === 1 && await p.isVisible('#updateBar'), 'after a tap it waits for you: bar shown, no reload');

  ok(errs.length === 0, 'no page errors ' + JSON.stringify(errs));
  await b.close(); srv.close();
})();
```

### `docs/GAME_DESIGN.md`

```markdown
# V60 Garage: how the game works

## The path (2026-10-15): one line, one step at a time
Kyle's brief: "one seed planted of info turns into a tree of knowledge but potentially more linear", without so many ways in that it overwhelms. His answers: strict (later steps stay locked), in the order a beginner learns a car, and the home cut down to the car, one next step and a progress bar.

- **The path** (`src/js/data/path.js`) is 113 steps in 18 units: 1 Safety first; 2 What the car is telling you; 3 The car's history and recalls; 4 Under the hood: the fluids; 5 Tires, the tire light and steering; 6 Brakes; 7 The diagnostic port; 8 Battery, fuses, lights and wipers; 9 The engine; 10 Transmission and driveline; 11 Heating and A/C; 12 Inside and out; 13 First jobs; 14 Shop jobs on record; 15 Diagnose: lights and codes; 16 Diagnose: sounds, feel and fluids; 17 Upgrades; 18 The Technician quizzes and the mock G1.
- **The order:** safety, then what this car is telling you and its history (bought as-is), then Know and Check one system at a time. Each system ends with its G1 study (ASE's tasks in ranges of 5 to 17) and its Owner quiz. Then Service (easiest jobs first), Diagnose, Upgrade, and the test. Every chapter and every G1 task is on the path exactly once; each quiz comes after the chapters and tasks it tests (`tests/path.js`).
- **Strict.** Only the current step is open. A chapter, a study range, a quiz and the mock all wait for the step before. Evidence still counts whenever it comes in: a step already done when the path reaches it is passed straight over.
- **Set aside.** A step that needs a shop, a purchase or a dealer (`park` in the data: the specialist inspection in 1.4.2, the oil change record, the timing belt, the transmission fluid, the S29842 dealer check) can be set aside from the Next card. The path moves on; the step stays listed under the card and closes by itself once its evidence arrives. For the track, a chapter set aside counts as hands-on done.
- **Home:** the Next card first (step, unit, title, what it is, one button, a progress bar, anything set aside, a waiting scene), then the car figure (tapping a locked view says which step opens it), the Index button and the red "Something's wrong" list. Gone from the home: the view sheet, the chapter 0 sheet, the Now strip and the readiness strip.
- **The whole path** (Index, or "The whole path" on the Next card): done units folded, the current unit open with its steps, later units by name only.
- **The bar:** The car, Glovebox, Link. Glovebox and Link are workbenches and always open. Cases (with Options) moved into the Index.
- **The story** no longer opens anything. Cases still close from evidence and scenes still play; the case board's next objective points at the path, and a case step past the current one shows "PATH STEP n" instead of Go. The guided walkthrough has no button for now (it followed the story's order); porting it onto path steps is on the roadmap.
- The rest of this file predates the path. Where it says chapters open each other (`opens`) or a case opens a chapter early, the path replaced that.

## The manual (redesign, Oct 2026): the car is the menu
Kyle's brief: an app a car person would want, not "an app Claude designed". Look at the car, tap a part, get that part's manual, and watch chapters unlock in order of difficulty. Mockup: the Design artifact "V60 Garage redesign mockup".

- **Home ("The car")** is a side-view figure with five numbered points, one per **view**: 1 Engine bay (hood open), 2 Wheels & brakes (the wheel), 3 Cabin (inside), 4 Underside, 5 Lights & body (walk-around). Tapping a point shows a sheet (where you stand, what is next) and an Open button into that view. Below: a Now strip (pick up here, urgent health items, a waiting scene), the contents list, the back matter (every old page the gate allows), and the red "Something's wrong" list.
- **A view** is a figure with numbered **items** (1.3 is the battery). The figure is a schematic drawing until the owner picks one of their own photos as the figure; the points start where they sit on the drawing and are dragged into place once ("Move points"). Positions are saved per view.
- **An item** is one part's manual: up to five **chapters** in order of difficulty, K Know it, C Check it, S Service it, D Diagnose it, U Upgrade it. Only chapters with sourced content exist. An item page shows "Your car" specs (from the car's data and the owner's photo readings, marked unconfirmed), the chapters, a glossary of facts by topic (locked terms show as black boxes), and evidence photos.
- **A chapter** is a short procedure: numbered steps that are things done on the car and in the app (a Training lesson, a Library article, a DIY job, a troubleshooter, a photo, a record, a real scan, a receipt, a bulletin mark, an upgrade decision). Since 2026-10-15 chapters are sections of the part page and each step opens in place: the article, the lesson, the job and the troubleshooter render inside the step, so reading never leaves the part. Steps that need a workbench (the Service log, Live link, photos, bulletins) keep a Go button; the crumb bar on that page leads back. Steps whose only evidence is "you went there" can also be confirmed by hand. A chapter closes when every step is done; it gets a dated stamp.
- **Unlocking, both ways.** The chapter before it in the same item opens the next one. A closed chapter can open chapters elsewhere (`opens`), at most two at a time so the car never lights up everywhere. A story case that is available opens its item's first chapter early (`caseOpens`): The Signal opens 3.3 the port, The Belt opens 1.4, The Thirst 1.1, The Light 2.1, The Paper Trail 3.5. Chapter 0, Before you touch anything (the Safe to Touch missions), opens 1.1 and 1.2; nothing else opens before it closes.
- **Two markers, by Kyle's choice.** Amber glow = a chapter is open and has never been opened; it stops the first time the chapter page is shown. Amber dot = the one chapter you last opened and have not closed ("pick up here"). Both roll up from chapter to item to view, so the home shows at a glance where something new is and where you left off.
- **The gate.** An old page (Library, DIY, Troubleshoot, Bulletins, Data lab, ...) is reachable once an open chapter's step points at it, or once the story reveals it as before. The bar always shows four roots: The car, Cases, Glovebox, Link; Glovebox and Link are drawn locked until 3.5 or The Paper Trail, and 3.3 or The Signal.
- **The story moves into the Cases drawer** (the Story tab). Each case still closes from evidence; the manual's chapters reuse the same evidence, so a chapter page says which case step it is.
- **Instruments stay instruments.** Live link and the Data lab keep gauges and teal traces.
- **Look.** A workshop manual: paper and ink, hairline rules, numbered sections, condensed display type (Barlow Condensed), IBM Plex Sans body, IBM Plex Mono numbers and labels. Square corners, no shadows, one accent (amber) that only ever means new. Light and dark.
- **Not built yet:** wheel and underside figures are schematic only; the Cases page keeps its old layout inside the new dress; Today's cards (guide announcements, welcome back) live under Back matter, Today's notes.


The app is a real-life game about one car. The main story, "The As-Is File", drives everything. On day one almost nothing is visible. Each case you open reveals the tools it needs, and finishing acts unlocks side content. Every objective is something done on or for the real car, then recorded in the app.

## Start
- Visible: **Today** (home), **Story**, the **Ask** bar (offline answers about the car), and the red **Something's wrong with the car** button. The button is always there and goes straight to the right troubleshooting guide, whatever the story progress.
- The prologue scene introduces the car (bought as-is, no records), the adapter (a box that speaks the car's language), and Lars, a fictional retired Volvo tech who narrates. Every fact he states is sourced elsewhere in the app.

## Story and Training
- **Story is the only place you play.** Each case says what to do on the real car and in what order.
- **Training is the how-to library behind the cases.** It used to be a separate "Academy" tab, which made it look like a second story. It is no longer in the menu. A step's **Lesson** button opens the matching lesson, which shows "Training for <case>" and a **Back to the case** button. Finishing the lesson ticks that step automatically.
- To browse every lesson, Story has a **Training library** link (with a count of lessons done).

## Guided mode (guide.js): strong help at first, then it lets go
- **Five areas, each with its own level:**
  - under the hood (Safe to Touch, The Thirst, First Wrench)
  - the adapter (The Signal, Baseline)
  - records and papers (The Belt, The Paper Trail)
  - tires (The Light That Won't Go Out)
  - reading data (Sixth Sense)
- **Level 0, Guided.** The next objective shows **Start**, which opens a full-screen walkthrough:
  - It first asks "Are you at the car right now?" once a day. When the answer is no, steps that need the car are skipped in favor of ones that don't.
  - Each screen shows one step, with why it matters, how to do it, and one big action: open the lesson, do it in the app, or Done for steps only the owner can confirm. "Show me where" opens the engine bay map.
  - Hands-on steps first need a four-item safety check, from the owner's manual rules already in Safe to Touch.
  - **I'm stuck** works as a ladder: a hint, then the lesson and the map, then "Can't do it now" (log a known risk) or "Show a different step".
  - Leaving to do a step in the app leaves a pill that leads back. When the step is done, the next screen starts with what was just finished.
- **Level 1, Assisted.** The case board as usual, with a "Walk me through it" button.
- **Level 2, On your own.** No extra prompting.
- **Levels rise from proof, not time.** Each counts as one point in its area:
  - a step finished in the walkthrough without "I'm stuck"
  - a right answer in a case debrief
  - an oil check, record, receipt, real scan or saved drive logged without being led there

  Level 1 needs 4 points and level 2 needs 10. Closed cases count 3 each, so existing progress starts at the right level.
- **Levels drop** after two stuck steps in a row in an area, or after 45+ days away. A long gap also brings a "Welcome back" recap on Today.
- **Every change is announced on Today by Lars,** with a **Keep guiding me** button that pins that area to guided (Kyle chose "just do it", 2026-10-11).
- **While any area is guided, a newly opened tab shows a one-line intro once.** The **Guide me** button in the header always opens the walkthrough.

## Cases (main story)
Each case has:
- a **briefing**: why it matters on this car, time, cost, tools, the risk if skipped, and sources
- **steps**: each with a Go button to the exact place in the app, sometimes a **Where** button that highlights the part on the engine bay map, and a few "Mark done" steps only you can confirm
- a **status**: Unknown → Lead (started) → Evidence (proof is coming in) → Closed
- a **debrief** when closed: what was found, in numbers where possible, plus a short scene and three quiz questions ("Check yourself")

Cases close from real evidence, not from tapping "done". If a case can't be finished yet (money, a shop appointment), "Can't close it yet?" logs it as a **known risk**. That keeps the story moving, but the case stays flagged in red and the finale names it.

| Act | Case | What closes it | What it reveals |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Arrival | Safe to Touch | Safety, hood and landmark lessons | Engine bay |
| 1 | The Signal | A real health check with the adapter, plus 5 decoded signals | Live link |
| | *Act 1 complete* | | Whole car map, Health score, Flashcards |
| 2 The Unknowns | The Belt | A logged timing belt record | Service log, Glovebox |
| 2 | The Thirst | Oil checks logged across 1,000 miles | Fuel & costs |
| 2 | The Light That Won't Go Out | Calibrated and the light stays off, or escalated with bulletin TJ29818 | DIY jobs, Troubleshoot |
| 2 | The Paper Trail | Recalls settled, build month entered, spark plug service action checked | Bulletins, My V60, Library |
| | *Act 2 complete* | | Side missions: achievements, seasonal events |
| 3 The Voice | Baseline | A real scan plus three saved drives | Data lab |
| | *Act 3 complete* | | Side mission: Simulator and mystery cars |
| 4 Ownership | First Wrench | First DIY job done | Upgrades |
| 4 | Sixth Sense | The stop-or-go final | Diagnose, plus side mission: Career shop jobs |
| | *Act 4 complete* | | The V60 Master exam |
| Finale | Master of the V60 | Six critical cases closed and the exam passed | Everything |

Within an act, the next case appears once you've started the current one. The next act appears when every case in the current act is closed.

After the finale, the story keeps going as **new cases**. Anything urgent the app detects becomes a case: a new code in a scan, an MPG drop, readiness lost, a bulletin symptom you marked, or a renewal coming due.

## The Codebook (the cipher)
The adapter's output starts as raw labels: "PID 0C", "MONITOR 04", "Encoded fault". Tapping **Decode** opens a card. The meaning resolves on screen, and the card explains what the signal measures and what it means on this car, with a source. From then on that label shows in plain words everywhere. There are no puzzles: one tap, once.

Decoding your first trouble code teaches the four parts every code is built from: letter, generic or Volvo-specific, subsystem, exact fault. After that, codes show their meaning straight away. The Codebook view lists all 30 entries: decoded, heard but not decoded yet, and not heard yet. Safety readings are never hidden: whether the check-engine light is on, emissions pass or fail, and the summary.

## The File
A dossier that builds itself from what you log:
- the car's identity, mileage and build month
- findings from closed cases
- service history and the oil consumption rate
- the latest health check
- recalls, marked bulletins, receipts and renewal dates
- known risks
- Codebook progress

It can be printed or saved as a PDF for a mechanic or a buyer. It never shows the VIN.

## Knowledge unlocks
Library articles and flashcards open with the case that uses them, marked "New entry". The Ask bar still answers anything at any time, and whatever you look up is added to your Library and card deck.

## Side missions
None of these block the story. They appear one by one as acts finish: Flashcards, DIY jobs, Fuel log, Photo mapping, Upgrades, Achievements and seasonal checklists, Simulator mystery cars, Career shop jobs.

## The certification track (replaces XP, ranks, the skill tree and the V60 Master exam, 2026-10-15)
Kyle may sit ASE's G1 (Auto Maintenance and Light Repair) one day, so progression is the G1's own shape: seven content areas with the study guide's question counts (Engine 9, Automatic transmission 4, Manual drivetrain & axles 6, Suspension & steering 13, Brakes 11, Electrical 8, HVAC 4; 55 scored of 65, 90 minutes). Each area is a level with two rungs:
- **Owner:** every part in the area has its Know and Check chapters closed on the car, then the Owner quiz is passed (10 questions, 70 %, the app's bar; ASE does not publish its pass mark). Manual drivetrain has no hands-on step on this car (no clutch, no gearbox), so its quiz opens at once and says so.
- **Technician:** every chapter closed, then the Technician quiz (diagnosis questions).
- **Readiness** per area = 40 % hands-on + 20 % flashcards mastered + 40 % best quiz score; the G1 number weights the areas as the test does. The header chip and the home strip show it.
- **Quizzes open hands-on first** (Kyle's choice): reading alone cannot level you up. Questions are original, in the styles ASE's guides show (scenario, most likely, EXCEPT, Technician A/B), each grounded in a sourced fact; misses show the answer, the explanation and the source, and land in weak spots that link back to the part.
- **Mock G1:** 55 questions drawn in the test's proportions (fewer while the bank is short), a 90-minute clock, a score report by area. A pass counts toward the finale once every area is at Owner; before that it is a practice score.
- **Perks:** Mechanic detail level after the first Owner rung; the Timeline after three services or receipts.

## Skill tree (retired 2026-10-15; kept for the record)
Four branches, each node earned by evidence already logged elsewhere. A branch builds tier by tier.
- **Hands-on:** Under the hood, Fluids, Tires, Wrench
- **Diagnostics:** Listener, Decoder, Data reader, Diagnostician
- **Knowledge:** Reader, Scholar, Certified
- **Ownership:** Record keeper, Paper trail, Budgeter
- **Master tech** (capstone): Tires, Data reader, Certified and Budgeter all earned

Three nodes grant perks that open features: Record keeper opens the **Timeline** view, Scholar opens the **Mechanic** detail level, and Data reader opens **Drive mode** in Live link. Each node is worth 25 XP, and the capstone 100.

## Progress and rewards
- **XP and rank:** the level chip in the header. XP comes from Training lessons and field missions, closed cases (40 each, 10 for a known risk, 150 for the finale), correct debrief answers (5 each), decoded signals (3 each), DIY jobs, receipts, scans, trips and more.
- **Achievements:** 18 real-proof badges, such as logging three oil checks, verifying the belt or passing the exam.
- **Scenes:** each closure or new case is a short scene. Scenes wait on Today until you watch them, and any scene can be replayed from Story, then Scenes.

## Around the app
- **Garage map (Today):** a top-down drawing of the car. Areas light up as the story opens them; tap one to go there.
- **Car pulse (header):** three dots, always visible: warning light or codes, last oil check, and the most urgent service item.
- **Swipeable Today** on phones, one card at a time.
- **Listen** buttons read briefings, decode cards, Library articles and DIY jobs aloud.
- **Proof photos:** a Photo button on every case step attaches a picture, shown on the step and in The File.
- **Cold open:** on first launch a short mystery teaser plays once, before the prologue.
- **Sync** (Story, then Options): every device shares the same progress through a private GitHub repository. Each device needs the repository name and a fine-grained token once. Photos sync too. The Claude version can't reach GitHub and stays separate.
- **Protect your progress card** on Today: appears when sync is off and there has been no backup for 14 days.
- **Monthly iPhone reminder** for the oil and tire check (in the Reminders app, created from Claude).

## Options (Story, then Options)
- **Detail level:** Short, Detailed or Mechanic. Mechanic adds part numbers, specs and bulletin details to briefings and steps.
- **Plain readings:** skips decoding in Live link.
- **Show everything:** skips the reveal and shows every tab.
```

### `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md`

````markdown
# Working on V60 Garage from your own computer

The GitHub repo is the whole project. Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` when it opens the folder, so there is nothing
else to prepare: clone, open, work, push.

Kyle is on Windows. Commands below are for PowerShell (right-click the Start button, then Terminal). Where the project's
other docs say `python3`, type `python` on Windows.

## 1. One-time setup
1. Install Git for Windows (git-scm.com, defaults are fine) and Python 3.12 or newer from python.org. In the Python installer tick "Add python.exe to PATH". Check in a new terminal: `git --version` and `python --version`.
2. Install Claude Code following Anthropic's Windows instructions at https://docs.claude.com (search "Claude Code"). Sign in with the same account you use here.
3. Clone the repo into a folder you will keep. Desktop is fine:
   ```
   cd $HOME\Desktop
   git clone https://github.com/bmcdoorz94/V60-Link.git
   ```
   That creates `Desktop\V60-Link` with the source (`src/`), tools, tests, docs and the built site.
4. Tell Git who you are, once:
   ```
   git config --global user.name "bmcdoorz94"
   git config --global user.email "kfitz719@gmail.com"
   ```
   The first push will ask you to sign in to GitHub (a browser window opens). Installing the GitHub CLI (`gh auth login`) makes that painless.

## 2. Each session
1. Open the folder in Claude Code (`cd $HOME\Desktop\V60-Link` then `claude`, or open the folder from the Claude desktop app's Code tab).
2. First message of a session, every time:
   > Read CLAUDE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md and docs/HANDOFF_STATE.md, pull the latest from GitHub, and tell me where things stand in plain words. Then wait for me.
   After that, say what you want in plain words, the same as here. Claude Code already knows the rules from `CLAUDE.md`: ask clarifying questions, cite sources, explain changes, build, test, push.
3. Claude builds with `python3 tools/build.py` and pushes to `main`; GitHub Pages serves it a minute or two later at https://bmcdoorz94.github.io/V60-Link/ (the `handoff` branch is rebuilt by GitHub at the same time).

## 3. Preview before pushing (optional)
```
python tools/build.py
python -m http.server 8000
```
then open http://localhost:8000 in a browser on the same computer. Bluetooth (Live link) still needs Bluefy on the phone.

## 4. Tests on your computer (optional)
Needs Node 20 or newer (nodejs.org). Then, once, inside the folder:
```
npm install
npx playwright install chromium webkit
```
Then `npm test` builds the app and runs every test twice: in Chromium, and in WebKit dressed as an iPhone (the engine Bluefy runs on, so iPhone-only problems show up here). It prints one line per test and the full output of anything that failed; screenshots land in `tests/shots/` (the iPhone ones end in `-iphone.png`). `node tests/run.js manual story` runs only those tests, `--webkit` or `--chromium` only one engine, `--no-build` skips the build. A single test also runs on its own: `node tests/regression.js` (no `PLAYWRIGHT_PATH` or `CHROMIUM_PATH` needed locally; those are only for the cloud session). `tests/scan.js`, `tests/tire.js` and `tests/docs.js` download Tesseract or pdf.js from jsDelivr the first time.

The repo pins LF line endings (`.gitattributes`) and the Python tools write UTF-8 with LF, so a build on Windows produces the same files as GitHub's build.

## 5. Things to keep straight
- Edit only `src/`, `tools/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `CLAUDE.md`. The root `index.html`, `js/`, `sw.js`, `link.html` and `dist-artifact/` are build output and are regenerated by the build (locally or by the GitHub Action).
- Pull before you start (`git pull --rebase -X theirs origin main`; the first-message prompt above asks Claude to do it): the GitHub Action commits build output after every push, so your copy is behind by one commit most of the time.
- Never put the VIN, plate or chassis number in any file. The repo is public.
- Photos and documents you give Claude locally stay on your computer unless Claude is asked to add them to the app; the app itself blacks out personal details before storing anything.
- The cloud Claude session, Claude Code on your computer and a Gemini handoff all work from the same repo, so you can switch between them freely as long as each one pushes before you move on.
````

## Photo batch upload and duplicates (Oct 2026)
- Done: several photos at once with one tagging screen; "Let the reader decide" uses the on-device text read (door/hood labels, tire sidewalls); everything else lands under "Something else" unless tagged.
- Done: duplicate guard. Each saved photo stores a SHA-256 of the original file and of the stored copy, plus a 64-bit look-alike print. An identical photo is never added again (single pick, batch, or a second device through sync). A look-alike is flagged and the owner chooses. Photos saved before this change have no fingerprint, so they cannot be matched.
- Not built: recognising what a photo shows from its picture alone (engine bay vs seats). It needs a downloaded image model; accuracy on this car is untested. Open question for Kyle.

# Getting started with cars and trucks (Sept 2026)

Chat on claude.ai, about 2026-09-10: https://claude.ai/chat/1fb6f07f-ec0c-4bd1-bd56-158df4abb0af (private to Kyle). Where the V60 project began. The VIN Kyle gave is left out on purpose.

## What Kyle said
- He wants an involved interest in cars and trucks, mainly to know his own vehicle. American Truck Simulator got him interested.
- He knew nothing yet, "from things like fixing a peeling window tint or what kind of engine is what".
- His car: a 2016 Volvo V60 T5.
- "I guess I should know as much as I can about it."
- He thinks the badge is "just T5" (no AWD badge), which settled front-wheel drive.
- He asked whether the information was for his vehicle specifically, then what information would make it specific, and whether that meant his VIN.
- He asked how to find his vehicle's own owner's manual online, then asked Claude to try the lookup for him.

## Facts established (all now in the app)
- Engine B4204T11, 2.0 L four-cylinder turbo (Drive-E), 240 hp at 5,600 rpm, 258 lb-ft from 1,500 to 4,500 rpm, bore 82 mm, stroke 93.2 mm. Source: the 2016 V60 owner's manual Kyle uploaded (MY16 web edition, TP 20238). In the app: facts f-engine, f-hp, f-tq, f-bore.
- Front-wheel drive, 8-speed automatic. In the app: f-drive and the transmission article.
- The owner's manual is the generic MY16 V60 edition, not tied to one VIN. Volvo keeps the maintenance intervals in a separate Warranty and Service Records booklet, and the oil spec on a label under the hood. In the app: a-schedule, and the hood-label row on 1.1 Oil.

## Said in that chat, corrected or not used since
- "In 2016, T5 AWD meant the 2.5 L five-cylinder with a 6-speed" was said without a source. Volvo's "2016 V60: What's New" release lists the V60 T5 AWD as "Model discontinued" for 2016 (https://mb.cision.com/Main/23622/4196507/3563273.pdf). Not in the app.
- Oil "usually 0W-30 or 5W-30" was generic. Volvo's manual and Kyle's hood label give ACEA A5/B5 5W-30, with Volvo 0W-20 also approved (1.1 Oil in the app).
- The oil-consumption extended warranty (8 years or 100,000 miles) was raised here. The app's oil-program article covers it from Volvo's own documents and notes it has very likely expired on this car by age.
- Forum and YouTube suggestions (SwedeSpeed, ChrisFix and others) and the list of "known weak points" (A/C, struts, electrics) had no sources and were not used.

## Open from this chat
- Volvo's support site only takes a VIN through an interactive form, which Claude could not fill in. Kyle can enter the VIN himself, or ask a Volvo dealer for the Warranty and Service Records booklet. Not done as far as the record shows.

# v60 log file upload (2026-10-14)

Chat on claude.ai: https://claude.ai/chat/718a4ddb-f7b7-4d15-a0ec-54f19e845d8e (private to Kyle). Two turns.

## What Kyle said
- He uploaded the Live link recording `v60-log-2026-10-14_1523.csv` and asked for it to go "in the v60 chat". A chat cannot pass files to another chat, so it was read there instead. The same file was analysed again in the main build chat (see 2026-10-non-work-ideas.md).

## What the recording showed (Kyle's car, his own data)
- Long-term fuel trim, bank 1: +22 to +24 % at idle; about 0 to -3 % under load and at speed.
- Short-term fuel trim at idle swung between about -20 % and +9 % in a cycle of roughly 10 seconds.
- Idle air flow 2.5 to 3.0 g/s at about 900 rpm, manifold pressure 44 to 48 kPa.
- Coolant 84 to 85 °C; voltage steady at 13.5 to 13.7 V.

## Reading given
- Lean at idle but near normal under load points to unmetered air (a vacuum leak, the crankcase ventilation hose, an intake boot or the brake booster line) more than to fuel delivery. Suggested next step: a smoke test of the intake and crankcase, or a look at the PCV hose and the oil cap. No source was cited in this chat; the app's Codebook entry on fuel trims states the same pattern with a source.
- The same day's health check found P0171 stored and pending (main chat). Whether the code has cleared since is not on record.

## In the app now
- Added 2026-10-15 to 3.3 The diagnostic port, "Your car": the health check result, the freeze frame and these log readings, with the lean code's status marked unconfirmed.

### `docs/chats/2026-10-15-ase.md`

```markdown
# ASE certification tiers (2026-10-15)

Chat on claude.ai: https://claude.ai/chat/ac671e44-e808-4efb-b2da-d14777a858fa (private to Kyle). Pay figures and personal details are left out on purpose.

## What Kyle said
- He asked for everything about ASE: tiers, costs, what they accomplish, and whether it is a viable option for him.
- "Cars seem interesting as of recently", and asked what certified people earn.
- "I just see things that seem interesting to me and am curious about them."
- Asked what pulls at him most: "Maintaining my own but other cars interest me as well."
- Said yes to both offers: a monthly walkaround checklist and a starter tool list. Claude built them as one claude.ai page, "V60 Walkaround" (an OK/Flag sheet with a mileage log, and three tool tiers with rough prices).

## Facts given, with sources (now in the app)
- ASE is a voluntary certification, not a license: pass a test and have matching work experience; credentials last five years. Tiers: Entry-Level (students), Professional tests (A1 to A9, G1 and others), Master (a full series, A1 to A8 for autos), Advanced Level L1 to L4.
- 2026 fees: $34 registration per order plus $62 per general test and $124 per Advanced Level test; G1 alone $96; A1 to A8 in one order $530; 90 days to test; in person at Prometric centers.
- Experience categories ASE lists; passing without them gives a score report, not a certification.
- Sources: ASE, Register Now (https://ase.com/tests/register-now/) and Work Experience (https://ase.com/tests/work-experience/). In the app: the ASE article (a-ase).
- ASE's free study guides work as a map of the car's systems, with the V60 as the reference object. This became the certification track and the G1 study entries.

## Decisions taken in the V60 Garage session that followed (same day)
- Kyle chose to bring in the ASE reference article and the tool list with prices from real stores that he can override. Store prices live in src/js/data/toolprices.js.
- Not brought in, by his choice: the pay figures, the OK/Flag walkaround sheet with its mileage log, and the video channel list.
- The chat said "Volvos use Torx fasteners heavily" without a source; the app does not state it.
```

### 2. Facts about the car established

- t12, t54: Kyle owns an OBD adapter. At t54 he says he already has it; the OBDLink CX is the model discussed from t17 on.
- t15: No dipstick; oil level is read electronically in the instrument cluster (ignition in mode II, thumb wheel on the left stalk to "Oil level"). Dipsticks are only on the five- and six-cylinder V60s. Source: Volvo, checking oil, 2016 V60, https://www.volvocars.com/us/support/car/v60/2016/article/527f24d2b96b2c38c0a801e8000aafe8
- t15: Hood release: a handle under the left side of the dash, turned about 20-25 degrees clockwise, then the catch near the front-right edge of the hood is pushed left. Source: Volvo, opening the hood, 2016 V60, https://www.volvocars.com/us/support/car/v60/2016/article/f2de677bb96926f2c0a801e801c6ec9e
- t15: Recommended tire pressures are on the driver's door pillar. The OBD-II port is under the dash on the driver's side, tagged "verify" (no source).
- t16: Odometer about 95,000 miles (Kyle's estimate, give or take 5k), October 2026.
- t20: Bought from an independent lot, probably "as is", at a little under 90,000 miles.
- t22: Bought about 14 months before 2026-10-10, recorded in CLAUDE.md (t47) as about August 2025. Oil changed recently. Tire pressure light always on with tires inflated.
- t22/t47: No service history is known; the timing belt history is unknown.
- t31 (NHTSA vPIC decode, https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/):
  - 2016 V60 wagon, Premier trim (SV33)
  - B4204T11 2.0 L four-cylinder turbo (Drive-E), 240 hp
  - ULEV, engine stop/start, front-wheel drive, 8-speed automatic
  - indirect tire pressure monitoring (no wheel sensors)
  - built at Volvo's Torslanda plant, Sweden
  - front, seat-cushion and curtain airbags (rows 1 and 2)
- t31: Recalls listed for the 2016 V60 model year (NHTSA recalls API, https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls). Whether each applies to his VIN was left for him to check.
  - 20V378000 (Volvo R10029): front seat belt anchor cable
  - 19V849000 (R89978): door latches
  - 16V798000 (R89708): front passenger buckle stud, cars built Feb 16, 2015 to Aug 22, 2016
  - 15V555000 (R39574): starter motor fuse on stop/start, cars built Apr 8 to Aug 19, 2015
- t33: From the VIN decode, the tire monitor is indirect, so the always-on light is "almost certainly" a calibration issue, not a broken sensor.
- t34: Engine bay layout. Source: Volvo 2016 V60 US Owner's Manual, https://ldgsvccassets.blob.core.windows.net/pdfs/610e4b1a5665ac4d99bd89bd1971f063df1c7284/V60_OwnersManual_MY16_en-US_TP20238.pdf
  - Brake fluid reservoir and washer filler on the driver side.
  - Battery in the engine bay under two covers, with the fuse box beside it.
  - Jump-start ground point at the passenger-side engine mount.
  - Radiator at the front; hood catch near the front-right edge.
  - No power steering fluid (electric steering).
  - The coolant tank and air box positions could not be confirmed.
- t34: Spec sheet. Sources: the Volvo 2016 V60 US Owner's Manual (above) and the Volvo 2016 Maintenance Schedule, https://www.volvocars.com/images/cs/v3/assets/bltccbab8edae0354cd/bltd8992f59bb25d587/684189d0f08427b79f2c3893/2016-Volvo-Maintenance-Schedule-v1.pdf?branch=prod_alias
  - Engine: B4204T11, 1,969 cc, bore and stroke 82 x 93.2 mm, compression 10.8:1, 240 hp at 5,600 rpm, 258 lb-ft at 1,500-4,500 rpm, timing belt.
  - Oil: full synthetic ACEA A5/B5 SAE 5W-30. Volvo's 0W-20 (VCC RBS0-2AE) is also approved. 6.2 US qt (5.9 L) with the filter.
  - Coolant: Volvo coolant, 50/50 with water, 8.7 US qt.
  - Transmission: Volvo AW1 fluid, about 7 US qt. Volvo says no change is needed in normal use.
  - Brake fluid: DOT 4, 0.63 US qt.
  - Washer fluid: 6.8 US qt (4.7 without headlight washers).
  - A/C: R134a, 1.7 lb, PAG oil.
  - Tires: 215/50R17 on 17 x 7.5 in wheels, 38 psi front and rear cold. Tire size source: https://tiresize.com/tires/Volvo/V60/2016/T5-FWD/
  - Wheel bolts: 103 lb-ft (140 Nm), tightened crosswise.
  - Battery: 12 V AGM, 800 CCA, required on start/stop cars.
  - Bulbs: H11 55 W low beam, H9 65 W high beam, PY24W front and PY21W rear turn signals.
  - Fuel: 17.8 US gal tank. 87 octane is fine; premium is recommended for best performance and 91+ for heat or towing; up to E10.
  - EPA: 25 city / 37 highway / 29 combined mpg (fueleconomy.gov, https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/noframes/36292.shtml).
  - Curb weight about 3,530-3,620 lb (sources differ); towing 3,300 lb braked, 1,650 lb unbraked; roof load 165 lb.
- t38/t47: Transmission is the Aisin TG-81SC 8-speed. Volvo bulletin codes for the car: engine code 40, vehicle type 155 (from Volvo bulletin TJ36858, https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2024/MC-11006558-0001.pdf).
- t42: The car's chassis number falls inside the range covered by Volvo's oil-consumption program P10186. Coverage ran 8 years from first delivery, so it has almost certainly expired; a Volvo dealer can confirm. Source: https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2023/MC-10242508-9999.pdf
- t42: Bulletin TJ34588 is for the five-cylinder engine and does not apply. The shift-quality bulletins are for the old 6-speed, not this 8-speed.
- Build month and year from the door-pillar label: still unknown at turn 99.

### 3. Findings and advice given

- t3: Found nothing worthwhile for the Volvo in public builds; suggested a maintenance log as a first build (no source given).
- t5 (first-pass intervals, later corrected at t34):
  - Oil 0W-20, Castrol Edge Professional V or VCC RBS0-2AE, about 5.6-5.9 L (Volvo: engine oil grade and volume, https://volvocars.com/uk/support/car/v60/15w17/article/3b599b62f78d1b3ac0a801e80197d148).
  - Oil service every 10,000 mi or 12 months (Firestone, https://vehicle.firestonecompleteautocare.com/volvo/v60/2016/maintenance/).
  - Brake fluid every 24 months (Haynes, https://uk.haynes.com/pages/maintenance-plans-car-volvo-s60-v60-2011-2018).
  - Air filter and spark plugs 37,000 mi, coolant 62,000 mi / 60 months, all marked "verify" (Haynes, https://uk.haynes.com/pages/maintenance-plans-car-volvo-s60-v60).
  - Transmission fluid: no fixed Volvo interval for normal driving (FCP Euro, https://www.fcpeuro.com/blog/how-to-service-volvo-p2-p3-spa-xc90-s60-v70-automatic-transmission; Volvo later-generation page, https://www.volvocars.com/au/support/car/v60/article/b51abbf67feb476ec0a8015139ecc710/).
- t5: 2015-2016 Drive-E engines have a documented oil-consumption problem. Volvo's extended warranty P10186 covered a piston and ring repair for 8 years or 100,000 miles, likely lapsed on a 2016 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2023/MC-10242508-9999.pdf). Related bulletin on the low oil level message: https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2016/SB-10075244-5448.pdf. Advice: keep an oil consumption log as a paper trail.
- t5: PCV clogging and thermostat failure are owner anecdotes, not failure rates (Edmunds, https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/v60/2015/consumer-reviews/; CarComplaints, https://www.carcomplaints.com/Volvo/S60/2015/engine/engine.shtml).
- t7: A web page or artifact cannot connect to the car directly; the route is CSV logs from a scanner app (no source given).
- t10: Running voltage near 12.6-13 V can be normal with smart charging, "likely including this one (verify)" (no source given). Long-term fuel trim lean points to P0171 causes and rich to P0172 causes (no source given).
- t15 (Unlocks research):
  - iPhones need a Bluetooth LE adapter. OBDLink CX $79.95 (https://www.obdlink.com/products/obdlink-cx/). Veepeak OBDCheck BLE+ $41.99 (https://veepeak.com/products/obdcheck-ble-plus). Vgate iCar Pro about $25-33. OBDLink MX+ $139.95, no BLE, cannot talk to a web page (https://scantool.net/obdlink-mxp/).
  - Car Scanner Pro is $7.99 (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/car-scanner-elm-obd2/id1259933623).
  - The OBDLink CX accepts new pairings only in the first 5 minutes after power-up (https://support.obdlink.com/support/solutions/articles/43000746707-obdlink-cx-adapter-notes).
- t15: Emissions:
  - Texas dropped safety inspections for personal cars on Jan 1, 2025; Travis County still requires an emissions test (https://www.dps.texas.gov/news/icymi-vehicle-safety-inspection-changes-take-effect-january-2025).
  - 2001-and-newer cars may have at most one readiness monitor not ready, and a check-engine light with a stored code fails (40 CFR 85.2222, https://www.customsmobile.com/regulations/title40_chapterI-i24_part85_subpartW_section85.2222).
  - Clearing codes resets the monitors. Only a generic drive cycle was found (AA1Car, https://www.aa1car.com/library/us50326.htm); no Volvo-specific cycle was confirmed.
- t15: Volvo VIDA diagnostics costs $48.15 for 3 days, plus a DiCE interface (about $500) and a Windows 11 Pro PC; the software tier is $73.14 for 3 days (https://www.volvotechinfo.com/vida). For a one-off non-engine fault, an independent specialist's scan is cheaper. At t31 the service-info tier was quoted at about $21 for 3 days (no source given in that turn).
- t15: Polestar Performance Optimization exists for this exact car (242 to 250 hp, 258 to 295 lb-ft, 0-60 mph 6.4 to 6.3 s, article 31459463). US price and 2026 availability are unconfirmed (https://engineered-api.polestar.com/optimisations/v60-t5-drive-e-fwd-automatic-2016/productSheet?market=us). No emissions-legal aftermarket tune was found; recalibration counts as tampering (EPA, https://www.epa.gov/node/226161; Tex. Transp. Code 547.605).
- t17: Timing belt: interference engine, so a snapped belt usually ruins the engine. Sources cite about 10 years and 150k, 144k or 90k miles, all from forums or a newer engine (Volvo forums, https://www.volvoforums.org.uk/forum/technical-topics/s60-v60-18-xc60-17-s90-v90-16-xc90-15-general/293287-timing-belt-change-v90?p=3741861; AutoPadre, https://www.autopadre.com/belt-or-chain/volvo-v60). The app showed 90k / 10 years until t34.
- t17: At ~95k with no records, plugs, coolant, brake fluid and air filter are past due if never done (later intervals corrected at t34).
- t17/t19: The OBDLink CX was recommended and "confirmed". It is the only adapter considered whose BLE data channel is published; the same CX also works with Car Scanner and OBDLink's app. It draws under 1 mA asleep, has a 180-day money-back guarantee and a 3-year warranty, and was out of stock at OBDLink when checked. Sources: OBDLink CX page; OBDAdvisor, https://obdadvisor.com/best-obdlink-scan-tool-review/; Scan Tool Compass, https://scantoolcompass.com/best-bluetooth-obd2-adapters/. Runner-up: vLinker MC+ about $60 (Fast Car, https://www.fastcar.co.uk/review/vlinker-mc-obd2-scanner-review/). Veepeak was dropped to fallback after ABRP flagged problems (https://abrp.featurebase.app/help/articles/7457755-choosing-an-obd-device).
- t19: Dealer inspection:
  - The FTC Used Car Rule requires the Buyers Guide (As Is or warranty) but no inspection (https://ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/dealers-guide-used-car-rule).
  - Dealers usually do a reconditioning check, and independent lots vary (no source given).
  - Certified by Volvo means 170+ points, a 12-month warranty and under 80,000 miles (https://volvocars.com/us/l/certified-by-volvo/).
  - Advice: ask the dealer for the reconditioning repair order and history report, and have a Volvo dealer pull service history by VIN.
- t21: As-is means no warranty. Advice: hunt for timing belt evidence (shop sticker, paperwork, Volvo dealer history), then book a baseline inspection at an independent Volvo specialist with a full-module scan (no source given for local prices).
- t25/t27: Tire light:
  - Steady with "Tire pressure low" means calibrate.
  - Flashing for about a minute then steady with "Tire press. syst Service required" means a system fault.
  - Calibration: set cold tires to the door-pillar pressure, then MY CAR > Settings > Car settings > Tire monitoring > Calibrate tire pressure, then drive at least 10 minutes above 20 mph.
  - Sources: Volvo US Tire Monitor, https://www.volvocars.com/us/support/car/v60/14w46/article/c43f9d2decd9952dc0a801513772c990/; calibrating, https://www.volvocars.com/us/support/car/v60/14w46/article/2f888f1af162f784c0a8015145e77ecc/; recalibration, https://www.volvocars.com/us/support/car/v60/14w46/article/5a300e78aa14d4f0c0a801e801efec26/.
  - Valve-stem tell (metal with a nut means sensors) (no source given).
- t25/t27: The CX plugs into the port and is powered by the car. It can read and clear stored, pending and permanent codes, show freeze frame, readiness, live data, CSV logs, Mode 06, and the VIN and ECU software ID. It cannot read airbag, ABS, TPMS, climate or body modules, or change software (OBDLink CX pages).
- t33: Recalls can be checked at nhtsa.gov/recalls or by calling Volvo; two of the four involve seat belts.
- t34: Corrections from Volvo's own documents (2016 owner's manual and maintenance schedule):
  - Oil: 5W-30 A5/B5 base spec, 0W-20 also approved (not 0W-20 only); 6.2 qt with filter.
  - Spark plugs: every 60k miles, not 37k.
  - Engine air filter: every 40k miles.
  - Brake fluid: every 3 years or 40k miles.
  - Cabin filter: every 20k miles or yearly.
  - Tires 38 psi; wheel bolts 103 lb-ft; 87 octane fine.
  - Timing belt hardware: 150k miles or 10 years; the car is at 10 years now, so it became the top Fix first item. Volvo's schedule lists the belt tensioner and idler at 150k/10 years; independent sources replace the belt with them as a kit.
- t34: Listed Volvo TSB TJ29818 (tire monitor false warnings), https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2016/MC-10120958-9999.pdf (also https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2019/MC-10165233-9999.pdf at t42).
- t34: 12-month budget with no service history: about $2,400-$3,600 at a shop, roughly $200-$300 a month (RepairPal timing belt, https://repairpal.com/estimator/volvo/v60/2016/timing-belt-replacement-cost; YourMechanic plugs, https://www.yourmechanic.com/estimates/volvo/v60/spark-plugs-replacement; FCP Euro kits, https://www.fcpeuro.com/Volvo-parts/V60/Timing-Belt-Kits/).
- t36: The 2016 system lacks CarPlay, so a retrofit was listed as an upgrade option (no source given).
- t42: Other bulletins and sources added to the app:
  - TJ31216: https://static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2019/MC-10169029-9999.pdf
  - Buchanan v. Volvo (oil consumption case): https://bergermontague.com/cases/buchanan-et-al-v-volvo-car-usa-llc-et-al
  - TG-81SC: https://www.transmissiondigest.com/?p=27645
  - NHTSA ruling on HID kits: https://www.nhtsa.gov/interpretations/shih3
  - Texas windshield mounting law: https://www.recordinglaw.com/us-laws/windshield-mounting-restrictions/texas-windshield-mounting-laws/
  - Volvo 2016 V60 What's New: https://mb.cision.com/Main/23622/4196507/3563273.pdf
  - Edmunds trims: https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/v60/2016/trims
  - Still unconfirmed: Polestar availability and price, 4G modem update, live tire prices, an LED-specific NHTSA ruling. 0-60 timing is accurate to about ±0.2 s.
- t47: Advice: build in Claude Code pointed at the repo, one feature per session, start with "Read CLAUDE.md and docs/ROADMAP.md", end with "Update the roadmap" (no source given).
- t57: Saving and offline use:
  - The Home Screen app stores data on the device and works offline after the first load. Bluefy keeps a separate copy, and the Claude version is a third copy in account cloud storage.
  - Apple's WebKit team said Home Screen web apps keep their own usage counter and their data is not expected to be deleted (https://webkit.org/blog/10218/full-third-party-cookie-blocking-and-more/). The 2023 policy says unused sites can be cleared and Home Screen apps are more likely to get persistent storage (https://webkit.org/?p=14403).
  - Real risks: deleting the app, clearing data, losing the phone.
  - A native app would need a Mac, Xcode and a paid Apple developer account (no source given).
- t59: A VM is not worth it. macOS on non-Apple hardware breaks Apple's license, and a free self-installed app expires after 7 days (no source given). The app cannot be installed remotely; Kyle adds it with Safari > Share > Add to Home Screen.
- t66: The GitHub iPhone app has no token settings, "as far as I know". Tokens are made on the website, are fine-grained, cover the one repo with Contents read/write, and are shown once (GitHub Docs, https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens).
- t70/t72: Bluefy is needed only for Bluetooth, but Bluefy-only use works. Apple's storage statement covers Home Screen apps, not Bluefy, and Bluefy's data retention could not be confirmed, so sync is the safety net.
- t78: Claude cannot see its usage limit, and a session stops without warning. Hence an always-ready handoff file on a branch.
- t80: Corrected Gemini: the handoff holds all source files (including the generated live.js) but not the build output, and none of Kyle's saved progress. It is roughly 250,000-300,000 tokens.
- t84: Gemini's scanner draft would not have worked as sent:
  - its link to the OCR library was broken
  - no upload in the app went through it
  - it missed multi-word phone numbers and addresses
  - it would have saved highlight boxes into the photo
  - there was no way to hide text it missed
- t98: Connection checklist:
  - Open the app in Bluefy.
  - Give Bluefy Bluetooth permission.
  - Close the OBDLink app and other OBD apps (the adapter talks to one app at a time).
  - Unplug and replug the CX with the ignition on, then connect within 5 minutes and accept pairing (PIN 123456 if asked).
  - Source: OBDLink CX adapter notes, https://support.obdlink.com/support/solutions/articles/43000746707-obdlink-cx-adapter-notes

  - B4204T11, 240 hp at 5,600 rpm, 258 lb-ft from 1,500 to 4,500 rpm, 82 × 93.2 mm, 10.8:1.
  - Oil 6.2 US qt with filter, no dipstick.
  - Coolant 8.7 US qt, 50/50, normally never changed.
  - AW1 transmission fluid about 7 US qt, no change in normal use.
  - DOT 4 brake fluid under the round cowl cover.
  - Washer 6.8 / 4.7 qt.
  - 800 CCA AGM battery under front and rear covers; the manual's fuse table lists an auxiliary battery.
  - Jump-start ground on the right engine mount's outer screw.
  - 17.8 gal tank; 87 octane is fine, premium recommended, 91+ for heat, towing or altitude; up to E10.
  - 215/50R17 at 38 psi; wheel bolts 103 lb-ft; tires replaced at 6 years; no required rotation, with the most tread on the rear.
  - Bulbs H11, H9, PY24W, PY21W.
  - Length 182.5 in, wheelbase 109.3 in.
  - Fuel door right rear; wading depth 10 in; cooling fan can run up to 6 minutes after shutdown.
  - Hood handle turned 20–25° clockwise, catch at the front right.
  - Sealing kit limits 50 mph / 120 miles; City Safety up to 30 mph; a loose fuel cap can light the check-engine light.
  - Door-label weights match the manual's four-cylinder FWD row.
  - Brake fluid boiling point above 536 °F; 0.63 US qt in the system.
- T169: Facts in the same manual that conflict or differ:
  - Roof load is 165 lb (75 kg) in the weights table and 220 lb (100 kg) on the loading pages.
  - A/C charge is 1.7 lb (770 g) in the manual and 800 g on the hood sticker.
  - Curb weight is 3,620–3,960 lb across engines, with the 2.0 FWD the lightest; 3,530 lb came from other sources.
  - Towing: 3,300 lb braked (2 in ball), 2,000 lb (1 7/8 in ball), 1,650 lb unbraked, 165 lb tongue.
  - Oil: 5W-30 A5/B5 for normal use; 0W-30 A5/B5, or 0W-20 (VCC RBS0-2AE, four-cylinders only), for extreme driving.
  - Oil level is valid after about 20 miles of driving or 5 minutes parked level with the engine off.
  - The four-cylinder engine bay drawing shows no power steering reservoir.
  - Not covered by the manual: service intervals, timing belt, Premier trim contents, EPA mpg, recalls and bulletins.
